conclusions:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ is integral (for example finite).
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_{small, *}$ transforms surjections into surjections (on sheaves
of sets and on abelian sheaves),
\item $f_{small}^{-1}f_{small, *}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$
is surjective for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_\etale$,
\item
$f_{small, *} :
\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)
\to
\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$
is faithful and reflects injections and surjections, and
\item
$f_{small, *} :
\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)
\to
\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}
Keep the distinction between *sheaves of sets* and *abelian sheaves*. Exactness is an **abelian-category** assertion, while direct image preservation of surjective maps also holds for set-valued sheaves.
hypotheses:

A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces a geometric morphism $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute et})$ with inverse-image functor $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to direct image $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$) and a ring map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^\sharp:f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$. A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

For any scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, define the following exact **three source properties** of its small étale-site pullback functor $V/Y\mapsto X\times_YV$: **(A)** for each étale $U\to X$ and $u\in U$, some étale $V\to Y$ admits a decomposition $X\times_YV=W\amalg W'$ and an $X$-morphism $W\to U$ whose image contains $u$; **(B)** for each étale $V\to Y$ and étale cover $\{U_i\to X\times_YV\}$, some étale cover $\{V_j\to V\}$ admits a decomposition $X\times_YV_j=\coprod_i W_{ij}$ for every $j$, with each $W_{ij}\to X\times_YV$ factoring through the relevant $U_i$; **(C)** for every étale $U\to X$, some étale $V\to Y$ admits a *surjective $X$-morphism* $X\times_YV\to U$. These are properties of the morphism, **not** generic properties of all scheme maps. In the topos notation $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\dashv f_{\mathrm{small},*}$, the map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}f_{\mathrm{small},*}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is the **counit**. A functor *reflects* monomorphisms/epimorphisms if whenever the image map is mono/epi, so was the original.

records.title: Lemma — Same image

conclusions: There is a factorization K→L̃→L of α with K→L̃ an admissible monomorphism, and a dg section s:L→L̃ of L̃→L such that its associated retraction is homotopic to id on L̃.
hypotheses: (A,d) is a dg algebra and α:K→L a morphism of dg A-modules.
records.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $\alpha : K \to L$ be a homomorphism of differential graded
$A$-modules. There exists a factorization
$$
\xymatrix{
K \ar[r]^{\tilde \alpha} \ar@/_1pc/[rr]_\alpha &
\tilde L \ar[r]^\pi & L
}
$$
in $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\tilde \alpha$ is an admissible monomorphism (i.e. split injective on the underlying graded $A$-modules),
\item there is a morphism $s : L \to \tilde L$
such that $\pi \circ s = \text{id}_L$ and such that
$s \circ \pi$ is homotopic to $\text{id}_{\tilde L}$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Extension

conclusions: Equivalence: every open cover of $X$ refines to a finite disjoint clopen partition of $X$ **if and only if** $X_0\to\pi_0(X)$ is bijective.
Under the additional sufficient condition both equivalent properties hold.
hypotheses: $X$ is a spectral topological space, $X_0$ its closed-point set, $\pi_0(X)$ its connected-component space.
For the *additional sufficient-condition* assertion only: $X_0$ is closed and every point of $X$ specializes to exactly one point of $X_0$.
records.statement:
Let $X$ be a spectral topological space; let $X_0\subseteq X$ be its closed points and let $\pi_0(X)$ denote the connected-component space. The following are equivalent:
(1) Every open cover of $X$ admits a refinement by a **finite partition** of $X$ into pairwise disjoint clopen subsets.
(2) The canonical map $X_0\to\pi_0(X)$ is bijective.
Furthermore, if $X_0$ is a closed subset of $X$ and every point of $X$ specializes to a unique point of $X_0$, then conditions (1) and (2) hold.

conclusions: Right adjoint of closed-immersion pushforward on O_Y is det normal shifted by -r.

Then the right-adjoint value on the structure sheaf admits an isomorphism
\[
\bigwedge^r_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal N[-r]\xrightarrow{\sim}a_i(\mathcal O_Y).
\]
If the rank varies between connected components the shift is understood componentwise.

records.title: Lemma — Colimit complexes

conclusions: $f^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_!$.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{D}$ be two sites.
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$ be a morphism of topoi.
Let $E \subset \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ be a subset such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $V \in E$ there exists a sheaf $\mathcal{G}$
on $\mathcal{C}$ such that $f^{-1}\mathcal{F}(V) = 
\Mor_{\Sh(\mathcal{C})}(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})$ functorially
for $\mathcal{F}$ in $\Sh(\mathcal{C})$,
\item every object of $\mathcal{D}$ has a covering by objects of $E$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_!$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. If the pro-objects $(K_n)$ and $(M_n)$ are each isomorphic in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X))$ to a Deligne system for $U\subseteq X$, then $(L_n)$ is also pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for this same open immersion.

For an étale map $U\to X$, its representable sheaf is $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$. In an abelian category a *weak Serre subcategory* is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions (without necessarily all subobjects).

**Statement (source hypotheses preserved):**
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a finite \'etale morphism of schemes.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a (finite) locally constant sheaf of sets,
(finite) locally constant sheaf of abelian groups, or
(finite type) locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules
on $X_\etale$, the same is true for $f_*\mathcal{F}$
on $Y_\etale$.

**Typed interpretation:** The claim is interpreted using the preceding explicit definitions; retain exactly the original assumptions and conclusion on the small étale site (distinguishing finite from finite-type local fibres).

records.title: Lemma — Determinant

conclusions: $X$ is Jacobson if and only if $|X|$ is Jacobson.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

records.title: Lemma — Proper finite fibre finite in neighbourhood

conclusions: Upper shriek preserves bounded-below coherent-derived complexes.
hypotheses: f separated finite-type S-morphism between FTS_S objects.
records.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, an object $D\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is a *dualizing complex* if on every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ it is the sheafification of a ring-theoretic dualizing complex: a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D_A,D_A)$. Write $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^\pm,D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b$ for derived complexes with coherent bounded-below, bounded-above and bounded cohomology respectively. If $f:X\to Y$ lies in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, then its upper-shriek functor maps bounded-below complexes with coherent cohomology to bounded-below complexes with coherent cohomology:
\[
f^!:D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_X).
\]
The assertion does not extend automatically to the unbounded-right-adjoint $a_f$ without a proper compactification.

records.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), a complex E^bullet is **perfect** when after a covering of every site object it has a quasi-isomorphism from a **strictly perfect** complex (bounded, termwise direct summand of finite free O-modules); a derived object is perfect if represented by such a complex (source Definition perfect at 12734–12746). Its relation to pseudo-coherence and local finite Tor dimension is an equivalence only where stated, not an inherited hypothesis. Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.

\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ and there exist a
covering $\{U_i \to X\}$, strictly perfect complexes $\mathcal{E}_i^\bullet$
of $\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-modules, and isomorphisms
 $\alpha_i : \mathcal{E}_i^\bullet \to E|_{U_i}$ in
$D(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})$, then $E$ is perfect.
\item If $E$ is perfect, then any complex representing $E$ is perfect.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.

records.title: Lemma — Adjoint ext

conclusions: Right adjoint to proper pushforward sends normalized D_Y to normalized D_X.
hypotheses: Proper f:X→Y of finite-type S-schemes, normalized D_X,D_Y.
records.statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a **proper** morphism between finite-type $S$-schemes, and let $D_X,D_Y$ be their dualizing complexes normalized relative to the same $D_S$. Let $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*$ (both schemes Noetherian and qcqs, but not necessarily separated over $S$). Then there is a canonical isomorphism $a_f(D_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_X$, compatible with the normalization on separated open pieces.

For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

If $X$ is Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional then $\omega_X^\bullet\simeq\omega_X[1]$, so Serre duality is $\operatorname{Ext}_X^{i+1}(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,\mathcal F),k)$. For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $1$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, its genus is $g(X)=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g(X)$. Such an $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay, and equidimensional of dimension $1$; its dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ and satisfies $H^1(X,\omega_X)\cong k$. Let $X$ be a smooth proper curve over a field $k$

conclusions: $\mathcal L$ has a regular meromorphic section.
hypotheses: X is a scheme and $\mathcal L$ invertible; at least one holds: X integral; X reduced with finitely many irreducible components on each qc open; X locally Noetherian with no embedded points.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
In each of the following cases $\mathcal{L}$ has a regular meromorphic
section:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is integral,
\item $X$ is reduced and any quasi-compact open has a finite
number of irreducible components,
\item $X$ is locally Noetherian and has no embedded points.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Stack in setoids descent

conclusions: Pullback of schemes with descent data along f is faithful.
hypotheses: f:X'→X over S is surjective and flat.
records.statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $f:X'\to X$ be a surjective flat morphism over $S$. Then the pullback functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ is faithful: two morphisms of descent data that become equal after pullback were already equal.

records.title: Lemma — Shriek composition

conclusions: Upper shriek takes dualizing complexes to dualizing complexes.
hypotheses: f in FTS_S and K a dualizing complex on Y.
records.statement: Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, an object $D\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is a *dualizing complex* if on every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ it is the sheafification of a ring-theoretic dualizing complex: a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D_A,D_A)$. Write $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^\pm,D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b$ for derived complexes with coherent bounded-below, bounded-above and bounded cohomology respectively. If $K$ is a dualizing complex on $Y$, then $f^!K$ is a dualizing complex on $X$. In particular, on every affine open of $X$ it corresponds to a ring-theoretic dualizing complex, and not merely to a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension without self-duality.

records.title: Lemma — Affine

conclusions: Composition of right adjoints equals right adjoint to composite restriction.
hypotheses: Commutative ring maps A→B→C; derived coinduction functors typed by rings.
records.statement:
For a homomorphism of commutative rings $\varphi:A\to B$, let $\varphi_*:D(B)\to D(A)$ be restriction of scalars. Its right adjoint $\mathcal C_\varphi(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,K)\in D(B)$ gives $B$ its action through precomposition on the $B$-argument. In general $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(L,\mathcal C_\varphi(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(\varphi_*L,K)$. For composable ring maps $A\to B\to C$, let $\mathcal C_{B/A}:D(A)\to D(B)$, $\mathcal C_{C/B}:D(B)\to D(C)$, and $\mathcal C_{C/A}:D(A)\to D(C)$ be their derived coinduction functors $R\operatorname{Hom}$. Then the canonical natural transformation
\[
\mathcal C_{C/B}\circ\mathcal C_{B/A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_{C/A}
\]
is an isomorphism; both sides are right adjoint to the same composite scalar restriction $D(C)\to D(A)$. This is an isomorphism of functors, not an untyped equality of two uses of $R\operatorname{Hom}$.

conclusions: $A \to B$ is ind-Zariski.
records.statement:
**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A **w-local** spectral space has closed set of closed points and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a w-local map between such spaces is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. A ring map $A\to B$ is a **local isomorphism** when near every prime of $B$ it induces an open immersion after inverting an element of $B$; it **identifies local rings** when $A_{q\cap A}\to B_q$ is an isomorphism for every prime $q$ of $B$. A ring map is **ind-Zariski** when its target is a filtered colimit of local-isomorphism algebras over the source.

Let $A \to B$ be ring map such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ identifies local rings,
\item the topological spaces $\Spec(B)$, $\Spec(A)$ are w-local, and
\item $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$ is w-local.
\end{enumerate}
Then $A \to B$ is ind-Zariski.

Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

A morphism of first-order thickenings $(f,f')$ is a commuting square of ringed spaces $(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{i}(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ over $(S,\mathcal O_S)\xrightarrow{t}(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$, with vertical morphisms $f:X\to S$ and $f':X'\to S'$. Put $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_{S'}\to\mathcal O_S)$. The induced homomorphism $(f')^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ equals $f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ for first-order thickenings. The morphism of thickenings is called strict if this map is surjective.

For a first-order thickening of ringed spaces with ideal $\mathcal I$, an extension of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal K$ on the thickened space means a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to0$ of $\mathcal O_{X'}$-modules, with $\mathcal I$ annihilating the two end terms. Isomorphisms of extensions fix their identified end terms.

records.title: Lemma — Inf ext rel

hypotheses:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian topological space.
Let $x \in X$.
Let $E \subset X$ be constructible in $X$.
records.statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian topological space.
Let $x \in X$.
Let $E \subset X$ be constructible in $X$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is a neighbourhood of $x$, and
\item for every irreducible closed subset $Y$ of $X$ which contains
$x$ the intersection $E \cap Y$ is dense in $Y$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Locally ringed morphism

conclusions: There is an induced map $N(\varphi):N(\mathcal L)\to N(\mathcal L^\prime)$ of invertible modules on Y.
For every $y\in Y$, $\varphi$ vanishes at some $x\in\pi^{-1}(y)$ iff $N(\varphi)$ vanishes at y.
hypotheses: $\pi:X\to Y$ is finite with a specified norm of degree $d\geq1$, and $\varphi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal L^\prime$ is a map of invertible modules on X.
records.statement:
For the norm N, $N(\mathcal L)$ is the line bundle obtained on opens V of Y where $\mathcal L|_{\pi^{-1}V}$ is trivial, by applying N to its transition functions; locally $N(\varphi)$ applies N to the scalar for $\varphi$. A norm of degree $d$ for a finite morphism $\pi:X\to Y$ means $d\geq1$ and a multiplicative sheaf map $N:\pi_*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ with $N(\pi^\sharp g)=g^d$, and such that for every open $V\subset Y$ and $a\in\Gamma(\pi^{-1}V,\mathcal O_X)$ vanishing at $x$, $N(a)$ vanishes at $\pi(x)$. Let $\pi : X \to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes. Assume there exists
a norm of degree $d$ for $\pi$. For any $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear map
$\varphi : \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{L}'$
of invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules there is an $\mathcal{O}_Y$-linear
map
$$
\text{Norm}_\pi(\varphi) :
\text{Norm}_\pi(\mathcal{L})
\longrightarrow
\text{Norm}_\pi(\mathcal{L}')
$$
with $\text{Norm}_\pi(\mathcal{L})$, $\text{Norm}_\pi(\mathcal{L}')$
as in Lemma \ref{lemma-norm-invertible}. Moreover, for
$y \in Y$ the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\varphi$ is zero at a point of $x \in X$ with $\pi(x) = y$, and
\item $\text{Norm}_\pi(\varphi)$ is zero at $y$.
\end{enumerate}

sections functor

is exact. In fact we have $\Gamma(S, \mathcal{F}) = \mathcal{F}_{\overline{s}}$

$$
\forall p\geq 1, \quad H_\etale^p(S, \mathcal{F})=0
$$
for all $\mathcal{F}\in \textit{Ab}(S_\etale)$.
The stalk is taken at the **closed geometric point** of the strict henselian local scheme; the sheaf sections and this stalk agree for set-valued sheaves.

records.title: Lemma — Affine base change

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $s \in S$.
Let $p : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y \to S$ and $X \to S$ proper,
\item $X$ is flat over $S$,
\item $X_s \to Y_s$ an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset S$ of $s$
such that the base change $X_U \to Y_U$ is an isomorphism.
Both morphisms X→S,Y→S are proper, but only X→S is required flat. If fibre X_s→Y_s is iso, then there exists some neighbourhood U of s over which X_U→Y_U is iso.
hypotheses:
For $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in a commutative ring $A$, the *Koszul complex* $K_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is the bounded exterior-algebra complex of $A^r$ whose differential contracts against the $f_i$. A *regular sequence* is successive nonzerodivisors with nonzero final quotient. A perfect object in $D(A)$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules.

For smooth proper morphisms $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$, a *relative equivalence kernel* is a perfect complex $K$ on $X\times_SY$ with a perfect inverse kernel $K'$ on **$Y\times_SX$** such that $K'\star K\simeq\Delta_{X/S,*}\mathcal O_X$ and $K\star K'\simeq\Delta_{Y/S,*}\mathcal O_Y$, where $\star$ denotes derived convolution along the intermediate factor, and $\Delta$ is the relative diagonal. The original source definition has a factor-order shorthand/typo in the written ambient space of $K'$; the two displayed convolution identities fix its correct typing. A *Fourier–Mukai equivalence* has kernel of this sort.

For smooth proper morphisms $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$, a *relative equivalence kernel* is a perfect complex $K$ on $X\times_SY$ with a perfect inverse kernel $K'$ on **$Y\times_SX$** such that $K'\star K\simeq\Delta_{X/S,*}\mathcal O_X$ and $K\star K'\simeq\Delta_{Y/S,*}\mathcal O_Y$, where $\star$ denotes derived convolution along the intermediate factor, and $\Delta$ is the relative diagonal. The original source definition has a factor-order shorthand/typo in the written ambient space of $K'$; the two displayed convolution identities fix its correct typing. A *Fourier–Mukai equivalence* has kernel of this sort.

Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $s \in S$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y \to S$ and $X \to S$ proper,
\item $X$ is flat over $S$,
\item $X_s \to Y_s$ an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset S$ of $s$
such that the base change $X_U \to Y_U$ is an isomorphism.

**Scope and interpretation:** Both morphisms X→S,Y→S are proper, but only X→S is required flat. If fibre X_s→Y_s is iso, then there exists some neighbourhood U of s over which X_U→Y_U is iso.

Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.

A one-dimensional reduced local ring has $\delta$-invariant $\operatorname{length}(\overline A/A)$, where $\overline A$ is its normalization, and its number of branches is the number of maximal ideals of the normalization of its completed local ring.

records.statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ and set $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=f^!\mathcal O_Y\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$. For any point $y\in Y$ with residue field $\kappa(y)$, set $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ and denote the projection by $h:X_y\to X$. Then $Lh^*(\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet})$ is a dualizing complex on the fibre $X_y$: its restriction to every affine open is the sheafification of a Noetherian ring-theoretic dualizing complex.

records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $f : X \to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes.
Let $\sigma : S \to X$ be a section of $f$.
Then $\sigma$ is a regular immersion.

A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.

\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

Let $S$ be a scheme.  Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski

is a special cocontinuous functor. Hence it induces an equivalence
of topoi from $\Sh(S_{affine, Zar})$ to $\Sh(S_{Zar})$.

records.title: Lemma — Noetherian topology

conclusions: Refinement pullback is fully faithful, and schemes over S embed fully faithfully into descent data on an fpqc cover.
hypotheses: Both covers fpqc and U refines V.
records.statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Let $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ both be fpqc coverings of $S$, and suppose $\mathcal U$ refines $\mathcal V$. Then the induced pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is fully faithful. Consequently, for any fpqc covering $\mathcal U$ of $S$, the category $\operatorname{Sch}/S$ embeds fully faithfully into $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ through canonical descent data. No assertion that this embedding is essentially surjective for all schemes is made.

hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be finite type over Noetherian rings. The *algebraic upper shriek* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ is defined by a chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$, with $A$-action by precomposition. For a surjection $\varphi$ this specializes to $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$. It is well-defined only *up to nonunique natural isomorphism*. records.statement:
Let $R\to A$ be finite type over Noetherian rings. The *algebraic upper shriek* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ is defined by a chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$, with $A$-action by precomposition. For a surjection $\varphi$ this specializes to $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$. It is well-defined only *up to nonunique natural isomorphism*. Its *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{A/R}^{\bullet}$ is $\varphi^!(R)$, again up to nonunique isomorphism. A *perfect map* is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension; finite-type flat maps are perfect.

Let $\varphi : R \to A$ be a finite type map of Noetherian rings.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\varphi$ is perfect, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ is in $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$,
\item $\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ has finite tor dimension over $R$, and
\item $A \to R\Hom_A(\omega_{A/R}^\bullet, \omega_{A/R}^\bullet)$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
\item If $\varphi$ is flat, then (1)(a), (1)(b), and (1)(c) hold and
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ is $R$-perfect
(More on Algebra,
Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-relatively-perfect}), and
\item for every map $R \to k$ to a field the base change
$\omega_{A/R}^\bullet \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} (A \otimes_R k)$
is a dualizing complex for $A \otimes_R k$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

**Scope and interpretation:** For perfect φ, the relative complex is bounded coherent, has finite relative Tor amplitude and the canonical homothety A→RHom_A(ω,ω) is an isomorphism. Flat φ also makes it R-perfect and its base change to every residue-field or field-valued R-point a dualizing complex on that fibre.

records.statement:
The kth Fitting ideal is locally generated by the $(m-k)$-minors of a relation matrix for a presentation with m module generators; the conventions give the unit ideal for nonpositive minor size. The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. A U-admissible blowup has some finitely presented closed center disjoint from U. Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finitely presented
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $U \subset X$ be a scheme theoretically
dense open such that $\mathcal{F}|_U$ is finite locally free of
constant rank $r$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the blowup $b : X' \to X$ of $X$ in the $r$th Fitting
ideal of $\mathcal{F}$ is $U$-admissible,
\item the strict transform $\mathcal{F}'$ of $\mathcal{F}$
with respect to $b$ is locally free of rank $r$,
\item the kernel $\mathcal{K}$ of the surjection
$b^*\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}'$ is
finitely presented and $\mathcal{K}|_U = 0$,
\item $b^*\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ are perfect
$\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules of tor dimension $\leq 1$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Syntomic locally finite presentation

conclusions:
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is Nagata.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is Nagata.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$
such that each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is Nagata.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is Nagata.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is Nagata then every open subscheme is Nagata.

conclusions:

There exist \'etale morphisms $U_i \to X$ and morphisms

is a Zariski covering of $V$.

A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

records.title: Lemma — Bounded triangulated subcategories

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\overline{s}$ be a geometric point of $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The stalk functor
$\textit{PAb}(S_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \textit{Ab}$,
$\mathcal{F}  \mapsto  \mathcal{F}_{\overline{s}}$
is exact.
\item We have $(\mathcal{F}^\#)_{\overline{s}} = \mathcal{F}_{\overline{s}}$
for any presheaf of sets $\mathcal{F}$ on $S_\mathrm{\acute etale}$.
\item The functor
$\textit{Ab}(S_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \textit{Ab}$,
$\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}_{\overline{s}}$ is exact.
\item Similarly the functors
$\textit{PSh}(S_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \textit{Sets}$ and
$\Sh(S_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \textit{Sets}$ given by the stalk functor
$\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}_{\overline{s}}$ are exact (see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-exact})
and commute with arbitrary colimits.
\end{enumerate}
Separate **four distinct claims**: stalk on abelian presheaves exact, sheafification unchanged at stalks for sets, stalk on abelian sheaves exact, and stalk on set-valued presheaves/sheaves preserves finite limits and all colimits. Do not conflate these with cohomology exactness.
hypotheses:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A **geometric point** $\bar s$ of a scheme $S$ is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. An **étale neighbourhood** of $\bar s$ is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ with $U\to S$ étale and a chosen $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $\bar s$; a morphism of such neighbourhoods is an $S$-morphism preserving the lifts. Their category is **cofiltered**, so a presheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** has stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar s}=\operatorname*{colim}_{(U,\bar u)}\mathcal F(U)$ over the opposite (filtered) category. Write $\mathcal F^\#$ for the associated sheaf. This is a *geometric* stalk, not merely a Zariski local-ring stalk.

records.title: Lemma — Stalk exact

conclusions:
$j \circ i$ is a regular immersion and
$(j \circ i)^! = i^! \circ j^!$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

Let $i : X \to Y$ and $j : Y \to Z$ be regular immersions
of schemes locally of finite type over $S$. Then
$j \circ i$ is a regular immersion and
$(j \circ i)^! = i^! \circ j^!$.

conclusions:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
$f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \textit{Ab}(X_\mathrm{\acute etale})$
is exact.
\item The functor
$f^{-1} : \Sh(Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \Sh(X_\mathrm{\acute etale})$

\item Let $\overline{x} \to X$ be a geometric point.

Then there is a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{G})_{\overline{x}} = \mathcal{G}_{\overline{y}}.
$$
where $\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$.
\item For any $V \to Y$ \'etale we have $f^{-1}h_V = h_{X \times_Y V}$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let ${\mathcal L}_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, r$ be invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules on $X$.
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of rank $r$ endowed with a filtration
$$
0 = \mathcal{E}_0 \subset \mathcal{E}_1 \subset \mathcal{E}_2
\subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{E}_r = \mathcal{E}
$$
such that $\mathcal{E}_i/\mathcal{E}_{i - 1} \cong \mathcal{L}_i$.
Set $c_1({\mathcal L}_i) = x_i$. Then
$$
c(\mathcal{E})
=
\prod\nolimits_{i = 1}^r (1 + x_i)
$$
in $A^*(X)$.

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. conclusions: The following are equivalent: every idempotent on an object of $\mathcal C$ has a kernel; every such idempotent has a cokernel; and each idempotent splits as a projection in a biproduct decomposition.
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive category.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a preadditive category. The following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{C}$ is Karoubian,
\item every idempotent endomorphism of an object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a
cokernel, and
\item given an idempotent endomorphism $p : z \to z$ of $\mathcal{C}$
there exists a direct sum decomposition $z = x \oplus y$ such
that $p$ corresponds to the projection onto $y$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

For $x\in|X|$ and an étale morphism $U\to X$, write $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ for a pointed étale neighborhood. It is *elementary* when $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is a monomorphism representing $x$. When $X$ is decent, such neighborhoods are cofiltered: they exist, any two have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized after refinement. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is the field of the unique representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, and the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}$ is the filtered colimit of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over elementary étale neighborhoods; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}^{h}$ for any elementary étale neighborhood.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

records.title: Lemma — Power equal

conclusions:
$i$ is regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.
hypotheses:
Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian. Then
$i$ is regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.

records.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n$ be elements of $R$
generating the unit ideal. Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
The sequence
$$
0 \to
M \xrightarrow{\alpha}
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1}^n M_{f_i} \xrightarrow{\beta}
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i, j = 1}^n M_{f_i f_j}
$$
is exact, where $\alpha(m) = (m/1, \ldots, m/1)$

conclusions:
a slight generalization of the above constructions

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Let $f, g \in R(X)^*$. Then
$$
\text{div}_X(fg) = \text{div}_X(f) + \text{div}_X(g)
$$
as Weil divisors on $X$.

records.title: Lemma — Criterion smoothing

conclusions:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a presheaf on $\Sch/S$. Then
$\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology
if and only if
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the sheaf property with respect to the
Zariski topology, and
\item for every faithfully flat morphism $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$
of affine schemes over $S$, the sheaf axiom holds for the covering
$\{\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)\}$. Namely, this means that
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(A)) \ar[r] &
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(B)) \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] &
\mathcal{F}(\Spec(B \otimes_A B))
}
$$
is an equalizer diagram.
\end{enumerate}
The affine test uses B⊗_A B and the two restriction maps. The Zariski sheaf axiom must be checked on all S-schemes; the affine faithfully flat test is sufficient *together* with it.

For a covering, a *matching family* consists of sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ whose restrictions to every fibre product $U_i\times_UU_j$ coincide (including $i=j$). A presheaf is *separated* if sections are uniquely determined by restrictions to each covering, and a *sheaf* if every matching family glues uniquely.

For a base scheme $S$, let $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ denote **all schemes over $S$** (using the source's size conventions). An *fpqc covering* $\{T_i\to T\}$ consists of flat maps whose images cover $T$ and such that for each affine open $U\subseteq T$ there are finitely many affine opens in some $T_i$ whose images cover $U$. A singleton $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is fpqc exactly when $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. An *fpqc sheaf property* for a presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ means the usual equalizer condition for **all** fpqc coverings; because of size issues this does not presume a single small fpqc site of all schemes exists.

Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. $\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion. If $Z$ and $X$ are
regular schemes, then $i$ is a regular immersion.

conclusions: $i$ is a regular immersion.
hypotheses:
Let

records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd] \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume that $Y \to S$ is smooth, $X \to S$ smooth, and
$i$ an immersion. Then $i$ is a regular immersion.

conclusions: The Gysin morphisms form a chain map with respect to the de Rham differential.
hypotheses: $Z$ is cut out by the given functions on $X/S$, and $\gamma^p$ is the indicated local-cohomology Gysin map.
records.statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, let $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ be global functions on $X$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be their common vanishing subscheme. For each $p\geq0$, define the local Gysin morphism
$$\gamma^p_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\longrightarrow\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$$
by the local cohomology/Čech class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$, for a lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$. Then the Gysin maps commute with the de Rham differentials:
$$d\circ\gamma^p_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}=\gamma^{p+1}_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}\circ d.$$

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

records.statement:
For a unital map of commutative rings $u:R\to S$, going down means: for every chain $\mathfrak p\subset\mathfrak p^\prime$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p^\prime$, there exists $\mathfrak q\subset\mathfrak q^\prime$ over $\mathfrak p$. Going up means: for every such chain and $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, there exists $\mathfrak q^\prime\supset\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p^\prime$. Let $R \to S$ be a ring map. If the induced map
$\varphi : \Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$ is open, then
$R \to S$ satisfies going down.

records.title: Lemma — Lim finite projective gives finite projective

conclusions: Dimension function for quotient dualizing equals restriction of δ for A.
hypotheses: Noetherian A with dualizing ω_A; surjective A→B; induced ω_B.
records.statement:
Let $A$ be Noetherian with a dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$. At each $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ let $\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)$ be the unique integer such that the stalk-localization $\omega_{A,\mathfrak p}^\bullet[-\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)]$ is normalized over $A_{\mathfrak p}$, meaning its derived Hom from $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[0]$. This is a *dimension function*: across an immediate specialization $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ of height-one difference, $\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)=\delta_\omega(\mathfrak q)+1$. Suppose $\varphi:A\twoheadrightarrow B=A/I$ is a surjective homomorphism of Noetherian rings, and choose $\omega_B^\bullet=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,\omega_A^\bullet)$ as the induced dualizing complex over $B$. Then the induced dimension functions satisfy
\[
\delta_{\omega_B^\bullet}(\mathfrak q)=\delta_{\omega_A^\bullet}(\varphi^{-1}\mathfrak q)
\qquad(\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B).
\]
The isomorphism is the restriction of the numerical function under the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$.

conclusions: There is a commutative comparison diagram from a sequence y₁→⋯→yₙ of admissible monomorphisms to the x-sequence, each vertical map yᵢ→xᵢ being a homotopy equivalence.

records.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$ and let $\mathcal A$ be a differential graded category over $R$ satisfying the following axioms. Axiom (A) requires a zero object and binary differential graded direct sums. Axiom (B) requires dg shift functors $[n]$, with $[0]=\mathrm{id}$ and $[n+m]=[n]\circ[m]$, and composition-compatible identifications $\operatorname{Hom}(x,y[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(x,y)[n]$ of dg modules. Axiom (C) requires, for every closed degree-zero $f:x\to y$, an admissible short exact sequence $y\to c(f)\to x[1]$ in $\operatorname{Comp}(\mathcal A)$ whose connecting morphism $x[1]\to y[1]$ agrees with $f[1]$.
let $x_1 \to x_2 \to \ldots \to x_n$
be a sequence of composable morphisms in $\text{Comp}(\mathcal{A})$.
Then there exists a commutative diagram in $\text{Comp}(\mathcal{A})$:
$$
\xymatrix{x_1\ar[r] & x_2\ar[r] & \ldots\ar[r] & x_n\\
y_1\ar[r]\ar[u] & y_2\ar[r]\ar[u] & \ldots\ar[r] & y_n\ar[u]}
$$
such that each $y_i\to y_{i+1}$ is an admissible monomorphism
and each $y_i\to x_i$ is a homotopy equivalence.

$$

\bigoplus\nolimits_{j = 1, \ldots, m}
j_{V_j!}\underline{\mathbf{Z}/m_j\mathbf{Z}}_{V_j}
\longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n}
j_{U_i!}\underline{\mathbf{Z}/n_i\mathbf{Z}}_{U_i}
\right)
$$
with $V_j$ and $U_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects of
$X_\etale$ and $m_j$, $n_i$ positive integers.
In fact, we can even assume $U_i$ and $V_j$ affine.
The finite presentation is a **cokernel of a map between finite direct sums of $j_!$ of constant finite abelian sheaves**; it is not a presentation by arbitrary sheaf coproducts.
