records.statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The site hypotheses are exactly (i) quasi-compact **final object X**, (ii) finite cofinal coverings of every quasi-compact object by quasi-compact objects, (iii) quasi-compact pairwise fibre products inside such finite covers. These imply **bounded-below** compactness for perfect K; an **additional** finite cohomological dimension of the final object X is required for compactness in the full unbounded category.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Assume
$\mathcal{C}$ has the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{C}$ has a quasi-compact final object $X$,
\item every quasi-compact object of $\mathcal{C}$
has a cofinal system of coverings which are finite
and consist of quasi-compact objects,
\item for a finite covering $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
with $U$, $U_i$ quasi-compact the fibre products $U_i \times_U U_j$ are
quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O})$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $K$ is a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$
in the following sense: if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(K, M) = \bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(K, M_i)$.
\item[(b)] If $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$
has finite cohomological dimension, i.e., if there exists
a $d$ such that $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $i > d$ for
any $\mathcal{O}$-module $\mathcal{F}$, then
$K$ is a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions:

hypotheses: A first-order thickening $i:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ of ringed spaces is a morphism inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces, a surjection $\mathcal O_{X'}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_X$, and a square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

A morphism of first-order thickenings $(f,f')$ is a commuting square of ringed spaces $(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{i}(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ over $(S,\mathcal O_S)\xrightarrow{t}(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$, with vertical morphisms $f:X\to S$ and $f':X'\to S'$. Put $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_{S'}\to\mathcal O_S)$. The induced homomorphism $(f')^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ equals $f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ for first-order thickenings. The morphism of thickenings is called strict if this map is surjective.

The induced homomorphism $(f')^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ equals $f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ for first-order thickenings. The morphism of thickenings is called strict if this map is surjective.

Let $(f, f')$ be a morphism of first order thickenings in the commutative square of first-order ringed-space thickenings defined above.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules and set
$\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$ and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{G}'$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear map.
Assume that $\mathcal{G}'$ is flat over $S'$ and that
$(f, f')$ is a strict morphism of thickenings.
The set of lifts of $\varphi$ to an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-linear map
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$ is, if nonempty, a principal
homogeneous space under
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F},
\mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} f^*\mathcal{J})

records.title: Lemma — Basis hypercovering

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat and quasi-compact, and
\item the geometric fibres of $f$ are connected.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $S_\mathrm{\acute etale}$.
Then $\Gamma(S, \mathcal{F}) = \Gamma(T, f^{-1}_{small}\mathcal{F})$.
The canonical pullback map on global sections is an isomorphism when f is **flat quasi-compact** with *geometrically connected fibres*. The target sheaf is the small étale inverse image on T; connectedness is of every geometric fibre, not merely the ordinary fibres.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the induced **morphism of small étale topoi** $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute etale})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute etale})$ has inverse image $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$); it sends **sheaves of sets** on $Y_{\acute etale}$ to sheaves on $X_{\acute etale}$, and also induces inverse image of abelian sheaves. For a morphism $g:T\to S$ denote the restriction of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ under $g$ by $g_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$.

For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale\}$ let $\pi_S:(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau\to S_\tau$ be the canonical morphism of the **big** to the **small** site; its inverse image $\pi_S^{-1}$ takes small-site sheaves to big-site sheaves. For $f:T\to S$, $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on the *small* $\tau$-site $T_\tau$, and $\Gamma(T_\tau,-)$ denotes global sections over its final object $T$. An **fpqc cover** means a flat jointly surjective family with the finite affine-source cover condition over each affine open.

Assume $X \to S$ smooth, and $i$, $j$ immersions.
If $j$ is a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular)

records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd]_j \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume $X \to S$ smooth, and $i$, $j$ immersions.
If $j$ is a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular)
immersion, then so is $i$.

records.title: Lemma — Pushout filtered

conclusions: The contravariant character-dual functor is exact and detects injections/surjections by reversing them.
hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring and $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$.
records.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$, define the contravariant $R$-module functor $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $R$-action $(r\cdot\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$. Then $C$ is an exact contravariant functor: for each short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ the sequence
$$0\to C(M'')\to C(M)\to C(M')\to0$$
is exact. Furthermore, it reflects monomorphisms and epimorphisms: an $R$-linear map $u:M\to N$ is injective if and only if $C(u):C(N)\to C(M)$ is surjective, and $u$ is surjective if and only if $C(u)$ is injective.

records.title: Lemma — ML local

conclusions: The proper relative dualizing complex with pre-rigidity is a relative dualizing pair.
hypotheses: S qcqs and f proper flat fp; omega=a_f(O_S); diagonal pre-rigidity morphism given.
records.statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes (no quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or Noetherian assumption). Choose an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X\times_SX$ of the diagonal for which $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$ is a closed immersion, and let $p_1:W\to X$ be the first projection. A *relative dualizing complex* is a **pair** $(K,\xi)$ consisting of an $S$-perfect complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ (pseudo-coherent with locally finite relative Tor amplitude) and a *rigidifying map* $\xi:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to Lp_1^*K$ in $D(\mathcal O_W)$ which induces an isomorphism $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_W}(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X,Lp_1^*K)$. The condition is independent of the choice of $W$ and uses the diagonal and derived internal Hom, not only self-duality of $K$. Now assume additionally $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to S$ *proper, flat and finitely presented*. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories and put $\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_S)$. Let $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow X\times_SX$ be the (closed) diagonal, $p_1$ the first projection, and $c_\Delta$ the right adjoint of $R\Delta_*$. The *pre-rigidity* isomorphism $\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c_\Delta(Lp_1^*\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet})$ from relative duality determines, by diagonal adjunction, a rigidifying map $\xi:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to Lp_1^*\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet}$. Then $(\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet},\xi)$ is a relative dualizing pair as above.

hypotheses: For a **connected** scheme $X$ with geometric basepoint $\bar x$, its étale fundamental group $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ is the profinite automorphism group of the fibre functor of finite étale covers of $X$. A *finite continuous $\pi_1$-set* is a finite set with continuous action; a *finite continuous $\pi_1$-module* is a finite abelian group with compatible continuous action. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_T W]_{q+r}$ with scheme-theoretic multiplicities. It also induces a map on Chow groups.

hypotheses: A *constructible locally closed subscheme* $T\subset X$ is a locally closed subscheme whose underlying subset is **constructible** (a finite Boolean combination of quasi-compact opens). On the **small étale site** $X_{\acute et}$, a sheaf of sets or abelian groups is *constructible* if on **every affine open** it admits a finite partition into constructible locally closed strata $T_i$ on which the sheaf is **finite locally constant**. If $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules is *constructible* if the restrictions on those strata are **finite type locally constant** (finitely generated $\Lambda$-fibres), possibly of infinite cardinality. On a qcqs base, these conditions are equivalent to existence of a global finite constructible stratification. A *weak Serre* subcategory is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions, whereas the stronger Serre condition also includes **arbitrary subobjects and quotients** of its objects.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. If $\mathcal{F}$ is a

records.statement:
A *constructible locally closed subscheme* $T\subset X$ is a locally closed subscheme whose underlying subset is **constructible** (a finite Boolean combination of quasi-compact opens). On the **small étale site** $X_{\acute et}$, a sheaf of sets or abelian groups is *constructible* if on **every affine open** it admits a finite partition into constructible locally closed strata $T_i$ on which the sheaf is **finite locally constant**. If $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules is *constructible* if the restrictions on those strata are **finite type locally constant** (finitely generated $\Lambda$-fibres), possibly of infinite cardinality. On a qcqs base, these conditions are equivalent to existence of a global finite constructible stratification. A *weak Serre* subcategory is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions, whereas the stronger Serre condition also includes **arbitrary subobjects and quotients** of its objects.

constructible sheaf of sets, abelian groups, or $\Lambda$-modules

conclusions:
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S$ is universally catenary,
\item there exists an open covering of $S$ all of whose members are
universally catenary schemes,
\item for every affine open $\Spec(R) = U \subset S$ the ring
$R$ is universally catenary, and
\item there exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup U_i$ such
that each $U_i$ is the spectrum of a universally catenary ring.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, in this case any scheme locally of finite type over $S$
is universally catenary as well.

records.title: Lemma — Strict monomorphism into filtered injective

conclusions: Restricting before or after upper shriek gives naturally isomorphic functors.
hypotheses: Noetherian S, commutative square in FTS_S, horizontal maps open immersions.
records.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For any commutative square $U\xrightarrow jX$, $V\xrightarrow{j'}Y$ with vertical arrows $g:U\to V$ and $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, where $j$ and $j'$ are open immersions and $f\circ j=j'\circ g$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism of functors
\[
j^*\circ f^!\xrightarrow{\sim}g^!\circ(j')^*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_U).
\]
The square is not required to be cartesian: the result follows from composition coherence and $j^!\cong j^*$ for open immersions.

A morphism of algebraic spaces $Y\to X$ is *integral* if it is affine and integral after base change to every scheme over $X$. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space, an integral cover by a scheme is a surjective integral morphism $Y\to X$ with $Y$ a scheme. The *schematic locus* of an algebraic space is its largest open subspace representable by a scheme, when such a locus exists; a dense open scheme in $X$ means an open subscheme with dense image in $|X|$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A quasi-compact open immersion is an open embedding whose source is quasi-compact. A reduced closed subspace of an algebraic space is its uniquely determined reduced induced closed subspace. An étale stratification of $X$ by schemes is a finite chain of closed subspaces $\varnothing=Z_{-1}\subset Z_0\subset\cdots\subset Z_n=X$, whose locally closed differences $Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ are schemes. An algebraic space is quasi-compact if it admits a finite affine étale cover, and quasi-separated when its diagonal is quasi-compact.

records.title: Lemma — Constructions invertible

conclusions: The sheafy trace map is an isomorphism only after applying DQ_Y in general.
hypotheses: f qcqs, E and K quasi-coherent-derived, a_f and quasi-coherator defined.
records.statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. Write $DQ_Y:D(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ for the *quasi-coherator*, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\hookrightarrow D(\mathcal O_Y)$. The canonical morphism
\[
Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(E,a_f(K))\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(Rf_*E,K),
\]
obtained from the derived internal-Hom pushforward map followed by the adjunction counit $Rf_*a_f(K)\to K$, becomes an isomorphism *after applying $DQ_Y$ to both sides*. Without the quasi-coherator the internal-Hom map need not be an isomorphism.

records.statement:
Let $R$ be a domain with fraction field $K$.
If $u, v \in K$ are almost integral over $R$, then so are
$u + v$ and $uv$. Any element $g \in K$ which is integral over $R$
is almost integral over $R$. If $R$ is Noetherian
then the converse holds as well.
A normal domain means a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. A normal ring means a ring whose localization at every prime ideal is a normal domain.
For a domain $A$ and $z\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, almost integral over $A$ means that some $0\ne a\in A$ satisfies $az^n\in A$ for every integer $n\geq0$.

}

such that $\pi s=1_y$ and $s\pi$ is homotopic to $1_{\tilde{y}}$.

records.title: Lemma — Contract basic

conclusions: $\deg(\omega_X|_C) = 0$.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

records.title: Lemma — Support closed

conclusions: Coinduction along Cartier quotient is derived tensor with conormal inverse shifted [-1].
hypotheses: Surjective R→A=R/I with invertible ideal I; N dual of I⊗_R A.
records.statement:
For a homomorphism of commutative rings $\varphi:A\to B$, let $\varphi_*:D(B)\to D(A)$ be restriction of scalars. Its right adjoint $\mathcal C_\varphi(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,K)\in D(B)$ gives $B$ its action through precomposition on the $B$-argument. In general $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(L,\mathcal C_\varphi(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(\varphi_*L,K)$. Suppose $R\twoheadrightarrow A=R/I$ is a surjective ring map and the ideal $I\subseteq R$ is an invertible $R$-module (equivalently, locally generated by a single nonzerodivisor). Let $L=I\otimes_RA$ be an invertible $A$-module and $N=L^{-1}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(L,A)$. Then for every $K\in D(R)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)\simeq K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[-1].
\]
The shift $[-1]$ places the unique nonzero Ext sheaf of $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,R)$ in cohomological degree $1$.

records.title: Lemma — Higher derived functors

conclusions: There is a canonical morphism $g^* Rf_*\mathcal F^\bullet\longrightarrow R(f')_*(g')^*\mathcal F^\bullet$ in $D^+(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D'})$.
hypotheses: The displayed square of ringed topoi is commutative, with morphisms $f,f',g,g'$ in the indicated directions.
$g$ and $g'$ are **flat** morphisms of ringed topoi.

records.statement:
Consider a **commutative** square of ringed topoi $\mathcal C'\xrightarrow{g'}\mathcal C$ over $\mathcal D'\xrightarrow{g}\mathcal D$, with vertical arrows $f':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D'$ and $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. Both horizontal maps $g,g'$ are assumed flat, so their pullback functors $g^*,(g')^*$ are exact and act on derived categories without additional derived-pullback notation. The assertion is **existence** of a canonical base-change morphism; it does **not** assert an isomorphism.

Let
$$
\xymatrix{
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'})
\ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} &
(\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \ar[d]^f \\
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})
\ar[r]^g &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules.
Assume both $g$ and $g'$ are flat.
Then there exists a canonical base change map
$$
g^*Rf_*\mathcal{F}^\bullet
\longrightarrow
R(f')_*(g')^*\mathcal{F}^\bullet
$$
in $D^{+}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. conclusions: The Čech tensor formula gives local cohomology and right adjunction.
hypotheses: I finitely generated with f_i generators, full subcategory of complexes with power-torsion cohomology.
records.statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ finitely generated, and $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion. Let $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the *augmented alternating Čech complex* $[A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i<j}A_{f_if_j}\to\cdots\to A_{f_1\cdots f_r}]$, with $A$ in degree $0$, the standard alternating restriction differentials, and all terms flat. Define $R\Gamma_Z(K)=C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$. This is local cohomology, unlike $R\Gamma_I$ above for general non-Noetherian $A$. Then the functor $R\Gamma_Z:D(A)\to D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$ is **right adjoint** to the full inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$, and the displayed augmented Čech formula is a natural isomorphism for *every* $K\in D(A)$. The Čech construction and its augmentation $R\Gamma_Z(K)\to K$ are independent of the generating set in the derived category.

conclusions: If C has a final object X and there is a covering {U_i→X} with strictly perfect E_i^bullet and derived maps E_i^bullet→E|_{U_i} inducing cohomology isomorphisms above m and a surjection in m, then E is m-pseudo-coherent.

hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, E∈D(O), and m∈Z.
records.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O) and integer m, a complex E^bullet is **m-pseudo-coherent** if locally on every site object it admits a map from a strictly perfect complex inducing isomorphisms in H^j for j>m and a **surjection** in H^m. An object E∈D(O) is m-pseudo-coherent if any representing complex has this property (equivalently some representative; see source lines 12038–12057). Pseudo-coherent means m-pseudo-coherent for every integer m, and it does **not** imply global bounded-above without extra quasi-compactness. The three assertions must be read separately; the first additionally assumes a **final object** X in C, and the other two do not.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ and if there exist a covering
$\{U_i \to X\}$, strictly perfect complexes $\mathcal{E}_i^\bullet$ of
$\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-modules, and
maps $\alpha_i : \mathcal{E}_i^\bullet \to E|_{U_i}$ in
$D(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})$ with $H^j(\alpha_i)$ an isomorphism for $j > m$
and $H^m(\alpha_i)$ surjective, then $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent.
\item If $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then any complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
representing $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent.
\item If for every object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ there exists a covering
$\{U_i \to U\}$ such that $E|_{U_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then
$E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Adjoint functorial injectives

conclusions:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an
algebraically closed field $k$ and let $n \geq 1$ be invertible in $k$.
Then there are canonical identifications
$$
H_\etale^q(X, \mu_n) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mu_n(k) & \text{ if }q = 0, \\
\Pic^0(X)[n] & \text{ if }q = 1, \\
\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z} & \text{ if }q = 2, \\
0 & \text{ if }q \geq 3.
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
Since $\mu_n \cong \underline{\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z}}$, this gives
(noncanonical) identifications
$$
H_\etale^q(X, \underline{\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z}}) \cong
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z} & \text{ if }q = 0, \\
(\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z})^{2g} & \text{ if }q = 1, \\
\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z} & \text{ if }q = 2, \\
0 & \text{ if }q \geq 3.
\end{matrix}
\right.

The identification of $H^1(X,\mu_n)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)[n]$ is **canonical**, whereas the identifications with $(\mathbf Z/n)^{2g}$ depend on choosing generators/bases.

hypotheses:

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$ .
records.statement:
Let $p > 0$ be a prime number. Let $S$ be a scheme in characteristic $p$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$ .
Then the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[d]_f \ar[r]_{F_{X/S}} & X^{(p)} \ar[d]^{f^{(p)}} \\
Y \ar[r]^{F_{Y/S}} & Y^{(p)}
}
$$
commutes.
Absolute Frobenius acts identically on points and by $a\mapsto a^p$ on functions. For $X/S$, $X^{(p)}=X\times_{S,F_S}S$, and $F_{X/S}$ is the canonical map induced by absolute Frobenius.

conclusions: There exist a K-flat complex $\mathcal N^\bullet$ and chain maps $b:\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal N^\bullet$, $c:\mathcal N^\bullet\to\mathcal L^\bullet$ such that $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $a$ is chain-homotopic to $c\circ b$.

hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.

records.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). A homotopy of chain maps is a degree-minus-one map witnessing equality up to boundary; the source requires a **single factorization up to homotopy** with $c$ a quasi-isomorphism. The additional termwise-flat conclusion is conditional on the source $\mathcal K^\bullet$ having flat terms.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $a : \mathcal{K}^\bullet \to \mathcal{L}^\bullet$ be a map of complexes
of $\mathcal{O}$-modules. If $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ is K-flat, then
there exist a complex $\mathcal{N}^\bullet$ and maps of complexes
$b : \mathcal{K}^\bullet \to \mathcal{N}^\bullet$
and $c : \mathcal{N}^\bullet \to \mathcal{L}^\bullet$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{N}^\bullet$ is K-flat,
\item $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism,
\item $a$ is homotopic to $c \circ b$.
\end{enumerate}
If the terms of $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ are flat, then we may choose
$\mathcal{N}^\bullet$, $b$, and $c$
such that the same is true for $\mathcal{N}^\bullet$.

records.title: Proposition — Leray

conclusions: $\omega_X^{\otimes 3}$ is very ample and $H^1(X, \omega_X^{\otimes 3}) = 0$.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *stable curve* (in the situation $g\ge2$) has no rational tails or rational bridges, equivalently each genus-zero irreducible component meets the remainder of $X$ in at least three geometric points. Its dualizing sheaf $\omega_X$ is invertible. A contraction to a stable curve means a proper morphism $c:X\to X_{\mathrm{st}}$ obtained by successively contracting rational tails and bridges and whose target has no such components.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

perfect complex of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-modules, then
$f^*\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ is a strictly perfect complex of

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

For closed immersions $i_j:X_j\hookrightarrow X$ with $X=X_1\cup X_2$ set-theoretically and a perfect $E_2$ on $X_2$ whose Chern classes are defined, assume its restriction to $X_1\cap X_2$ is zero (for the power-sum class $P'_p(E_2)$), or a finite locally free sheaf of rank less than $p$ in degree zero (for the Chern class $c'_p(E_2)$). The canonical localized classes $P'_p(E_2),c'_p(E_2)\in A^p(X_2\to X)$ agree with $P_p(E_2),c_p(E_2)$ on cycles pushed from $X_2$ and vanish on cycles pushed from $X_1$, respectively, compatibly with locally finite type base changes.

records.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, say *at worst nodal of relative dimension one* if $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and each nonempty geometric fibre is an equidimensional one-dimensional scheme with at-worst-nodal singularities. Equivalently $f$ is syntomic of relative dimension one and $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$, defined by the first Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/S}$, is unramified over $S$. Here syntomic means flat, locally of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres. This property is stable under base change and local for the étale topology on the source and fpqc topology on the target.

Let $f : X \to S$ be at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$.
If $Y \to X$ is an \'etale morphism, then the composition $g : Y \to S$
is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$.

Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

The *representable presheaf* $h_X:\mathcal C^{op}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ is $h_X(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(U,X)$; for $v:V\to U$ it sends $f:U\to X$ to $f\circ v:V\to X$. records.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a **small** category and $X,Y$ objects. The *representable presheaf* $h_X:\mathcal C^{op}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ is $h_X(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(U,X)$; for $v:V\to U$ it sends $f:U\to X$ to $f\circ v:V\to X$. The category $\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C)$ has these contravariant set-valued functors as objects and natural transformations as morphisms. Then the assignment $f:X\to Y\mapsto h_f:h_X\to h_Y$, with $h_f(U)(g)=f\circ g$, is a **natural bijection**
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Nat}(h_X,h_Y).
\]
Its inverse sends a natural transformation $\eta$ to $\eta_X(\operatorname{id}_X)\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,Y)$. No sheaf condition or topology on $\mathcal C$ is needed.

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\overline{s}$ be a geometric point of $S$.
Let $(U, \overline{u})$ be an \'etale neighborhood of $\overline{s}$.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{\varphi_i : U_i \to U \}_{i\in I}$ be an \'etale covering.
Then there exist $i \in I$ and $\overline{u}_i : \overline{s} \to U_i$
such that $\varphi_i : (U_i, \overline{u}_i) \to (U, \overline{u})$
is a morphism of \'etale neighborhoods.
The lifted morphism must preserve the **specific geometric point** ̅u of U; existence follows because the nonempty étale geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field has a point.
hypotheses:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A **geometric point** $\bar s$ of a scheme $S$ is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. An **étale neighbourhood** of $\bar s$ is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ with $U\to S$ étale and a chosen $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $\bar s$; a morphism of such neighbourhoods is an $S$-morphism preserving the lifts. Their category is **cofiltered**, so a presheaf $\mathcal F$ on the **small étale site** has stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar s}=\operatorname*{colim}_{(U,\bar u)}\mathcal F(U)$ over the opposite (filtered) category. Write $\mathcal F^\#$ for the associated sheaf. This is a *geometric* stalk, not merely a Zariski local-ring stalk.

Tor-independence of $X$ and $Z$ over $S$ means the higher relative Tor sheaves of their structure sheaves vanish.

hypotheses: Let (R,m) be local, R → S finitely presented and flat with geometrically integral fibres, p=mS, q a prime over m, and N a finite S-module.
records.statement:
Let $(R, \mathfrak m)$ be a local ring. Let $R \to S$ be a finitely presented
flat ring map with geometrically integral fibres. Write
$\mathfrak p = \mathfrak mS$. Let $\mathfrak q \subset S$ be a prime ideal
lying over $\mathfrak m$. Let $N$ be a finite $S$-module.
There exist $r \geq 0$ and an $S$-module map
$$
\alpha : S^{\oplus r} \longrightarrow N
$$
such that
$\alpha : \kappa(\mathfrak p)^{\oplus r} \to N \otimes_S \kappa(\mathfrak p)$
is an isomorphism. For any such $\alpha$ the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat,
\item $\alpha$ is $R$-universally injective and
$\Coker(\alpha)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat,
\item $\alpha$ is injective and
$\Coker(\alpha)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat,
\item $\alpha_{\mathfrak p}$ is an isomorphism and
$\Coker(\alpha)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat, and
\item $\alpha_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective and
$\Coker(\alpha)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat.
\end{enumerate}

records.statement:
Fix a ring $R$, integers $m\geq0$ and $n\geq1$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}R[x_1,\ldots,x_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n]=\mathbf A^{m+n}_S$, and let $i:Z=\mathbf A^m_S\hookrightarrow X$ be defined by $(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$. Let $b:L=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(X)\to X$ be the blow-up, $P=Z\times_S\mathbf P^{n-1}_S$, and $p:P\to Z$ the projection. Identify the exceptional divisor $E\subset L$ with $P$ via its zero-section embedding into the natural line bundle $L\to P$.

For every $a\geq0$:
(1) the natural map $\Omega^a_{X/S}\xrightarrow{\sim}b_*\Omega^a_{L/S}$ is an isomorphism;
(2) the natural map $\Omega^a_{Z/S}\xrightarrow{\sim}p_*\Omega^a_{P/S}$ is an isomorphism; and
(3) the map $Rb_*\Omega^a_{L/S}\to i_*Rp_*\Omega^a_{P/S}$ induces an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^j$ for every $j\geq1$.

For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. It induces an equivalence Sh((Aff/S)_Zar)≃Sh((Sch/S)_Zar).
hypotheses: S is a scheme.
Sch_Zar is a big Zariski site containing S.
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski
site containing $S$.
The functor $(\textit{Aff}/S)_{Zar} \to (\Sch/S)_{Zar}$
is a special cocontinuous functor. Hence it induces an equivalence
of topoi from $\Sh((\textit{Aff}/S)_{Zar})$ to
$\Sh((\Sch/S)_{Zar})$.
Here special cocontinuous means continuous and cocontinuous, locally faithful (equal image arrows become equal on a cover), locally full (arrows between images lift on a cover of the source object), and cover-dense (every target object has a cover by images).

hypotheses: A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a proper $k$-scheme $T$ and a zero-cycle $\gamma=\sum n_i[x_i]$, define $\deg(\gamma)=\sum n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. For a proper $k$-scheme $T$ and a zero-cycle $\gamma=\sum n_i[x_i]$, define $\deg(\gamma)=\sum n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. For a locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of constant rank $r$ on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, set $\deg(\mathcal E)=\chi(T,\mathcal E)-r\chi(T,\mathcal O_T)$, where $\chi(T,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\dim_kH^j(T,\mathcal F)$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ of dimension $\leq 1$.

rank. Then

Let $S$ be a scheme.

of algebraic spaces, and
\item there exists a surjective \'etale morphism
$Y' \to Y$ of algebraic spaces such that $Y' \times_Y X \to Y'$
is a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}

records.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $j : U \to X$ be an
open subspace. Let $T \subset X$ be a closed subset contained in $U$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $E$ is an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ whose cohomology sheaves

hypotheses:

records.statement:
Let $S$ be a Nagata scheme (and in particular locally Noetherian).
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes locally
of finite type over $S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ proper,
\item for any commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
U \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d]^f \\
C \ar[r] \ar@{..>}[ru] & Y
}
$$
of schemes over $S$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $C$ is a normal integral scheme of finite type over $S$,
\item $U = C \setminus \{c\}$ for some closed point $c \in C$,
\item $A = \mathcal{O}_{C, c}$ has dimension $1$\footnote{It follows
that $A$ is a discrete valuation ring, see
Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-characterize-dvr}.
Moreover, $c$ maps to a finite type point $s \in S$ and
$A$ is essentially of finite type over $\mathcal{O}_{S, s}$.}
\end{enumerate}
then in the commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec(K) \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d]^f \\
\Spec(A) \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[ru] & Y
}
$$
where $K = \text{Frac}(A)$ there exists exactly one dotted arrow\footnote{By
Lemma \ref{lemma-morphism-glueing-near-closed-point} this is
equivalent to asking for the existence and uniqueness of the dotted arrow
making the first commutative diagram commute.}
making the diagram commute.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

\item either $f$ is quasi-compact or $f$ is separated.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a dense open $V \subset Y$
such that $f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

records.statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a proper finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension $d$. Let $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $a_p$ be the right adjoint to $Rp_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, where $Rp_*$ identifies with derived global sections $R\Gamma(X,-)$. Define the *canonical normalized dualizing complex* $D_X=a_p(k[0])$; it is the compactification-based $p^!k$. Put $\omega_X=H^{-d}(D_X)$ and let $t:H^0(X,D_X)\to k$ be the cohomological trace induced by the adjunction counit $R\Gamma(X,D_X)\to k$. Suppose $X$ is additionally Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension $d$, and set $\omega_X=H^{-d}(D_X)$. Then $D_X\simeq\omega_X[d]$, and (1) $\omega_X$ is a dualizing module on $X$ (the lowest cohomology of its dualizing complex); (2) $\omega_X$ is coherent and Cohen–Macaulay as a module, supported on all of $X$; (3) for any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and integer $i$, $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(K,\omega_X[d])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{-i}(X,K),k)$ naturally and compatibly with shifts and distinguished triangles; (4) for any quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$, $\operatorname{Ext}^{d-i}_X(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^i(X,\mathcal F),k)$ naturally. All Ext groups are *global derived Ext*, not sheaf Ext.

records.statement:
Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Given *any* morphism $g:Y'\to Y$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, form $X'=X\times_YY'$ with $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. Write $a'=a_{f'}$. As $f$ is flat the square is Tor-independent, and the canonical duality base-change map
\[
L(g')^*a_f(K)\longrightarrow a_{f'}(Lg^*K)
\]
is an isomorphism for all $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. No Tor-dimension assumption is needed on $g$ beyond qcqs.

conclusions: Upper-shriek structure complex invertible and f^! preserves perfect complexes.
hypotheses: f local complete intersection in FTS_S.
records.statement: Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ is a *local complete intersection morphism*: locally on its source it factors as a regular (Koszul-regular) closed immersion into a smooth $Y$-scheme. Then (1) $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is *derived-invertible*: locally on $X$ it is a shift of an invertible sheaf and admits a two-sided inverse for derived tensor product; and (2) the upper-shriek functor $f^!$ takes perfect objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ to perfect objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, interpreted on the bounded-below subcategory where $f^!$ is defined.

records.title: Lemma — Check injective on ass

conclusions: $c^*\omega_Y \cong \omega_X$.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

records.title: Lemma — Rational bridge canonical

conclusions:
there exists an
ind-Zariski ring map $A \to B$ such that $\Spec(B)$ is w-local,
the set of closed points is $V(IB)$, and $A/I \cong B/IB$.
hypotheses:
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $V(I) \subset \Spec(A)$ be a closed subset
which is a profinite topological space.
records.statement:
**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A **w-local** spectral space has closed set of closed points and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a w-local map between such spaces is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. A ring map is **ind-Zariski** when its target is a filtered colimit of local-isomorphism algebras over the source.

Let $A$ be a ring. Let $V(I) \subset \Spec(A)$ be a closed subset
which is a profinite topological space. Then there exists an
ind-Zariski ring map $A \to B$ such that $\Spec(B)$ is w-local,
the set of closed points is $V(IB)$, and $A/I \cong B/IB$.

conclusions:
the rule that to $f : X' \to X$ assigns

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. Under base change, the pulled-back section defines the corresponding Gysin map. This Gysin map descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

records.title: Lemma — Cap c1 bivariant

conclusions:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a $k$-linear
triangulated category such that $\dim_k \Hom_\mathcal{T}(X, Y) < \infty$
for all $X, Y \in \Ob(\mathcal{T})$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a $k$-linear equivalence
$S : \mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{T}$ and $k$-linear isomorphisms
$c_{X, Y} : \Hom_\mathcal{T}(X, Y) \to \Hom_\mathcal{T}(Y, S(X))^\vee$
functorial in $X, Y \in \Ob(\mathcal{T})$,
\item for every $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{T})$
the functor $Y \mapsto \Hom_\mathcal{T}(X, Y)^\vee$
is representable and the functor $Y \mapsto \Hom_\mathcal{T}(Y, X)^\vee$
is corepresentable.
\end{enumerate}
Representability and corepresentability must use the appropriate covariant or contravariant Hom variance. Finite-dimensional Hom spaces allow bidual identification and construction of a quasi-inverse.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-linear triangulated category is a triangulated category with $k$-vector-space Hom sets and $k$-linear composition and shift. For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Let $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote perfect complexes (locally bounded finite-rank vector-bundle complexes), $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the bounded derived category with coherent cohomology. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.A *Serre functor* on a Hom-finite $k$-linear triangulated category $\mathcal T$ is a $k$-linear self-equivalence $S$ equipped with bifunctorial isomorphisms $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(Y,S(X))^\vee$. The specified bifunctorial isomorphisms are part of the Serre data. A covariant functor is *representable* if isomorphic to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(Q,-)$ for some $Q$ and *corepresentable* if of the opposite Hom variance.

records.title: Lemma — Serre functor exists

conclusions: For every integer n, the cohomology H^n(RHom(N,M)) agrees with Ext^n in D(B) from N to M; this is natural in M and contravariantly in N.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule and M a dg right B-module.
records.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Here $M$ is any differential graded right $B$-module, viewed as an object of $D(B,\mathrm d)$ as appropriate.

Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded algebras
over a ring $R$. Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Then for every $n \in \mathbf{Z}$ there are isomorphisms
$$
H^n(R\Hom(N, M)) = \Ext^n_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, M)
$$
of $R$-modules functorial in $M$. It is also functorial in $N$
contravariantly under homomorphisms of differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodules (by precomposition on derived Hom).

records.title: Lemma — Compare tr deg

conclusions:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $\Lambda$
be a Noetherian ring. The category of constructible sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules is exactly the category of modules of the form
$$
\Coker\left(
\bigoplus\nolimits_{j = 1, \ldots, m} j_{V_j!}\underline{\Lambda}_{V_j}
\longrightarrow
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} j_{U_i!}\underline{\Lambda}_{U_i}
\right)
$$
with $V_j$ and $U_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects of

conclusions: $\mathcal J$ is quasi-regular iff it is finite type, $\mathcal J/\mathcal J^2$ is finite locally free over $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal J$, and every canonical map $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathcal J/\mathcal J^2)\to\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism for $n\geq0$.
hypotheses: X is a locally ringed space and $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O_X$ is an ideal sheaf.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X$ be a locally ringed space. Let $\mathcal{J} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be a sheaf of ideals. Then $\mathcal{J}$ is quasi-regular if and
only if the following conditions are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{J}$ is an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite type,
\item $\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{J}^2$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}$-module, and
\item the canonical maps
$$
\text{Sym}^n_{\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}}(\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{J}^2)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{J}^n/\mathcal{J}^{n + 1}
$$
are isomorphisms for all $n \geq 0$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: If E has Tor-amplitude [a,b], then every stalk E_p has Tor-amplitude [a,b] over O_p.

For a ringed site (C,O), an object E∈D(O) has **Tor-amplitude in [a,b]** (integers a≤b) if H^i(E⊗^L_O F)=0 for every O-module F and every i outside [a,b]. of the site $\mathcal{C}$ the object $E_p$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_p)$
has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$.

records.title: Theorem — Tsen

conclusions: The base change f':X×_Y Y'→Y' has P.

records.statement: A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms is *local on the target for the $\tau$-topology* if for every $\tau$-covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}$, a morphism $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$ if and only if each base-changed morphism $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ has $\mathcal P$. records.title: Lemma — Formal consequence

conclusions: i is quasi-regular iff it is locally of finite presentation, its conormal sheaf is finite locally free, and $\operatorname{Sym}^*(\mathcal C_{Z/X})\to\mathcal C_{Z/X,*}$ is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: $i:Z\to X$ is an immersion of schemes.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. For an immersion $i:Z\to X$, choose an open $V\subset X$ where it is closed, with ideal $\mathcal I$; the conormal algebra $\mathcal C_{Z/X,*}$ has degree $n$ piece corresponding to $\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ on $Z$, and $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal C_{Z/X,1}$. Its canonical map from $\operatorname{Sym}^*(\mathcal C_{Z/X})$ is induced by multiplication of ideals. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes. Then $i$ is a quasi-regular
immersion if and only if the following conditions are satisfied
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is locally of finite presentation,
\item the conormal sheaf $\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ is finite locally free, and
\item the map (\ref{equation-conormal-algebra-quotient}) is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

affine open $U \subset X$ with $E \subset U$.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, say *at worst nodal of relative dimension one* if $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and each nonempty geometric fibre is an equidimensional one-dimensional scheme with at-worst-nodal singularities. Here syntomic means flat, locally of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres. This property is stable under base change and local for the étale topology on the source and fpqc topology on the target.

records.title: Lemma — Descent representable transformations property

conclusions: Bifunctorial pro-adjunction Hom(K,f^!L)≈Hom_Pro(Rf_!K,L).
hypotheses: f in FTS_S, K bounded coherent on X, L bounded below coherent on Y, compactification-based upper/lower shriek.
records.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$; let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of separated schemes of finite type over $S$. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, the *upper shriek* $f^!$ sends $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ and is built from proper compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$ by $j^*a_{\bar f}$, where $a_{\bar f}$ is right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$. The corresponding *lower shriek* $Rf_!:D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_Y))$ is $R\bar f_*Rj_!$ for any compactification; proper pushforward is applied termwise to the pro-system. Then for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ and every *bounded-below coherent* $L\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ there is a bifunctorial isomorphism of Hom sets
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(K,f^!L)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y))}(Rf_!K,L).
\]
The right side regards $L$ as a **constant** pro-object; this is the coherent pro-category analogue of an adjunction, not an ordinary adjunction between $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)$ and $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(Y)$ alone.

conclusions:
Let $R \to R'$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $R \to A$ be of finite type. Set $A' = A \otimes_R R'$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R \to R'$ is flat, or
\item $R \to A$ is flat, or
\item $R \to A$ is perfect
and $R'$ and $A$ are tor independent over $R$,
\end{enumerate}
then there is an isomorphism
$\omega_{A/R}^\bullet \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' \to \omega^\bullet_{A'/R'}$
in $D(A')$.
