\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i\in I}$ is an \'etale covering and for each
$i$ we have an \'etale covering $\{T_{ij} \to T_i\}_{j\in J_i}$, then
$\{T_{ij} \to T\}_{i \in I, j\in J_i}$ is an \'etale covering.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i\in I}$ is an \'etale covering
and $T' \to T$ is a morphism of schemes then
$\{T' \times_T T_i \to T'\}_{i\in I}$ is an \'etale covering.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. conclusions: Scalar extension of ω_A is dualizing over A[x].
hypotheses: A Noetherian, dualizing ω_A, B=A[x].
records.statement: For a Noetherian ring $A$, let $D_{\rm Coh}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full derived category of complexes with finitely generated cohomology in every degree. A *dualizing complex* $\omega_A^\bullet\in D(A)$ means a bounded complex with finite injective dimension and finitely generated cohomology such that the homothety map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\omega_A^\bullet,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. The functor $\mathbb D_A(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is contravariant. If $\omega_A^\bullet$ is dualizing, then the flat scalar extension $\omega_A^\bullet\otimes_A A[x]$ is a dualizing complex over the polynomial ring $A[x]$. No cohomological shift is needed merely to obtain *a* dualizing complex; normalization in a local sense is a separate question.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

hypotheses: Finite type X/S, dualizing D_X normalized relative D_S, dimension function by normalized stalk.
records.statement:
Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. For a dualizing complex $D_T$ on a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, its associated dimension function $\delta_T:T\to\mathbf Z$ assigns to $t$ the unique integer such that the stalk $D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)]$ is a *normalized* dualizing complex over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, i.e. $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}(\kappa(t),D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)])\simeq\kappa(t)[0]$. For $x\in X$ above $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the fibre and $\dim_x(X_y)$ its local topological dimension at $x$ (minimum dimension of neighbourhoods in the fibre). Let $f:X\to S$ be of finite type, and $D_X$ normalized relative to $D_S$. For every $x\in X$, with $s=f(x)$, one has
\[
\delta_X(x)-\delta_S(s)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x).
\]
Here $\delta_X,\delta_S$ are normalized dualizing dimension functions, and $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is the induced residue-field extension.

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ and $q : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$
be $1$-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.
If $p$ and $q$ are limit preserving on objects, then so is the composition
$q \circ p$.

conclusions: Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined for f, in the regular-section-preserving sense above.
hypotheses:
$f:X\to Y$ is a scheme morphism and at least one of the seven cases below holds: every weakly associated point of $X$ maps to
a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$, ; $X$, $Y$ are integral and $f$ is dominant, ; $X$ is integral and the generic point of $X$ maps
to a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$, ; $X$ is reduced and every generic point of every irreducible
component of $X$ maps to the generic point of an irreducible component
of $Y$, ; $X$ is locally Noetherian, and any associated point of
$X$ maps to a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$, ; $X$ is locally Noetherian, has no embedded points and
any generic point of an irreducible component of
$X$ maps to the generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$, and ; $f$ is flat.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
In each of the following cases pullbacks of meromorphic
functions are defined.
\begin{enumerate}
\item every weakly associated point of $X$ maps to
a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$, $Y$ are integral and $f$ is dominant,
\item $X$ is integral and the generic point of $X$ maps
to a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$ is reduced and every generic point of every irreducible
component of $X$ maps to the generic point of an irreducible component
of $Y$,
\item $X$ is locally Noetherian, and any associated point of
$X$ maps to a generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$,
\item $X$ is locally Noetherian, has no embedded points and
any generic point of an irreducible component of
$X$ maps to the generic point of an irreducible component of $Y$, and
\item $f$ is flat.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth curves over $k$, the following are equivalent: the function-field extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ is finite separable, the map of invertible differential sheaves $df:f^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$ is generically nonzero, and $f$ is étale on a dense open subscheme of $X$. Under these conditions, the different ideal is the zeroth Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/Y}$, whose closed zero scheme $R_f$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$. Its degree is $\deg R_f=\sum_x\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal O_{R_f,x})[\kappa(x):k]$. For proper smooth curves, $\deg f=[k(X):k(Y)]$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth curves over $k$, the following are equivalent: the function-field extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ is finite separable, the map of invertible differential sheaves $df:f^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$ is generically nonzero, and $f$ is étale on a dense open subscheme of $X$. Under these conditions, the different ideal is the zeroth Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/Y}$, whose closed zero scheme $R_f$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$. Its degree is $\deg R_f=\sum_x\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal O_{R_f,x})[\kappa(x):k]$. For proper smooth curves, $\deg f=[k(X):k(Y)]$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

For an extension of discrete valuation rings $A\subset B$ with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_B$, the ramification index $e(B/A)$ is defined by $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B^e$. For a finite extension of fields $L/k$, the inseparable degree $[L:k]_i$ is $[L:k]/[L:k]_s$.\n\nLet $X$ be a smooth curve over a field $k$. Let
$\overline{x} \in X_{\overline{k}}$ be a closed
point with image $x \in X$. The ramification index of
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x} \subset \mathcal{O}_{X_{\overline{k}}, \overline{x}}$
is the inseparable degree of $\kappa(x)/k$.

\begin{reference}

\end{reference}
Let $F : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}'$ be an exact functor of
triangulated categories. Let $S \subset \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ be
a set of objects. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ has both right and left adjoints,
\item for $K \in \mathcal{D}$ if $\Hom(E, K[i]) = 0$ for all
$E \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ then $K = 0$,
\item for $K \in \mathcal{D}$ if $\Hom(K, E[i]) = 0$ for all
$E \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ then $K = 0$,

is bijective for all $E, E' \in S$ and $i \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is fully faithful.
S is a set of left- and right-spanning objects: vanishing of all shifted Hom from S and to S separately detects zero. Both adjoints to F are assumed, and the Hom comparison for all E,E' in S and all shifts is bijective.

conclusions: For every U∈B, j_{U!}O_U has the **bounded-below** compactness property: Hom(j_{U!}O_U,⊕_iM_i)≅⊕_iHom(j_{U!}O_U,M_i) whenever the sum is bounded below.

records.statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The selected covers Cov form a **finite cofinal system** for every U∈B, with all finite iterated fibre products remaining in B; this condition, not mere quasi-compactness of U, is the source hypothesis.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site
with set of coverings $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ with $I$ finite,
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then for $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the object $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$ is
a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$ in the following sense:
if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U, M) =
\bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U, M_i)$.

conclusions:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let
$\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf\}$.
Let $\mathcal{C}_1 \subset \mathcal{C}_2 \subset (\Sch/X)_\tau$ be full
subcategories with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For an object $U/X$ of $\mathcal{C}_t$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $\{U_i \to U\}$ is a covering of $(\Sch/X)_\tau$, then
$U_i/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$,
\item $U \times \mathbf{A}^1/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$.
\end{enumerate}
\item $X/X$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}_t$.
\end{enumerate}
We endow $\mathcal{C}_t$ with the structure of a site whose coverings are
exactly those coverings $\{U_i \to U\}$ of $(\Sch/X)_\tau$ with
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C}_t)$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] The functor $\mathcal{C}_1 \to \mathcal{C}_2$
is fully faithful, continuous, and cocontinuous.
\end{enumerate}
Denote $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}_1) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C}_2)$ the corresponding
morphism of topoi. Denote $\mathcal{O}_t$ the restriction of $\mathcal{O}$
to $\mathcal{C}_t$. Denote $g_!$ the functor of
Modules on Sites, Definition \ref{sites-modules-definition-g-shriek}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(b)] The canonical map $g_!\mathcal{O}_1 \to \mathcal{O}_2$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
The sites are **full subcategories** of the selected big-$\tau$ site, closed under base-site covering members and $U\times_X\mathbf A^1_X$, containing $X/X$. The left adjoint $g_!$ here is the **module lower-shriek** functor from the included site, and the comparison is specifically $g_!\mathcal O_1\simeq\mathcal O_2$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. For an immersion $i:Z\to X$, choose an open $V\subset X$ where it is closed, with ideal $\mathcal I$; the conormal algebra $\mathcal C_{Z/X,*}$ has degree $n$ piece corresponding to $\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ on $Z$, and $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal C_{Z/X,1}$. Its canonical map from $\operatorname{Sym}^*(\mathcal C_{Z/X})$ is induced by multiplication of ideals. Let $i : Z \to Y$ and $j : Y \to X$ be immersions of schemes. Assume
$j$ is locally of finite presentation and that the sequence
$$
0 \to i^*\mathcal{C}_{Y/X} \to
\mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to
\mathcal{C}_{Z/Y} \to 0
$$
of
Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-transitivity-conormal}
is exact and locally split.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $j \circ i$ is a quasi-regular immersion, so is $i$.
\item If $j \circ i$ is a $H_1$-regular immersion, so is $i$.
\item If both $j$ and $j \circ i$ are Koszul-regular immersions, so is $i$.
\end{enumerate}

covering $\{U_i \to X\}$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is the map of
constant abelian sheaves associated to a map of abelian groups.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a ring.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be a map
of locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$.

A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

conclusions: The two upper-shriek base-change objects are locally isomorphic on suitable affine opens, with no global canonical map asserted.
hypotheses: Cartesian square in FTS_S; f flat; E and Lg^*E bounded below; affine U' maps into affine opens in all relevant schemes.
records.statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Consider any cartesian square $X'=X\times_YY'$ with maps $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, and $g':X'\to X$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$. Suppose $f$ is flat and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ is such that $Lg^*E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_{Y'})$. For each affine open $U'\subseteq X'$ whose images are contained in affine opens of $X,Y,Y'$, the two derived complexes $L(g')^*(f^!E)|_{U'}$ and $(f')^!(Lg^*E)|_{U'}$ are isomorphic in $D(\mathcal O_{U'})$. This is an assertion of existence of local isomorphisms and does not claim they glue to a canonical global base-change transformation.

hypotheses: A divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$ is a commutative ring $A$, ideal $I$, and operations $\gamma_n:I\to I$ ($n\ge1$), with $\gamma_0(x)=1$, $\gamma_1(x)=x$, $\gamma_n(ax)=a^n\gamma_n(x)$, $\gamma_n(x+y)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_j(y)$, $\gamma_m(x)\gamma_n(x)=\binom{m+n}{m}\gamma_{m+n}(x)$, and $\gamma_m(\gamma_n(x))=(mn)!/(m!(n!)^m)\,\gamma_{mn}(x)$. A homomorphism of divided power rings carries distinguished ideals into one another and commutes with all divided power operations.

For a divided power ring $(A,I,\gamma)$, an $A$-algebra $B$ and an ideal $J\subset B$ containing $IB$, the divided power envelope $D_{B,\gamma}(J)=(D,\bar J,\bar\gamma)$ is the universal divided power $(A,I,\gamma)$-algebra equipped with a ring map $B\to D$ carrying $J$ into $\bar J$: maps $D\to(C,K,\delta)$ of divided power $A$-algebras correspond naturally to $A$-algebra maps $B\to C$ carrying $J$ into $K$. The canonical map $D\to B/J$ has kernel $\bar J$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

records.title: Lemma — Make base

conclusions: The following are equivalent: $Q(X)$ is zero; some zero map $X\to Y$ belongs to $S$; and some zero map $Z\to X$ belongs to $S$.
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be additive, $S$ a multiplicative system, $X\in\mathcal C$, and $Q:\mathcal C\to S^{-1}\mathcal C$ its localization functor.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an additive category. Let $S$ be a multiplicative
system. Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$, and $Q:\mathcal C\to S^{-1}\mathcal C$ the localization functor. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Q(X) = 0$ in $S^{-1}\mathcal{C}$,
\item there exists $Y \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ such that
$0 : X \to Y$ is an element of $S$, and
\item there exists $Z \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ such that
$0 : Z \to X$ is an element of $S$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Abelian variety multiplication by p

conclusions: Transitivity/coherence of comparison μ with composition of schemes.
hypotheses: Two composable qcqs maps f,g and the canonical comparison μ for f,g,h.
records.statement:
For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ for the unbounded derived category of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology on $T$, and let $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$. Its unit and counit are $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_fRf_*$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be composable qcqs scheme maps, $h=g\circ f$, and write $a=a_f$, $b=a_g$, $c=a_h\simeq a\circ b$. For any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ there are two natural maps from
\[
Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes_Y^{\mathbf L}b(\mathcal O_Z))\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}a(\mathcal O_Y)
\]
to $c(K)$: (i) apply $\mu_{f,Lg^*K\otimes b(\mathcal O_Z)}$ and then $a(\mu_{g,K})$, or (ii) first apply the base-change associativity and the comparison at the structure sheaf to identify the source with $Lh^*K\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}c(\mathcal O_Z)$, then apply $\mu_{h,K}$. These two maps agree, with the canonical identifications of pullbacks and right adjoints.

records.title: Lemma — Thickening quasi affine

conclusions: Any algebraic space locally of finite type over $X$ is Jacobson.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

records.title: Lemma — Derived complete limit

conclusions: The adjunction unit $K\to Rf_*f^*K$ is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: $f$ is a **flat** morphism of ringed topoi.
$K\in D^+(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ is bounded below.
For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the unit $H^q(K)\to Rf_*f^*H^q(K)$ is an isomorphism.
records.statement:
Let $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O')$ be a morphism of ringed topoi, with adjoint derived functors $Lf^*:D(\mathcal O')\to D(\mathcal O)$ and $Rf_*:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$. A weak Serre subcategory is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions arising from its morphisms; $D_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal O)$ consists of derived objects whose cohomology modules lie in $\mathcal A$. With $f$ flat and $K$ bounded below **downstairs**, the source assumes each cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ satisfies the derived adjunction **unit** $H^q(K)\to Rf_*f^*H^q(K)$. The conclusion is the unit on the **whole** complex.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Let $K$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat,
\item $K$ is bounded below,
\item $H^q(K) \to Rf_*f^*H^q(K)$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $K \to Rf_*f^*K$ is an isomorphism.

records.title: Lemma — Improve distinguished triangle homotopy

conclusions: $\delta$ is a dimension function.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

decent and locally Noetherian algebraic spaces. Let
$\delta : |X| \to \mathbf{Z}$ be a function. If $\delta \circ |f|$ is a
dimension function, then $\delta$ is a dimension function.

records.title: Lemma — Affine big site smooth

conclusions: For each $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map of sheaves $H^q(R\varprojlim_nK_n)\to\varprojlim_n H^q(K_n)$ is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site and $(K_n)$ is an inverse system in $D(\mathcal O)$.
$\mathcal B\subseteq\mathrm{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ covers every site object.
For all $U\in\mathcal B$ and all $q\in\mathbf Z$, $H^p(U,H^q(K_n))=0$ for all $p>0$ and every $n$, and $R^1\varprojlim_n H^0(U,H^q(K_n))=0$.
records.statement:
For an inverse system of complexes $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, $R\varprojlim K_n$ is its homotopy/derived inverse limit. The $R^1\varprojlim$ terms are first right-derived inverse limits of systems of abelian groups, and the natural comparison to the termwise inverse limit need not be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses. The canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_n\tau_{\ge -n}E$ uses good truncations. Here $H^q(K_n)$ denotes cohomology **sheaves**, and $H^0(U,H^q(K_n))$ denotes their section groups. The $R^1\varprojlim$ hypothesis is imposed on these degree-zero section groups for each site object in a covering set and each cohomology degree.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $(K_n)$
be an inverse system of objects of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be a subset. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item every object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a covering whose members are
elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
\item for all $U \in \mathcal{B}$ and all $q \in \mathbf{Z}$ we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(U, H^q(K_n)) = 0$ for $p > 0$,
\item the inverse system $H^0(U, H^q(K_n))$ has vanishing $R^1\lim$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^q(R\lim K_n) = \lim H^q(K_n)$ for $q \in \mathbf{Z}$.

records.title: Lemma — Classical generator generator

conclusions: Derived dual with ω_A equals degree-zero Matlis dual.
hypotheses: Normalized local dualizing ω_A, injective hull E, finite-length N.
records.statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring, with a *normalized* dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$: this is a dualizing complex satisfying $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\kappa[0]$. For an $A$-module $M$ put $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M,\omega_A^\bullet)=H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,\omega_A^\bullet))$. Let $E$ be an injective hull of the residue field $\kappa$, i.e. an injective $A$-module in which $\kappa$ is an essential submodule. For every finite-length $A$-module $N$, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,E)[0].
\]
The right-hand side is the ordinary Matlis dual viewed in degree $0$; its derived higher cohomology vanishes on finite-length $N$. The isomorphism is functorial in $N$, not merely one selected for each module.

Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. \[
Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\xrightarrow{\mu_{f,K}}a_f(K)
\]
is an isomorphism. In particular, the functor $a_f$ is obtained by derived pullback followed by tensoring with the relative dualizing complex, functorially on the full unbounded quasi-coherent derived category.

records.title: Lemma — Covering sheaf

conclusions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
The topological space of $X$ is catenary
(Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-catenary}).
\item
For $x \in X$ closed, we have $\dim_x(X) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$.
\item
For $X$ irreducible we have $\dim(X) = \dim(U)$ for any
nonempty open $U \subset X$ and $\dim(X) = \dim_x(X)$
for any $x \in X$.
\item
For $X$ irreducible any chain of irreducible closed subsets can be
extended to a maximal chain and all maximal chains of irreducible
closed subsets have length equal to $\dim(X)$.
\item
For $x \in X$ we have
$\dim_x(X) = \max \dim(Z) = \min \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'})$
where the maximum is over irreducible components
$Z \subset X$ containing $x$ and the minimum is over
specializations $x \leadsto x'$ with $x'$ closed in $X$.
\item
If $X$ is irreducible with generic point $x$, then
$\dim(X) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x))$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is an immediate specialization
of points of $X$, then we have
$\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x')) + 1$.
\item
The dimension of $X$ is the supremum of the numbers
$\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x))$ where $x$ runs over the
generic points of the irreducible components of $X$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is a nontrivial specialization of points of $X$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim_x(X) \leq \dim_{x'}(X)$,
\item $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) < \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'})$,
\item $\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) > \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x'))$, and
\item any maximal chain of nontrivial specializations
$x = x_0 \leadsto x_1 \leadsto \ldots \leadsto x_n = x'$ has
length $n = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) - \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x'))$.
\end{enumerate}
\item
For $x \in X$ we have
$\dim_x(X) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) + \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is an immediate specialization
of points of $X$ and $X$ is irreducible or equidimensional, then
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'}) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) + 1$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.
records.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
The topological space of $X$ is catenary
(Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-catenary}).
\item
For $x \in X$ closed, we have $\dim_x(X) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$.
\item
For $X$ irreducible we have $\dim(X) = \dim(U)$ for any
nonempty open $U \subset X$ and $\dim(X) = \dim_x(X)$
for any $x \in X$.
\item
For $X$ irreducible any chain of irreducible closed subsets can be
extended to a maximal chain and all maximal chains of irreducible
closed subsets have length equal to $\dim(X)$.
\item
For $x \in X$ we have
$\dim_x(X) = \max \dim(Z) = \min \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'})$
where the maximum is over irreducible components
$Z \subset X$ containing $x$ and the minimum is over
specializations $x \leadsto x'$ with $x'$ closed in $X$.
\item
If $X$ is irreducible with generic point $x$, then
$\dim(X) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x))$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is an immediate specialization
of points of $X$, then we have
$\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x')) + 1$.
\item
The dimension of $X$ is the supremum of the numbers
$\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x))$ where $x$ runs over the
generic points of the irreducible components of $X$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is a nontrivial specialization of points of $X$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim_x(X) \leq \dim_{x'}(X)$,
\item $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) < \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'})$,
\item $\text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) > \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x'))$, and
\item any maximal chain of nontrivial specializations
$x = x_0 \leadsto x_1 \leadsto \ldots \leadsto x_n = x'$ has
length $n = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) - \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x'))$.
\end{enumerate}
\item
For $x \in X$ we have
$\dim_x(X) = \text{trdeg}_k(\kappa(x)) + \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$.
\item
If $x \leadsto x'$ is an immediate specialization
of points of $X$ and $X$ is irreducible or equidimensional, then
$\dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x'}) = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) + 1$.
\end{enumerate}

A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, use $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for an integral closed subscheme $W\subset T$ write $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly. This operator also descends to Chow groups.

For a pair $(\mathcal M,u)$ with $\mathcal M$ invertible on $T$, $u\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal M)$, and $j:E=Z(u)\hookrightarrow T$, define the Gysin map $j^*:Z_{q+1}(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_q(E)$ on integral closed $W\subset T$ by $j^*[W]=[E\cap W]_q$ if $W\not\subset E$, and $j^*[W]=(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. When $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor, write $E\cdot\alpha=j_*j^*\alpha$ for the resulting intersection class. The Gysin map also descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the pushforward of an integral $[W]\in Z_q(T')$ is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if $\dim_\delta h(W)=q$, and $0$ if that dimension is smaller. This extends linearly and induces a map on Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly. This operator also descends to Chow groups.

For a pair $(\mathcal M,u)$ with $\mathcal M$ invertible on $T$, $u\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal M)$, and $j:E=Z(u)\hookrightarrow T$, define the Gysin map $j^*:Z_{q+1}(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_q(E)$ on integral closed $W\subset T$ by $j^*[W]=[E\cap W]_q$ if $W\not\subset E$, and $j^*[W]=(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. When $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor, write $E\cdot\alpha=j_*j^*\alpha$ for the resulting intersection class. The Gysin map also descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the pushforward of an integral $[W]\in Z_q(T')$ is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if $\dim_\delta h(W)=q$, and $0$ if that dimension is smaller. This extends linearly and induces a map on Chow groups.

Let $X$ be locally
of finite type over $S$. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$, let $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and let $D=Z(s)$ with closed immersion $i:D\hookrightarrow X$. Then
$i^*i_* : \mathrm{CH}_k(D) \to \mathrm{CH}_{k - 1}(D)$ sends $\alpha$ to
$c_1(\mathcal{L}|_D) \cap \alpha$.

conclusions: There is a canonical isomorphism $R\SheafHom(K,E)\simeq R\lim_n(E\otimes^\mathbf L_{\mathcal O_X}K_n^\vee)$, using the inverse system of perfect dual complexes.
hypotheses: $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a ringed space; $(K_n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ is a directed sequence of perfect objects in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, with homotopy colimit $K$; $E$ is any object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$.
records.statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let
$(K_n)_{n \in \mathbf{N}}$ be a system of perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $K = \text{hocolim} K_n$ be the derived colimit
(Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-derived-colimit}).
Then for any object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ we have
$$
R\SheafHom(K, E) = R\lim E \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathcal{O}_X} K_n^\vee
$$
where $(K_n^\vee)$ is the inverse system of dual perfect complexes.

conclusions: φ^!(K)≈D_B(D_A(K)⊗^L_A B) for coherent K.
hypotheses:
Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a finite-type homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Define its *algebraic upper-shriek functor* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ by choosing a presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and putting
\[
\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n].
\]
For surjective $\varphi$, one may use $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$ with its natural $A$-action. Different polynomial presentations give isomorphic functors, but the isomorphisms are *not canonical*. Here $D^\pm$ means bounded below/above cohomology, $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}$ means coherent cohomology, and a *perfect* ring map is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension (equivalently $A$ is a perfect $P$-complex after a suitable finite polynomial presentation).

Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\omega_A^\bullet$ be a dualizing complex for $A$. Set
$\omega_B^\bullet = \varphi^!(\omega_A^\bullet)$. Denote
$D_A(K) = R\Hom_A(K, \omega_A^\bullet)$ for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$
and
$D_B(L) = R\Hom_B(L, \omega_B^\bullet)$ for $L \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(B)$.
records.statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a finite-type homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Define its *algebraic upper-shriek functor* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ by choosing a presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and putting
\[
\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n].
\]
For surjective $\varphi$, one may use $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$ with its natural $A$-action. Different polynomial presentations give isomorphic functors, but the isomorphisms are *not canonical*. Here $D^\pm$ means bounded below/above cohomology, $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}$ means coherent cohomology, and a *perfect* ring map is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension (equivalently $A$ is a perfect $P$-complex after a suitable finite polynomial presentation).

Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\omega_A^\bullet$ be a dualizing complex for $A$. Set
$\omega_B^\bullet = \varphi^!(\omega_A^\bullet)$. Denote
$D_A(K) = R\Hom_A(K, \omega_A^\bullet)$ for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$
and
$D_B(L) = R\Hom_B(L, \omega_B^\bullet)$ for $L \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(B)$.
Then there is a functorial isomorphism
$$
\varphi^!(K) = D_B(D_A(K) \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B)
$$
for $K \in D_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$.

D_A and D_B are two different ring-specific duality functors: D_A(K)=RHom_A(K,ω_A) and D_B(L)=RHom_B(L,ω_B), ω_B=φ^!(ω_A).

For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

records.title: Lemma — Flat finitely presented permanence algebra

conclusions:
the set of
isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under
$\Ext^1_B(\NL_{B/A}, N)$.
hypotheses: Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel $I$; let $A\to B$ be an $A$-algebra, $N$ a $B$-module, and $c:I\to N$ an $A$-linear map. A solution of the lifting problem is a commutative diagram of ring homomorphisms with exact rows $0\to I\to A'\to A\to0$ and $0\to N\to B'\to B\to0$ in which $N\subset B'$ is square-zero, $B'$ is an $A'$-algebra and the induced map $I\to N$ equals $c$. Isomorphisms of solutions commute with the maps from $A'$ and to $B$ and are the identity on the identified $N$.

For a homomorphism of rings $A\to B$ choose a polynomial presentation $P=A[E]\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel $J$. The naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ is the two-term complex $(J/J^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB)$ in cohomological degrees $-1,0$, well defined up to quasi-isomorphism. The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ is its $H^0$. The notation $\operatorname{Ext}_B^q(K,N)$ means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,N[q])$. For ringed spaces, topoi, and schemes, $\mathrm{NL}$ denotes the corresponding locally defined complex of sheaves of modules.
records.statement:
Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel $I$; let $A\to B$ be an $A$-algebra, $N$ a $B$-module, and $c:I\to N$ an $A$-linear map. A solution of the lifting problem is a commutative diagram of ring homomorphisms with exact rows $0\to I\to A'\to A\to0$ and $0\to N\to B'\to B\to0$ in which $N\subset B'$ is square-zero, $B'$ is an $A'$-algebra and the induced map $I\to N$ equals $c$. Isomorphisms of solutions commute with the maps from $A'$ and to $B$ and are the identity on the identified $N$.

For a homomorphism of rings $A\to B$ choose a polynomial presentation $P=A[E]\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernel $J$. The naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ is the two-term complex $(J/J^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{P/A}\otimes_PB)$ in cohomological degrees $-1,0$, well defined up to quasi-isomorphism. The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{B/A}$ is its $H^0$. The notation $\operatorname{Ext}_B^q(K,N)$ means $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(K,N[q])$. For ringed spaces, topoi, and schemes, $\mathrm{NL}$ denotes the corresponding locally defined complex of sheaves of modules.

If there exists a solution to the square-zero ring-algebra lifting problem specified above, then the set of
isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}, N)$.

conclusions: Every quasi-coherent descent datum is effective, and restriction to the covering is fully faithful.
hypotheses: $S$ is affine and $\mathcal U$ is a finite standard fpqc family of affine schemes with faithfully flat disjoint union over $S$.
records.statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be affine, and let $\mathcal U=\{f_i:U_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ be a finite standard fpqc covering: each $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ is affine, and the map $\coprod_{i=1}^nU_i\to S$ is faithfully flat (equivalently, $R\to\prod_{i=1}^nA_i$ is faithfully flat). Given a family of scheme maps $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves is a collection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\mathcal F_i$ with isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $U_i\times_S U_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on every triple overlap. It is effective if the $\mathcal F_i$ are obtained, up to isomorphism of descent data, by pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Then every such datum is effective and the canonical functor $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\to\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal U}(\operatorname{QCoh})$ is fully faithful; in fact it is an equivalence.

hypotheses: Let $(K^\bullet,F)$ be a filtered complex in an abelian category with countable direct sums.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $(K^\bullet, F)$ be a filtered complex of $\mathcal{A}$.
Assume $\mathcal{A}$ has countable direct sums.
Let $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ be the spectral sequence
associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The map
$$
d_1^{p, q} :
E_1^{p, q} = H^{p + q}(\text{gr}^p(K^\bullet))
\longrightarrow
E_1^{p + 1, q} = H^{p + q + 1}(\text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet))
$$
is equal to the boundary map in cohomology associated to the short
exact sequence of complexes
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet) \to
F^pK^\bullet/F^{p + 2}K^\bullet \to \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet) \to 0.
$$
\item Assume that $d(F^pK) \subset F^{p + 1}K$ for all $p \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Then $d$ induces the zero differential on $\text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)$
and hence
$E_1^{p, q} = \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)^{p + q}$.
Furthermore, in this case
$$
d_1^{p, q} :
E_1^{p, q} = \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet)^{p + q}
\longrightarrow
E_1^{p + 1, q} = \text{gr}^{p + 1}(K^\bullet)^{p + q + 1}
$$
is the morphism induced by $d$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

For the full site, $R\Gamma(\mathrm{Cris}(X/S),\mathcal F)$ denotes derived global sections. If $\mathcal F$ is locally quasi-coherent, its restriction $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent on $T$.

records.title: Lemma — Morphism sheaves with P effective descent etale

conclusions: Associated-sheaf equivalences commute with pullback; generally not with big-site pushforward; qcqs small-Zariski/étale pushforward is compatible.
hypotheses: f:T→S is a scheme morphism; qcqs is required for the small-site pushforward claim.
records.statement:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). Let $f:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. (1) For every eligible $\tau$, passing from quasi-coherent sheaves to the associated big-site sheaves commutes with pullback, and the same holds on the small Zariski and étale sites: $f_{\mathrm{site}}^*(\mathcal G^a)\cong(f^*\mathcal G)^a$. (2) The analogous big-site pushforward compatibility is false in general (and $f_*$ need not preserve quasi-coherence). records.title: Lemma — Descending property surjective

conclusions: There is a functorial long exact cohomology sequence with degree-raising connecting maps, compatible with shifted cohomology $H^j(K[k])\cong H^{j+k}(K)$.
hypotheses: $0\to A^\bullet\to B^\bullet\to C^\bullet\to0$ is short exact in cochain complexes of an abelian category.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Suppose that
$$
0 \to
A^\bullet \to
B^\bullet \to
C^\bullet \to
0
$$
is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then there is a long exact cohomology sequence
$$
\xymatrix{
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \ar[lld] \\
H^i(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^i(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
H^{i + 1}(A^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(B^\bullet) \ar[r] &
H^{i + 1}(C^\bullet) \ar[lld] \\
\ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\
}
$$
The construction produces long exact cohomology sequences
which are functorial in the short exact
sequence and compatible with shifts as in
the cochain-shift identification $H^j(K[k])\cong H^{j+k}(K)$ using the signed shift differential.

hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring and $M$ a finite-length $R$-module of length $\ell$. An admissible sequence is an $\ell$-tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ with $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i}Re_j$. The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. This line is one-dimensional. An isomorphism $h:M\to N$ induces $\det_\kappa(h)$ by applying $h$ to admissible symbols. For a short exact sequence $0\to K\to L\to N\to0$, the canonical determinant isomorphism $\gamma_{K\to L\to N}:\det_\kappa K\otimes_\kappa\det_\kappa N\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_\kappa L$ concatenates an admissible sequence of $K$ with chosen lifts of one from $N$; it is natural under isomorphisms of exact sequences.

For finite-length $R$-module $M$ and endomorphisms $\varphi,\psi:M\to M$ with $\varphi\psi=\psi\varphi=0$ and $\ker\varphi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, $\ker\psi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, call $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ an exact $(2,1)$-periodic complex. With $I_\varphi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, $I_\psi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, put $K_\varphi=\ker\varphi=I_\psi$, $K_\psi=\ker\psi=I_\varphi$. Let $\gamma_\varphi:\det K_\varphi\otimes\det I_\varphi\to\det M$, $\gamma_\psi:\det K_\psi\otimes\det I_\psi\to\det M$ be the determinant isomorphisms and $\sigma$ swap the tensor factors. Define $\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)\in\kappa^\times$ as the unique scalar such that $\gamma_\psi\circ\sigma\circ\gamma_\varphi^{-1}$ acts on $\det M$ by $(-1)^{\ell(I_\varphi)\ell(I_\psi)}\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)$.

Define the determinant symbol $d_M(a,b)=\det_\kappa(M/abM,a,b)\in\kappa^\times$. hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring.
records.statement:
**Source-defined terminology (not inherited hypotheses):** A **w-local** spectral space has closed closed-point set and unique closed specialization of each point; a w-local map is spectral and maps closed points to closed points. An **ind-étale** map is a filtered colimit of étale algebras. A ring $A$ is **w-contractible** iff every faithfully flat weakly étale map $A\to B$ admits an $A$-algebra retraction.

Let $A$ be a ring. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is w-contractible,
\item every faithfully flat, ind-\'etale ring map $A \to B$ has
a retraction, and
\item $A$ satisfies
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Spec(A)$ is w-local,
\item $\pi_0(\Spec(A))$ is extremally disconnected, and
\item for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m \subset A$ the
local ring $A_\mathfrak m$ is strictly henselian.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly. This operator also descends to Chow groups.

For a pair $(\mathcal M,u)$ with $\mathcal M$ invertible on $T$, $u\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal M)$, and $j:E=Z(u)\hookrightarrow T$, define the Gysin map $j^*:Z_{q+1}(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_q(E)$ on integral closed $W\subset T$ by $j^*[W]=[E\cap W]_q$ if $W\not\subset E$, and $j^*[W]=(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. When $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor, write $E\cdot\alpha=j_*j^*\alpha$ for the resulting intersection class.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the pushforward of an integral $[W]\in Z_q(T')$ is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if $\dim_\delta h(W)=q$, and $0$ if that dimension is smaller. This extends linearly and induces a map on Chow groups.

conclusions: K^vee:=RSheafHom(K,O) is perfect and the double dual (K^vee)^vee≅K.

hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, K∈D(O) is perfect and M∈D(O).
records.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), the monoidal category of complexes uses total tensor with signed differential, and the symmetric monoidal category D(O) uses derived tensor ⊗^L with Koszul signs. A *left dual* of K is an object K^vee with coevaluation η:O→K⊗K^vee and evaluation ε:K^vee⊗K→O satisfying both triangular identities (using the relevant underived or derived tensor). For perfect K, K^vee=RSheafHom(K,O), and for a chain complex locally strictly perfect the ordinary Hom complex supplies its candidate dual. For any **perfect derived** K, the derived dual K^vee:=RSheafHom(K,O) is again perfect; the formulas are functorial in every M∈D(O), and the H^0 equality is a group-level global-section equality.

$$
M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K^\vee = R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(K, M)
$$
and
$$
H^0(\mathcal{C}, M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} K^\vee) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(K, M)

for $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$.

& &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \ar[d]^{(e, e^\sharp)}
\\

\ar[rr]^{(h, h^\sharp)} & &
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}'), \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'})
}
$$
where
\begin{enumerate}
\item $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C}')$

$\mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{C}'$ (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-special-cocontinuous-functor}),
\item $e : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D}')$

Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-special-cocontinuous-functor}),

\item $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'} = e_*\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$
and $e^\sharp$ is the obvious map,

and fibre products (i.e., all finite limits),

Sites, Proposition \ref{sites-proposition-get-morphism}), and

a representable sheaf on $\mathcal{C}'$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{D}'$).
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $(f, f^\sharp)$ is an equivalence of ringed topoi,
then we can choose the diagram such that
$\mathcal{C}' = \mathcal{D}'$,
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}'} = \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{D}'}$
and $(h, h^\sharp)$ is the identity.

conclusions: There is an abelian Serre quotient $\mathcal A/\mathcal C$ and an essentially surjective exact quotient functor $F$ with kernel $\mathcal C$.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{A}$ be a Serre subcategory.
There exists an abelian category $\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}$
and an exact functor
$$
F : \mathcal{A} \longrightarrow \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}
$$
which is essentially surjective and whose kernel is $\mathcal{C}$.
The category $\mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C}$ and the functor $F$ are
characterized by the following universal property: For any abelian category $\mathcal{B}$ and exact functor $G : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ such that
$\mathcal{C} \subset \Ker(G)$ there exists a factorization
$G = H \circ F$ for a unique exact functor
$H : \mathcal{A}/\mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{B}$.

records.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. Assume $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering and each $X_i\to S_i$ is quasi-affine, meaning that locally on the base the source is quasi-compact and an open subscheme of an affine scheme over that base. Then the descent datum $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ is effective. In particular, the relative affine hulls $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S_i}((p_i)_*\mathcal O_{X_i})$ descend by affine descent, and the compatible quasi-compact open subschemes $X_i$ descend to an open subscheme of the resulting affine hull over $S$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

records.title: Lemma — Closure

conclusions: If K⊗^L_O (O/I) is bounded above, then the reductions K⊗^L_O(O/I^n) are **uniformly** bounded above for all n≥1.
If the reduction K⊗^L_O(O/I), as an object of D(O/I), has Tor-amplitude [a,b], then for every n≥1 the reduction K⊗^L_O(O/I^n), considered in D(O/I^n), has the same Tor-amplitude [a,b].
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, I⊂O is a sheaf of ideals and K∈D(O).
records.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), an object E∈D(O) has **Tor-amplitude in [a,b]** (integers a≤b) if H^i(E⊗^L_O F)=0 for every O-module F and every i outside [a,b]. Finite Tor dimension means such a bounded interval exists; **locally** finite Tor dimension means each object has a cover on which a finite interval exists (the interval may vary). An O-module F has Tor dimension ≤d when F[0] has Tor-amplitude in [−d,0] (source Definition tor-amplitude lines 12376–12394). Let I⊂O be a **sheaf of ideals**; derived tensor reduction modulo I^n produces a complex in D(O/I^n). Uniformly bounded above means there exists one upper cohomological bound valid for **all positive n**. The second clause must distinguish Tor-amplitude as an O/I^n-module from Tor-amplitude over O.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
Let $K$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}$
is bounded above, then
$K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n$
is uniformly bounded above for all $n$.
\item If $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I})$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$,
then $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n)$
has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$ for all $n$.
\end{enumerate}
