A spectral space is **w-local** when its closed-point subset $Z_0$ is closed and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a continuous map between w-local spaces is **w-local** if it is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. This is terminology, not an additional ambient hypothesis.

Let $X$ be a spectral space such that its set of closed points $X_0$ is closed and each $x\in X$ specializes to a unique closed point. records.title: Lemma — Reduced finite irreducible

conclusions: The family is a universally effective epimorphism; representable functors are fpqc sheaves.
hypotheses: The family is fpqc, with arbitrary base change and target test scheme.
records.statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. If $\{T_i\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering of a scheme $T$, then it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes. Equivalently, for every base change $T'\to T$ and every test scheme $Z$, every family of maps $h_i:T_i\times_TT'\to Z$ whose restrictions agree on all pairwise fibre products $(T_i\times_TT')\times_{T'}(T_j\times_TT')$ comes from a unique map $h:T'\to Z$. Thus every representable presheaf $\operatorname{Hom}(-,Z)$ on schemes satisfies fpqc descent.

conclusions: Tensoring with N defines a dg functor from dg right A-modules to dg right B-modules, and induces functors on ordinary dg-module and homotopy categories.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule.
records.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$
be differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. Then
$M \mapsto M \otimes_A N$ defines a functor
$$
- \otimes_A N :
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(A, \text{d})}
\longrightarrow
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}
$$
of differential graded categories. This functor induces functors
$$
\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})} \to \text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})}
\quad\text{and}\quad
K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})})
$$ by passing to closed degree-zero maps and homotopy classes.

records.title: Lemma — Components locally finite

conclusions:
any decent algebraic
space locally of finite type over $X$ is universally catenary.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

records.title: Lemma — Universally catenary

conclusions: The relative Frobenius is finite syntomic and its relative de Rham trace is supported in top differential degree, where it is surjective.
hypotheses: $X/S$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ in characteristic $p$, with the indicated relative Frobenius.
records.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $S$ a scheme of characteristic $p$, and $X\to S$ a smooth morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$. Let $X^{(p)}=X\times_{S,F_S}S$ and let $F_{X/S}:X\to X^{(p)}$ denote relative Frobenius. Then $F_{X/S}$ is finite syntomic. Let
$$\Theta_{X/X^{(p)}}:F_{X/S,*}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}\longrightarrow\Omega^\bullet_{X^{(p)}/S}$$
be its relative de Rham trace map. All graded components of this map vanish except in degree $d$; in degree $d$ the map $F_{X/S,*}\Omega^d_{X/S}\to\Omega^d_{X^{(p)}/S}$ is surjective.

conclusions:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. For any covering
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ of $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$
and any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$
there is a spectral sequence
$$
E_2^{p, q}
=
\check H^p(\mathcal{U}, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
\Rightarrow
H^{p+q}(U, \mathcal{F}),
$$
where $\underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F})$ is the abelian presheaf
$V \mapsto H^q(V, \mathcal{F})$.
The E2 coefficients are Čech cohomology of the **cohomology presheaf** underline H^q(F), not simply Čech cohomology of F in degree q. Repeated cover indices are used; the spectral sequence converges to sheaf cohomology H^{p+q}(U,F).

records.title: Theorem — Cech ss

conclusions: Dualizing complex condition ascends and descends under these covers.
hypotheses: f surjective locally Noetherian, syntomic or flat lci or finite-type Gorenstein; K in D_QCoh(Y).
records.statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism of locally Noetherian schemes satisfying at least one of: (i) $f$ syntomic (flat lfp lci); (ii) $f$ flat and a local complete intersection; (iii) $f$ a finite-type Gorenstein morphism (flat with Gorenstein fibres). For any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the complex $K$ is dualizing on $Y$ iff its derived pullback $Lf^*K$ is dualizing on $X$. The assertion includes both ascent and descent; no properness of $f$ is imposed.

A field $K$ is **$C_r$** if, for every positive integer degree $d$ and number of variables $n>d^r$, every homogeneous degree-$d$ polynomial over $K$ in $n$ variables has a **nonzero common solution** (for one polynomial). A *variety over $k$* in this source means a **separated integral scheme of finite type** over $k$, and its function field is the local ring at the generic point.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let
$f_1, \ldots, f_s \in k[T_1, \ldots, T_n]$
be homogeneous polynomials of degree $d_1, \ldots, d_s$ with $d_i
> 0$. If $s < n$, then $f_1 = \ldots = f_s = 0$ have a common nontrivial
solution.

conclusions: Two pre-rigidity identities and a quadratic rigidity isomorphism for omega.
hypotheses: f proper flat finite presentation over qcqs Y; omega=a_f(O_Y), c right adjoint of diagonal pushforward.
records.statement:
Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Write $X\times_YX$ for the fibre square, $\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2:X\times_YX\to X$ for its two projections, and $\Delta:X\to X\times_YX$ for the diagonal. Let $c:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X\times_YX})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint to $R\Delta_*$. Then there are canonical isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal O_X)$:
\[
\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet})
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c(L\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}),
\]
and
\[
\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}
c(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X\times_YX}}^{\mathbf L}L\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}).
\]
The statement uses the right adjoint for the *diagonal*, not for $f$ itself, and the two projections are taken on the fibre product.

records.title: Lemma — Characterize spec connected

conclusions: $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.
hypotheses: For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, the standing Cohen–Macaulay curve hypotheses imply $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional. Let $\omega_X$ be its coherent dualizing module, equal to $H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for the structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. A regular global section of an invertible sheaf is one whose multiplication map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is injective; an ample invertible sheaf is very ample if its global sections define a closed immersion into projective space.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

C \ar[r] \ar@{..>}[ru] & Y

}
$$
where $K = \text{Frac}(A)$ there exists at most one dotted arrow\footnote{By
Lemma \ref{lemma-morphism-glueing-near-closed-point} this is

records.title: Lemma — Fitting ideal well defined

conclusions: The six conditions listed in the source—strictness, the coimage/image isomorphism, its graded isomorphism, exactness at the middle of each of two graded sequences, and exactness of their combined five-term sequence—are equivalent.
hypotheses: Let $f:A\to B$ be a morphism of finite filtered objects of an abelian category.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of finite
filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is strict,
\item the morphism $\Coim(f) \to \Im(f)$ is an isomorphism,
\item $\text{gr}(\Coim(f)) \to \text{gr}(\Im(f))$ is an
isomorphism,
\item the sequence
$\text{gr}(\Ker(f)) \to \text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B)$
is exact,
\item the sequence $\text{gr}(A) \to \text{gr}(B) \to
\text{gr}(\Coker(f))$ is exact, and
\item the sequence
$$
0 \to
\text{gr}(\Ker(f)) \to
\text{gr}(A) \to
\text{gr}(B) \to
\text{gr}(\Coker(f)) \to 0
$$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

Let $X$ be a scheme
locally of finite type over $S$. Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a virtual normal
sheaf for a closed subscheme $Z$ of $X$. Let $Y \to X$ be a morphism
which is locally of finite type. Given integers $r$, $n$ assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{N}$ is locally free of rank $r$,
\item every irreducible component of $Y$ has $\delta$-dimension $n$,
\item $\dim_\delta(Z \times_X Y) \leq n - r$, and
\item for $\xi \in Z \times_X Y$ with $\delta(\xi) = n - r$
the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi}$ is Cohen-Macaulay.
\end{enumerate}
Then $c(Z \to X, \mathcal{N}) \cap [Y]_n = [Z \times_X Y]_{n - r}$
in $\mathrm{CH}_{n - r}(Z \times_X Y)$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

A morphism of algebraic spaces $Y\to X$ is *integral* if it is affine and integral after base change to every scheme over $X$. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space, an integral cover by a scheme is a surjective integral morphism $Y\to X$ with $Y$ a scheme. The *schematic locus* of an algebraic space is its largest open subspace representable by a scheme, when such a locus exists; a dense open scheme in $X$ means an open subscheme with dense image in $|X|$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A quasi-compact open immersion is an open embedding whose source is quasi-compact. A reduced closed subspace of an algebraic space is its uniquely determined reduced induced closed subspace. An étale stratification of $X$ by schemes is a finite chain of closed subspaces $\varnothing=Z_{-1}\subset Z_0\subset\cdots\subset Z_n=X$, whose locally closed differences $Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ are schemes. An algebraic space is quasi-compact if it admits a finite affine étale cover, and quasi-separated when its diagonal is quasi-compact.

records.title: Proposition — Cohomological dimension spectral

conclusions: The induced pullback functor on descent-data categories is an equivalence.
hypotheses: f:X'→X over S admits any reverse S-map g:X→X'.
records.statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $f:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$. Assume there exists an $S$-morphism $g:X\to X'$ (in particular, a section of $f$ suffices, but $f\circ g=\mathrm{id}_X$ is not required). Then $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse $g^*$, since both composites are pullbacks by $S$-selfmaps and hence naturally isomorphic to the identity.

For an inverse system of complexes $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, $R\varprojlim K_n$ is its homotopy/derived inverse limit. The $R^1\varprojlim$ terms are first right-derived inverse limits of systems of abelian groups, and the natural comparison to the termwise inverse limit need not be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses. be a morphism of ringed topoi. Then $Rf_*$ commutes with $R\lim$, i.e.,

hypotheses: $f:X\to Y$ is a morphism of ringed spaces, $X=U\cup V$ with $U,V$ open; $a,b,c$ are its restrictions to $U,V,U\cap V$; $\mathcal F$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module.
records.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.
Suppose that $X = U \cup V$ is a union of two open subsets.
Denote $a = f|_U : U \to Y$, $b = f|_V : V \to Y$, and
$c = f|_{U \cap V} : U \cap V \to Y$.
For every $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$
there exists a long exact sequence
$$
0 \to
f_*\mathcal{F} \to
a_*(\mathcal{F}|_U) \oplus b_*(\mathcal{F}|_V) \to
c_*(\mathcal{F}|_{U \cap V}) \to
R^1f_*\mathcal{F} \to \ldots
$$
This long exact sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. records.title: Lemma — Bivariant zero

conclusions:
Any representable presheaf on $\Sch/S$ satisfies the
sheaf condition for the fpqc topology.
For a fixed S-scheme Y, the representable h_Y(T)=Hom_S(T,Y) satisfies the fpqc equalizer for every fpqc cover of each S-scheme T. This is subcanonicity of fpqc descent and includes non-affine target Y.
hypotheses:
A *site* $\mathcal C$ is a small category endowed with covering families $\{U_i\to U\}$ satisfying the isomorphism, composition/refinement, and base-change axioms. A *presheaf* of sets (or abelian groups) is a contravariant functor. For a covering, a *matching family* consists of sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ whose restrictions to every fibre product $U_i\times_UU_j$ coincide (including $i=j$). A presheaf is *separated* if sections are uniquely determined by restrictions to each covering, and a *sheaf* if every matching family glues uniquely.

For a base scheme $S$, let $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ denote **all schemes over $S$** (using the source's size conventions). An *fpqc covering* $\{T_i\to T\}$ consists of flat maps whose images cover $T$ and such that for each affine open $U\subseteq T$ there are finitely many affine opens in some $T_i$ whose images cover $U$. A singleton $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is fpqc exactly when $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. An *fpqc sheaf property* for a presheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ means the usual equalizer condition for **all** fpqc coverings; because of size issues this does not presume a single small fpqc site of all schemes exists.

conclusions:
there is a canonical bivariant class
$$
P'_p(E_2),\text{ resp. }c'_p(E_2) \in A^p(X_2 \to X)
$$

$$

\quad\text{and}\quad

\quad\text{and}\quad

$X' \to X$ locally of finite type.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. conclusions: The map of sections of cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^m(R\varprojlim_nK_n)(V)\to\mathcal H^m(K_{n(V)})(V)$ is injective.

There exist an index $n(V)$ and a cofinal system of coverings $\mathrm{Cov}_V$ such that, for every member $\{V_i\to V\}$ and each $i$, $R^1\varprojlim_n H^{m-1}(V_i,K_n)=0$.
For every such $V_i$ and all $n\ge n(V)$, the transition $H^m(V_i,K_n)\to H^m(V_i,K_{n(V)})$ is injective.
records.statement:
For an inverse system of complexes $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, $R\varprojlim K_n$ is its homotopy/derived inverse limit. The $R^1\varprojlim$ terms are first right-derived inverse limits of systems of abelian groups, and the natural comparison to the termwise inverse limit need not be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses. The canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_n\tau_{\ge -n}E$ uses good truncations. For an inverse system $(K_n)$ of derived objects, write $\mathcal H^m(R\varprojlim K_n)$ for the $m$th cohomology **sheaf** of its homotopy limit. Its evaluation on $V$ is different in general from $H^m(V,R\varprojlim K_n)$; the conclusion is injectivity on sections of cohomology **sheaves**. The function $n(V)$ is an integer depending only on $V$, and $\mathrm{Cov}_V$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $V$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $(K_n)$ be an
inverse system in $D(\mathcal{O})$. Let $V \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$
and $m \in \mathbf{Z}$. Assume there exist an integer $n(V)$
and a cofinal system $\text{Cov}_V$ of coverings of $V$ such that
for $\{V_i \to V\} \in \text{Cov}_V$
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R^1\lim H^{m - 1}(V_i, K_n) = 0$, and
\item $H^m(V_i, K_n) \to H^m(V_i, K_{n(V)})$ is injective
for $n \geq n(V)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map on sections $H^m(R\lim K_n)(V) \to H^m(K_{n(V)})(V)$ is injective.

conclusions: If $i$ and $j$ are regular immersions, so is $j \circ i$.

hypotheses: Let $i : Z \to Y$ and $j : Y \to X$ be immersions of schemes.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to Y$ and $j : Y \to X$ be immersions of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $i$ and $j$ are regular immersions, so is $j \circ i$.
\item If $i$ and $j$ are Koszul-regular immersions, so is $j \circ i$.

records.statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. For an open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ of finite-type $S$-schemes and dualizing complexes $D_X,D_Y$ normalized relative to the same fixed base dualizing complex $D_S$, there is a canonical isomorphism $D_X\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*D_Y$, compatible with the local normalizing isomorphisms.

records.title: Lemma — Geometrically irreducible function field

conclusions: Any locally Noetherian decent algebraic space is quasi-separated.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

records.title: Proposition — Topological invariance

conclusions:
Let $A \to B$ be a ring map inducing algebraic extensions on residue fields.
There exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
B \ar[r] & D \\
A \ar[r] \ar[u] & C \ar[u]
}
$$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to C$ is faithfully flat and ind-\'etale,
\item $B \to D$ is faithfully flat and ind-\'etale,
\item $\Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item $\Spec(D)$ is w-local,
\item $\Spec(D) \to \Spec(C)$ is w-local,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(D)$ is the inverse image
of the set of closed points of $\Spec(C)$,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(C)$ surjects onto $\Spec(A)$,
\item the set of closed points of $\Spec(D)$ surjects onto $\Spec(B)$,
\item for $\mathfrak m \subset C$ maximal the local ring
$C_\mathfrak m$ is strictly henselian.
\end{enumerate}

A map $A\to B$ is étale **at** $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ if $A\to B_h$ is étale for some $h\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$. An étale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ has étale maps and jointly surjective images.

Any \'etale covering is an fpqc covering.

**Precise scope:** An étale cover by possibly infinitely many source schemes is fpqc: étale implies flat/open; on each **affine open in U**, quasi-compactness yields a *finite* family of affine opens in the sources with images covering it.

hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C'),\mathcal O')$ is a **flat** morphism of ringed topoi.

The exact pullback $f^*$ induces an equivalence $\mathcal A'\simeq\mathcal A$.
For every $\mathcal F'\in\mathcal A'$, the derived unit $\mathcal F'\to Rf_*f^*\mathcal F'$ is an isomorphism.
records.statement:

A weak Serre subcategory is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions arising from its morphisms; $D_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal O)$ consists of derived objects whose cohomology modules lie in $\mathcal A$. Here $f^*$ is exact because $f$ is flat. The derived categories are the **bounded-below** subcategories whose cohomology sheaves lie in the given weak Serre classes. The unit hypothesis concerns every object $\mathcal F'$ of the target class $\mathcal A'$, and the equivalence $f^*:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$ is part of the premises.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')$
be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{A} \subset \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$
and $\mathcal{A}' \subset \textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}')$
be weak Serre subcategories. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is flat,
\item $f^*$ induces an equivalence of categories
$\mathcal{A}' \to \mathcal{A}$,
\item $\mathcal{F}' \to Rf_*f^*\mathcal{F}'$ is an isomorphism
for $\mathcal{F}' \in \Ob(\mathcal{A}')$.
\end{enumerate}

$f^* : D_{\mathcal{A}'}^+(\mathcal{O}') \to D_\mathcal{A}^+(\mathcal{O})$
is an equivalence of categories with quasi-inverse given by
$Rf_* : D_\mathcal{A}^+(\mathcal{O}) \to D_{\mathcal{A}'}^+(\mathcal{O}')$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

conclusions: There is a spectral sequence of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal E}$-modules $E_2^{p,q}=R^p g_*(R^q f_*\mathcal F)\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(g\circ f)_*\mathcal F$, functorial in $\mathcal F$.
An analogous relative Leray spectral sequence exists for bounded-below complexes of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules.
hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ and $g:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal E),\mathcal O_{\mathcal E})$ are composable morphisms of ringed topoi.
$\mathcal F$ is an $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module.
records.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be composable morphisms of ringed topoi, and let $R^q f_*$ and $R^p g_*$ denote their higher direct images. The spectral sequence computes the higher direct images of the composite $g\circ f$, not merely global cohomology. The same construction is asserted for bounded-below complexes in place of a single module.

Let
$f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
and
$g : (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{E}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{E})$
be morphisms of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-module.
There is a spectral sequence with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = R^pg_*(R^qf_*\mathcal{F})
$$
converging to $R^{p + q}(g \circ f)_*\mathcal{F}$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$, and there
is a version for bounded below complexes of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules.

conclusions:

hypotheses:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\xi \in Y$ be a point.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$, $Y$ are integral,
\item $Y$ is locally Noetherian
\item $f$ is proper, dominant and $R(Y) \subset R(X)$ is finite, and
\item $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi}) = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
records.statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For $X$ locally of finite type over $S$, $\delta_X(x)=\delta(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$; $\dim_\delta(W)$ is its value at the generic point of integral $W$.

$Z_k(X)$ is the group of locally finite integer combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$. The cycle $[Z]_k$ of a closed subscheme $Z$ of dimension at most $k$ sums its $k$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point stalk lengths; $[\mathcal F]_k$ uses lengths of a coherent sheaf at the corresponding generic points of its support.

For a proper map $f:X\to Y$, $f_*[W]=0$ if $\dim_\delta f(W)<\dim_\delta W$, otherwise it is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{f(W)})][f(W)]$. For flat $f$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback of $[W]$ is the cycle $[X\times_Y W]_{\dim_\delta W+r}$ of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with component multiplicities.

$\mathrm{CH}_k(X)=Z_k(X)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}$, where rational equivalence is generated by locally finite sums of principal divisors of nonzero rational functions on integral closed subschemes of dimension $k+1$, pushed into $X$. An envelope is a proper map $f:Y\to X$ such that every $x\in X$ has some $y$ above it with $\kappa(y)\simeq\kappa(x)$.

Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\xi \in Y$ be a point.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$, $Y$ are integral,
\item $Y$ is locally Noetherian
\item $f$ is proper, dominant and $R(Y) \subset R(X)$ is finite, and
\item $\dim(\mathcal{O}_{Y, \xi}) = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open neighbourhood $V \subset Y$ of $\xi$
such that $f|_{f^{-1}(V)} : f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.

conclusions: If $R$ is not Jacobson, there exist a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $f\in R$ such that $\mathfrak p$ is not maximal, $f\notin\mathfrak p$, $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\}$, and $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ is a field.
If $R$ is Jacobson, for every nonmaximal prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and every $f\notin\mathfrak p$, the set $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)$ is infinite.
hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring with identity.
records.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. If $R$ is not Jacobson there exist
a prime $\mathfrak p \subset R$, an element $f \in R$
such that the following hold
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathfrak p$ is not a maximal ideal,
\item $f \not \in \mathfrak p$,
\item $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f) = \{\mathfrak p\}$, and
\item $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ is a field.

Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an index category, i.e., a category. Assume
that for every pair of objects $x, y$ of $\mathcal{I}$
there exist an object $z$ and morphisms $x \to z$ and $y \to z$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $M$ and $N$ are diagrams of sets over $\mathcal{I}$,
then $\colim (M_i \times N_i) \to \colim M_i \times \colim N_i$
is surjective,
\item in general colimits of diagrams of sets over $\mathcal{I}$
do not commute with finite nonempty products.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Affineline special

conclusions: Gorenstein iff dualizing complex invertible, with local and open-locus claims and O_X normalization.
hypotheses: X locally Noetherian; dualizing D_X for part 1, X Gorenstein for part 2.
records.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. (1) If $D_X$ is any dualizing complex on $X$, then (a) $X$ is Gorenstein iff $D_X$ is derived-invertible on $X$; (b) for every $x\in X$, the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Gorenstein iff its derived stalk $(D_X)_x$ is an invertible object of $D(\mathcal O_{X,x})$; and (c) the locus of Gorenstein points is an open Gorenstein subscheme. (2) If $X$ is Gorenstein, then the existence of *some* dualizing complex on $X$ is equivalent to the structure complex $\mathcal O_X[0]$ itself being dualizing. The equivalences refer to derived-invertibility, not mere invertibility of a chosen cohomology sheaf unless the complex is concentrated in one degree.

records.statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. Now full compactness in unbounded D(O) follows because there is **one uniform finite cohomological-dimension bound d for the object U**, in addition to preservation of sums.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$ be an object of
$\mathcal{C}$. The $\mathcal{O}$-module $j_!\mathcal{O}_U$ is a
compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$ if there exists an integer $d$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > d$, and
\item the functors $\mathcal{F} \mapsto H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$
commute with direct sums.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Proposition — Locally quasi separated open dense scheme

conclusions: Four precise composition and descent implications for Gorenstein morphisms.
hypotheses: Three locally Noetherian fibre systems; additional flatness of f for converse directions.
records.statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be morphisms such that *all* fibres of $f,g,g\circ f$ are locally Noetherian. Then (1) if $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$, $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$; (2) if $f$ and $g$ are Gorenstein everywhere, then $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein; (3) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$, then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$; (4) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $f$ flat everywhere, then $f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $g$ is Gorenstein **at points in the image of $f$**, not necessarily outside that image.

records.title: Lemma — Base change representable

conclusions: The stated assignments define a functorial cosimplicial $(A/R)_\bullet$-module.
hypotheses: $R\to A$ is a commutative-ring map and $(N,\varphi)$ a module descent datum satisfying the cocycle identity.
records.statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. An $A$-module descent datum is an $A$-module $N$ together with an isomorphism of $A\otimes_R A$-modules $\varphi:N\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes_R N$ such that the two induced ways of transporting $N$ across three $A$-factors agree (the usual cocycle identity on $A\otimes_R A\otimes_R A$). Set $B_n=A^{\otimes_R(n+1)}$ for $n\geq0$. For $0\leq i\leq n$, define the $B_n$-module $N_{n,i}=A^{\otimes_R i}\otimes_R N\otimes_R A^{\otimes_R(n-i)}$ with $N$ in tensor position $i$. The descent isomorphism supplies compatible $B_n$-linear identifications $\varphi^n_{ij}:N_{n,i}\to N_{n,j}$ for $i\leq j$, and for an order-preserving map $\beta:[n]\to[m]$ there is a canonical $B_n\to B_m$-semilinear map $N_{\beta,n}:N_{n,n}\to N_{m,\beta(n)}$ sending $1\otimes\cdots\otimes n$ to the corresponding tensor in position $\beta(n)$. Define $N_n=N_{n,n}$ and
$$N_\bullet(\beta)=\varphi^m_{\beta(n),m}\circ N_{\beta,n}:N_n\to N_m.$$
Then $(N_n,N_\bullet(\beta))$ is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial $R$-algebra $B_\bullet$, and the construction is functorial in $(N,\varphi)$.

records.title: Lemma — Finite free open

conclusions: Derived duality preserves coherent complexes, swaps boundedness and yields biduality.
hypotheses: A Noetherian, ω dualizing, K coherent-derived.
records.statement:
For a Noetherian ring $A$, let $D_{\rm Coh}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full derived category of complexes with finitely generated cohomology in every degree. A *dualizing complex* $\omega_A^\bullet\in D(A)$ means a bounded complex with finite injective dimension and finitely generated cohomology such that the homothety map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\omega_A^\bullet,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. The functor $\mathbb D_A(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is contravariant. If $\omega_A^\bullet$ is dualizing, then $\mathbb D_A$ defines an exact anti-equivalence $D_{\rm Coh}(A)\to D_{\rm Coh}(A)$, interchanging the bounded-below and bounded-above subcategories and restricting to an anti-equivalence of the bounded coherent subcategory. The evaluation map
\[
K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega_A^\bullet),\omega_A^\bullet)
\]
is an isomorphism, natural in every $K\in D_{\rm Coh}(A)$, so $\mathbb D_A^2\simeq\mathrm{id}$.

hypotheses: f:Y→X quasi-finite between Noetherian schemes, with relative dualizing sheaf built from finite compactifications.
records.statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a quasi-finite morphism of Noetherian schemes. For an affine map of Noetherian rings $A\to B$ arising locally from $f$, define $\omega_{B/A}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,A)\otimes_EB$ using a finite $A$-algebra $E$ for which $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is an open immersion, and let $\omega_{Y/X}$ be the coherent sheaf formed by gluing these modules. The following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is a Gorenstein morphism; (2) $f$ is flat and every scheme-theoretic fibre is Gorenstein (equivalently, its local rings are Gorenstein); (3) $f$ is flat and $\omega_{Y/X}$ is an invertible sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules; (4) for every $y\in Y$ there are affine opens $y\in V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $f(V)\subseteq U$, such that $A\to B$ is flat and $\omega_{B/A}$ is invertible as a $B$-module. The invertibility requirement is that the relative dualizing module be locally free of rank one, not merely that it be flat.

records.title: Lemma — Base change envelope

conclusions: A locally separated algebraic space is decent.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

conclusions:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category with enough negative objects.
Let $f : X \to X'$ be a morphism of $D^b(\mathcal{A})$. Let $b \in \mathbf{Z}$
such that $H^i(X) = 0$ for $i > b$ and $H^i(X') = 0$ for $i \geq b$.
Then there exists a map $N[-b] \to X$ such that the induced map
$N \to H^b(X)$ is surjective, such that $\Hom(H^b(X), N) = 0$, and
such that the composition $N[-b] \to X \to X'$ is zero.
Besides surjecting on top H^b(X), the selected map from N[-b] becomes zero after composing to X', using that X' has no cohomology in degrees >=b. The negative-object condition is Hom(H^b(X),N)=0.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

hypotheses: For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

Given a commutative square of ring maps $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$ with maps $A\to A'$ and $B\to B'$, functoriality of the simplicial polynomial resolutions induces a canonical morphism $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\to L_{B'/A'}$ in $D(B')$. If the square is Tor-independent, meaning $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq B'$, this is the canonical base-change comparison.

For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

Given a commutative square of ring maps $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$ with maps $A\to A'$ and $B\to B'$, functoriality of the simplicial polynomial resolutions induces a canonical morphism $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\to L_{B'/A'}$ in $D(B')$. If the square is Tor-independent, meaning $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq B'$, this is the canonical base-change comparison.

Let $A\to B$ and $A'\to B'$ be a commutative square of ring maps. If the natural map from the derived tensor product is a quasi-isomorphism
$B \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} A' = B'$, then the functoriality map
induces an isomorphism
$$
L_{B/A} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} B' \longrightarrow L_{B'/A'}
$$

records.title: Lemma — Flat base change cotangent complex

conclusions:
for every \'etale morphism
$\varphi : U \to X$ from a scheme $U$ and any $u \in U$ with
$\varphi(u) = x$, exists a point $u'\in U$, $u' \leadsto u$ with
$\varphi(u') = x'$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

For $x\in|X|$ and an étale morphism $U\to X$, write $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ for a pointed étale neighborhood. It is *elementary* when $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is a monomorphism representing $x$. When $X$ is decent, such neighborhoods are cofiltered: they exist, any two have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized after refinement. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is the field of the unique representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, and the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}$ is the filtered colimit of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over elementary étale neighborhoods; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}^{h}$ for any elementary étale neighborhood.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

records.title: Lemma — Decent specialization

conclusions: Perfect φ with Tor-independent base-change gives φ^! comparison isomorphism for any K.
hypotheses:
Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a finite-type homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Define its *algebraic upper-shriek functor* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ by choosing a presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and putting
\[
\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n].
\]
For surjective $\varphi$, one may use $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$ with its natural $A$-action. Different polynomial presentations give isomorphic functors, but the isomorphisms are *not canonical*. Here $D^\pm$ means bounded below/above cohomology, $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}$ means coherent cohomology, and a *perfect* ring map is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension (equivalently $A$ is a perfect $P$-complex after a suitable finite polynomial presentation).

(More on Algebra, Definition

Let $\varphi' : R' \to A' = A \otimes_R R'$ be the map induced by $\varphi$.

(More on Algebra, Definition
the perfect-map condition stated above)

records.title: Lemma — Bc

conclusions:
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $k'$ splits $A$, and
\item there exists a finite central simple algebra $B$ similar to $A$
such that $k' \subset B$ and $[B : k] = [k' : k]^2$.
\end{enumerate}
Here, a field extension $k'/k$ splits $A$ if $A\otimes_k k'$ is a matrix algebra over $k'$, and two finite central simple $k$-algebras $A,B$ are similar if $\operatorname{Mat}_n(A)\cong\operatorname{Mat}_m(B)$ as $k$-algebras for some positive integers $n,m$.

Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$.
Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\operatorname{Spec}(k) \ar[rr] \ar[rd] & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
Assume that the image point $s \in S$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to S$ is
a closed point and that $\kappa(s) \subset k$ is algebraic.
Then the image $x$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ is a closed point of $|X|$.

Let $\tau \in \{fppf, syntomic, smooth, \mathrm{\acute etale}, Zariski\}$.
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$, or on
$S_\tau$ in case $\tau = \mathrm{\acute etale}$, and let
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a standard $\tau$-covering of this site.
Let $V = \coprod_{i \in I} U_i$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $V$ is an affine scheme,
\item $\mathcal{V} = \{V \to U\}$ is an fpqc covering
and also a $\tau$-covering unless $\tau = Zariski$,
\item the {\v C}ech complexes
$\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet (\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})$ and
$\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{F})$ agree.
\end{enumerate}
Finite disjoint unions of affine sources V are affine. The singleton V→U is fpqc; it is also τ-cover for τ≠Zariski, while in the **Zariski** case it generally is not a covering in that site. The natural refinement map of Čech complexes is a **degreewise isomorphism for sheaves** because F preserves disjoint coproducts as products. Never extend this claim to arbitrary presheaves.

conclusions: Finite generation, finite presentation, flatness, faithful flatness, and finite projectivity descend and ascend along $f$.

records.statement: A homomorphism $f:R\to S$ of commutative rings is universally injective (or pure as an $R$-module map) if, for every $R$-module $T$, the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_R S$ is injective. For each one of the following properties, $M$ has the property over $R$ if and only if $M\otimes_RS$ has it over $S$: (a) finitely generated; (b) finitely presented; (c) flat; (d) faithfully flat; (e) finite projective (finitely generated projective). The same pure ring map $f$ is used in each assertion.

}

be a commutative diagram.

then the diagram is cartesian and $h$ is a monomorphism.

conclusions:

records.title: Lemma — Godement resolution

conclusions: For any two étale neighbourhoods (U_i,u_i) of (S,s), i=1,2, there is an étale neighbourhood (U,u) with morphisms to both.
If h_1,h_2: (U,u) → (U′,u′) are morphisms of étale neighbourhoods inducing the same map κ(u′) → κ(u), then some morphism h: (U″,u″) → (U,u) of étale neighbourhoods satisfies h_1 ∘ h = h_2 ∘ h.
hypotheses: Let S be a scheme and s ∈ S.
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $s$ be a point of $S$.
The category of \'etale neighborhoods has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(U_i, u_i)_{i=1, 2}$ be two \'etale neighborhoods of
$s$ in $S$. Then there exists a third \'etale neighborhood
$(U, u)$ and morphisms
$(U, u) \to (U_i, u_i)$, $i = 1, 2$.
\item Let $h_1, h_2: (U, u) \to (U', u')$ be two
morphisms between \'etale neighborhoods of $s$.
Assume $h_1$, $h_2$ induce the same map $\kappa(u') \to \kappa(u)$ of residue
fields. Then there exist an \'etale neighborhood $(U'', u'')$ and a morphism
$h : (U'', u'') \to (U, u)$
which equalizes $h_1$ and $h_2$, i.e., such that
$h_1 \circ h = h_2 \circ h$.
\end{enumerate}

The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. For a morphism $g:T\to S$ denote the restriction of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ under $g$ by $g_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$.

For $f:T\to S$, $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on the *small* $\tau$-site $T_\tau$, and $\Gamma(T_\tau,-)$ denotes global sections over its final object $T$. An **fpqc cover** means a flat jointly surjective family with the finite affine-source cover condition over each affine open.

conclusions:
We have the following implications
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is a regular sequence $\Rightarrow$
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is a Koszul-regular sequence $\Rightarrow$
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is an $H_1$-regular sequence $\Rightarrow$

records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X$ be a ringed space.
Let $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$.
We have the following implications
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is a regular sequence $\Rightarrow$
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is a Koszul-regular sequence $\Rightarrow$
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is an $H_1$-regular sequence $\Rightarrow$
$f_1, \ldots, f_r$ is a quasi-regular sequence.

records.title: Lemma — Projection formula

conclusions: Canonical module support is maximal-dimensional components and satisfies S2.
hypotheses: Normalized Noetherian local A, d=dim A, ω_A=H^{-d} dualizing.
records.statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring, with a *normalized* dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$: this is a dualizing complex satisfying $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa,\omega_A^\bullet)\simeq\kappa[0]$. For an $A$-module $M$ put $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(M,\omega_A^\bullet)=H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,\omega_A^\bullet))$. Let $d=\dim A$ and define the *dualizing module* (canonical module of $A$) by $\omega_A=H^{-d}(\omega_A^\bullet)$, a finite $A$-module. Then (1) $\operatorname{Supp}_A(\omega_A)$ is exactly the union of irreducible components $V(\mathfrak p)$ with $\mathfrak p$ minimal and $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=d$; and (2) $\omega_A$ satisfies Serre condition $(S_2)$ as a module: for every $\mathfrak p$, $\operatorname{depth}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}(\omega_A)_{\mathfrak p}\ge\min\{2,\dim\operatorname{Supp}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}(\omega_A)_{\mathfrak p}\}$. This is a module statement even if $A$ is not Cohen–Macaulay.

conclusions: For $X\subset A$ filtered by induced filtration and $A/X$ by quotient filtration, the associated-graded sequence is short exact in every degree.
For a filtered map $f:A\to B$, both graded short exact sequences involving $\ker f$, $\operatorname{coim}f$, $\operatorname{im}f$, and $\operatorname{coker}f$ in the source are exact.
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A$ be abelian.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $A$ be a filtered object and $X \subset A$. Then for each $p$
the sequence
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(X) \to \text{gr}^p(A) \to \text{gr}^p(A/X) \to 0
$$
is exact (with induced filtration on $X$ and quotient filtration on $A/X$).
\item Let $f : A \to B$ be a morphism of filtered objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
Then for each $p$ the sequences
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(\Ker(f)) \to \text{gr}^p(A) \to
\text{gr}^p(\Coim(f)) \to 0
$$
and
$$
0 \to \text{gr}^p(\Im(f)) \to \text{gr}^p(B) \to
\text{gr}^p(\Coker(f)) \to 0
$$
are exact.
\end{enumerate}
