conclusions: a_f preserves supports and localizes on arbitrary opens.
hypotheses: f perfect proper Noetherian; T closed and V open.
records.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. A complex in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ is *supported on* a closed subset $T$ if every cohomology sheaf is zero on $Y\setminus T$. If $V\subseteq Y$ is open, $U=f^{-1}(V)$, and $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $j':U\hookrightarrow X$, the *restriction comparison* is the natural map $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_{f|_U}(j^*K)$. Then (1) for every closed $T\subseteq Y$, any $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ supported on $T$ has $a_f(Q)$ supported on $f^{-1}(T)$; and (2) for every open $V\subseteq Y$ and every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the natural restriction map $\rho_K:a_f(K)|_{f^{-1}(V)}\to a_{f|_{f^{-1}(V)}}(K|_V)$ is an isomorphism, understood locally on the open $V$ when it is not quasi-compact.

Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent sheaf on $X$.
The set of coherent subsheaves
$$
\{
\mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{F}
\mid
\text{Supp}(\mathcal{K})\text{ is nowhere dense in }\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})
\}
$$
has a maximal element $\mathcal{K}$.
Setting $\mathcal{F}' = \mathcal{F}/\mathcal{K}$ we have the
following
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}') = \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$,
\item $\mathcal{F}'$ has no embedded associated points, and
\item there exists a dense open $U \subset X$ such that
$U \cap \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ is dense in $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$
and $\mathcal{F}'|_U \cong \mathcal{F}|_U$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: Listed closure properties for sums, colimits, kernels/cokernels, extensions, tensor products and finite-presentation internal Hom.
hypotheses: Quasi-coherent modules on the small étale ringed site of a scheme.
records.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $\operatorname{QCoh}(S_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\mathcal O)$ denote quasi-coherent modules on its small étale ringed site. This category has the following closure properties (where exactness, colimits and internal Hom are taken in the ambient category of site modules): (1) arbitrary direct sums and (2) arbitrary colimits are quasi-coherent; (3) kernels and cokernels of morphisms between quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; (4) in a short exact sequence of site modules, if any two of the three terms are quasi-coherent, so is the third; (5) tensor products of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; (6) if $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are quasi-coherent and $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation, then $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is quasi-coherent.

conclusions: CM at x iff relative upper-shriek structure complex locally has only one nonzero cohomology sheaf.
hypotheses: f flat separated finite-type between S-schemes and point x.
records.statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and the category $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. For $f:X\to Y$ therein, let $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ be the upper-shriek functor built from the right adjoint to proper pushforward on a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to Y$. In particular $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is a coherent bounded complex when $f$ is perfect. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, and $x\in X$. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) the fibre-local ring $\mathcal O_{X_{f(x)},x}$ is Cohen–Macaulay; (2) there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $f^!\mathcal O_Y|_U$ is quasi-isomorphic to a *single* coherent cohomology sheaf placed in one cohomological degree (the degree may depend on $U$). In particular this is a neighbourhood statement about the relative dualizing complex, not just its single stalk.

conclusions: The functor $\mathcal F^\bullet\mapsto\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal F^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ on $K(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ takes every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism.

For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is **K-flat** if for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules the total tensor complex $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic (definition at sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). \longmapsto
\text{Tot}(\mathcal{F}^\bullet \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{K}^\bullet)

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I$.
Write $S = \Spec(A)$ and $S_n = \Spec(A/I^n)$.
Let $X \to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type.
For $n \geq 1$ we set $X_n = X \times_S S_n$.
Suppose given a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Z_1 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z_2 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z_3 \ar[r] \ar[d] & \ldots \\
X_1 \ar[r]^{i_1} & X_2 \ar[r]^{i_2} & X_3 \ar[r] & \ldots
}
$$
of schemes with cartesian squares. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z_1 \to X_1$ is a closed immersion, and
\item $Z_1 \to S_1$ is proper.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a closed immersion of schemes $Z \to X$ such that
$Z_n = Z \times_S S_n$. Moreover, $Z$ is proper over $S$.

Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $\overline{s}$ be a geometric point of $S$.
The category of \'etale neighborhoods is cofiltered. More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(U_i, \overline{u}_i)_{i = 1, 2}$ be two \'etale neighborhoods of
$\overline{s}$ in $S$. Then there exists a third \'etale neighborhood
$(U, \overline{u})$ and morphisms
$(U, \overline{u}) \to (U_i, \overline{u}_i)$, $i = 1, 2$.
\item Let $h_1, h_2: (U, \overline{u}) \to (U', \overline{u}')$ be two
morphisms between \'etale neighborhoods of $\overline{s}$. Then there exist an
\'etale neighborhood $(U'', \overline{u}'')$ and a morphism
$h : (U'', \overline{u}'') \to (U, \overline{u})$
which equalizes $h_1$ and $h_2$, i.e., such that
$h_1 \circ h = h_2 \circ h$.
\end{enumerate}
Cofiltered means any pair of lifted étale neighbourhoods has a common *refinement*, and any two parallel morphisms are made equal after a further refinement. The fibre-product/étale diagonal construction uses the chosen geometric lifts.

records.title: Lemma — Hom from tensor product

conclusions: $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 6}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.
hypotheses: For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, the standing Cohen–Macaulay curve hypotheses imply $X$ is connected, Cohen–Macaulay and purely one-dimensional. Let $\omega_X$ be its coherent dualizing module, equal to $H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for the structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. A regular global section of an invertible sheaf is one whose multiplication map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is injective; an ample invertible sheaf is very ample if its global sections define a closed immersion into projective space.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ has a regular global section,
\item $H^1(X, \mathcal{L}) = 0$, and
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is ample.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 6}$ is very ample on $X$ over $k$.

records.title: Lemma — Conormal effective Cartier divisor

conclusions:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \mathrm{\acute etale}\}$. Consider the morphism
$$
\pi_S : (\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau \longrightarrow S_\tau
$$
of Topologies, Lemma \ref{topologies-lemma-at-the-bottom} or
\ref{topologies-lemma-at-the-bottom-etale}. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on
$S_\tau$. Then $\pi_S^{-1}\mathcal{F}$ is given by the rule
$$
(\pi_S^{-1}\mathcal{F})(T) = \Gamma(T_\tau, f_{small}^{-1}\mathcal{F})
$$
where $f : T \to S$. Moreover, $\pi_S^{-1}\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the
sheaf condition with respect to fpqc coverings.
For τ=Zariski or étale, the site morphism π_S is from the **big to small** τ-site; the inverse-image sheaf on a big-site object T is computed by *global sections of a small-site inverse-image sheaf on T*. The resulting presheaf satisfies even **fpqc descent**, a condition stronger than τ-sheafhood.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the induced **morphism of small étale topoi** $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute etale})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute etale})$ has inverse image $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$); it sends **sheaves of sets** on $Y_{\acute etale}$ to sheaves on $X_{\acute etale}$, and also induces inverse image of abelian sheaves. It is different from the **ringed-site module pullback** $f^*$, which additionally tensors by the target structure sheaf. For an étale $V\to Y$, let $h_V$ be its representable sheaf and $X\times_Y V$ the fibre product, an object of $X_{\acute etale}$. For a morphism $g:T\to S$ denote the restriction of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ under $g$ by $g_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$.

For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale\}$ let $\pi_S:(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau\to S_\tau$ be the canonical morphism of the **big** to the **small** site; its inverse image $\pi_S^{-1}$ takes small-site sheaves to big-site sheaves. For $f:T\to S$, $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on the *small* $\tau$-site $T_\tau$, and $\Gamma(T_\tau,-)$ denotes global sections over its final object $T$. An **fpqc cover** means a flat jointly surjective family with the finite affine-source cover condition over each affine open.

records.title: Lemma — Describe pullback

conclusions:
$f = s/s'$
is an element of $R(X)^*$ and we have
$$
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s)[Z]
=
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s')[Z]
+
\text{div}(f)
$$
as Weil divisors.
hypotheses:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s, s' \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be nonzero
meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{L}$.
records.statement:
For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s, s' \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be nonzero
meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{L}$. Then $f = s/s'$
is an element of $R(X)^*$ and we have
$$
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s)[Z]
=
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s')[Z]
+
\text{div}(f)
$$
as Weil divisors.

records.title: Lemma — Finite residue extension closed

conclusions: There exists i\ge 0 such that f_i:X_i\to Y_i is affine.
hypotheses: I is a directed indexing set, 0\in I, and (S_i)_{i\in I} is an inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms.
S=\varprojlim_{i\in I}S_i.
f_0:X_0\to Y_0 is a morphism of schemes over S_0.
S_0, X_0, Y_0 are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
For every i\ge 0, f_i:X_i\to Y_i is obtained from f_0 by base change along S_i\to S_0.
f:X\to Y is the corresponding base change of f_0 along S\to S_0.
f:X\to Y is affine.
records.statement: Let \((S_i)_{i\in I}\) be a directed inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms and limit \(S=\varprojlim_i S_i\). Fix \(0\in I\) and a morphism of \(S_0\)-schemes \(f_0:X_0\to Y_0\) with \(S_0,X_0,Y_0\) quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For each \(i\ge 0\), let \(f_i:X_i\to Y_i\) be the base change of \(f_0\) to \(S_i\), and let \(f:X\to Y\) be its base change to \(S\). If \(f\) is affine, then there exists \(i\ge 0\) such that \(f_i\) is affine.

records.title: Lemma — Finite type nagata

conclusions:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $K/k$ a field extension
of transcendence degree 1. Then for all $q \geq 1$,
$H_\etale^q(\Spec(K), \mathbf{G}_m) = 0$.
The claim is interpreted using the preceding explicit definitions; retain exactly the original assumptions and conclusion in group cohomology, Brauer groups, and $C_r$ field theory.
hypotheses: Let $K$ be a field with separable closure $K^{sep}$ and absolute Galois group $G_K$. For a maximal pro-$\ell$ subgroup $H\subseteq G_K$, its fixed field is $L=(K^{sep})^H$, so $\operatorname{Gal}(K^{sep}/L)=H$; $\ell$-*primary torsion étale sheaves* on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ are discrete continuous $G_K$-modules killed elementwise by some power of $\ell$. Their cohomology agrees with continuous Galois cohomology. The *Brauer group* $\operatorname{Br}(K)$ consists of Morita classes of finite-dimensional central simple $K$-algebras. A field $K$ is **$C_r$** if, for every positive integer degree $d$ and number of variables $n>d^r$, every homogeneous degree-$d$ polynomial over $K$ in $n$ variables has a **nonzero common solution** (for one polynomial). A *variety over $k$* in this source means a **separated integral scheme of finite type** over $k$, and its function field is the local ring at the generic point.

records.title: Lemma — Relative proj finite type

conclusions: If S is a domain finite-dimensional over k, then S is a field.
If S is a domain integral over k, then S is a field.
If S is integral over k, every prime ideal of S is maximal.
hypotheses: k is a field.
S is a k-algebra.
records.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $S$ be a $k$-algebra over $k$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $S$ is a domain and finite dimensional over $k$,
then $S$ is a field.
\item If $S$ is integral over $k$ and a domain,
then $S$ is a field.
\item If $S$ is integral over $k$ then every prime of
$S$ is a maximal ideal (see
Lemma \ref{lemma-ring-with-only-minimal-primes}
for more consequences).
\end{enumerate}

records.statement: Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Let $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$, and assume the Noetherian local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is Cohen–Macaulay (its depth equals its Krull dimension). Suppose for every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of $X$ containing $x$, the residue extension satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(\xi))}\kappa(\xi)\le r$ for some integer $r\ge0$. Then $H^i(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x\ne0$ implies $i\ge-r$. Moreover the finitely generated $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x$ satisfies Serre's condition $(S_2)$: for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, its localization has depth at least $\min\{2,\dim\operatorname{Supp}(H^{-r}(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x)_{\mathfrak p}\}$, with the usual convention for zero modules.

For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. conclusions:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Denote

\Sh(Y_\etale)$
the associated morphism of small \'etale topoi. Assume at least one

\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is integral, or
\item $f$ is separated and locally quasi-finite.
\end{enumerate}
Then the functor
$f_{small, *} :
\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)
\to
\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)$
has the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item the map
$f_{small}^{-1}f_{small, *}\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$
is always surjective,
\item $f_{small, *}$ is faithful, and
\item $f_{small, *}$ reflects injections and surjections.
\end{enumerate}
The two hypotheses are alternatives: **integral** or **separated locally quasi-finite**. The assertions concern the **small-site abelian-sheaf** direct image, its counit, and reflection of both mono and epi.

Let $X_{\acute et}$ and $Y_{\acute et}$ denote the **small étale sites** of schemes $X$ and $Y$, and let $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})$ be the corresponding topoi of sheaves of sets, with structure sheaves of local rings $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Y$ on these sites. A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces a geometric morphism $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute et})$ with inverse-image functor $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to direct image $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$) and a ring map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^\sharp:f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$. A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

For any scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, define the following exact **three source properties** of its small étale-site pullback functor $V/Y\mapsto X\times_YV$: **(A)** for each étale $U\to X$ and $u\in U$, some étale $V\to Y$ admits a decomposition $X\times_YV=W\amalg W'$ and an $X$-morphism $W\to U$ whose image contains $u$; **(B)** for each étale $V\to Y$ and étale cover $\{U_i\to X\times_YV\}$, some étale cover $\{V_j\to V\}$ admits a decomposition $X\times_YV_j=\coprod_i W_{ij}$ for every $j$, with each $W_{ij}\to X\times_YV$ factoring through the relevant $U_i$; **(C)** for every étale $U\to X$, some étale $V\to Y$ admits a *surjective $X$-morphism* $X\times_YV\to U$. A functor *reflects* monomorphisms/epimorphisms if whenever the image map is mono/epi, so was the original.

records.title: Lemma — Flat over thickening

conclusions:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ which
is regular. Let $x \in X$ be a closed point and denote $\mathcal{O}_x$
the skyscraper sheaf at $x$ with value $\kappa(x)$. Let $K$ in
$D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\Ext^i_X(\mathcal{O}_x, K) = 0$ then there exists an open
neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $H^{i - d_x}(K)|_U = 0$ where
$d_x = \dim(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$.
\item If $\Hom_X(\mathcal{O}_x, K[i]) = 0$ for all
$i \in \mathbf{Z}$, then $K$ is zero in an open neighbourhood of $x$.
\item If $\Ext^i_X(K, \mathcal{O}_x) = 0$ then there exists an open
neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $H^i(K^\vee)|_U = 0$.
\item If $\Hom_X(K, \mathcal{O}_x[i]) = 0$ for all
$i \in \mathbf{Z}$, then $K$ is zero in an open neighbourhood of $x$.
\item If $H^i(X, K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_x) = 0$
then there exists an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that
$H^i(K)|_U = 0$.
\item If $H^i(X, K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}_x) = 0$
for $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ then $K$ is zero in an
open neighbourhood of $x$.
\end{enumerate}
Each clause has its own vanishing hypothesis: individual Ext^i gives a single nearby cohomology sheaf vanishing, while all shifts give complete vanishing near x; the two Hom directions correspond to K and K^vee respectively.

records.title: Lemma — Bourbaki finite type general base at point

conclusions:
Let $(R, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local ring. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R$ is henselian,
\item for any $f\in R[T]$ and any factorization $\bar f = g_0 h_0$ in
$\kappa[T]$ with $\gcd(g_0, h_0)=1$, there exists a factorization $f = gh$ in
$R[T]$ with $\bar g = g_0$ and $\bar h = h_0$,
\item any finite $R$-algebra $S$ is isomorphic to a finite product of
local rings finite over $R$,
\item any finite type $R$-algebra $A$ is isomorphic to a product
$A \cong A' \times C$ where $A' \cong A_1 \times \ldots \times A_r$
is a product of finite local $R$-algebras and all the irreducible
components of $C \otimes_R \kappa$ have dimension at least 1,
\item if $A$ is an \'etale $R$-algebra and $\mathfrak n$ is a maximal ideal of
$A$ lying over $\mathfrak m$ such that $\kappa \cong A/\mathfrak n$, then there
exists an isomorphism $\varphi : A \cong R \times A'$ such that
$\varphi(\mathfrak n) = \mathfrak m \times A' \subset R \times A'$.
\end{enumerate}
All five equivalent conditions apply to the **same arbitrary local ring** (not necessarily Noetherian). The finite algebra condition includes decomposition into *local* finite R-algebras; the condition for étale A includes a specified maximal ideal n over m with κ≅A/n. The polynomial factorization hypothesis is exactly as stated in source, including coprimality in κ[T].

records.statement:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is locally of finite presentation,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation, and
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is flat at $x$ over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a commutative diagram of pointed schemes
$$
\xymatrix{
(X, x) \ar[d] & (X', x') \ar[l]^g \ar[d] \\
(S, s) & (S', s') \ar[l]
}
$$
whose horizontal arrows are elementary \'etale neighbourhoods
such that $X'$, $S'$ are affine and such that
$\Gamma(X', g^*\mathcal{F})$ is a projective
$\Gamma(S', \mathcal{O}_{S'})$-module.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.
records.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ having dimension $1$
and $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = k$. Assume the singularities of $X$ are
at-worst-nodal. Let $C \subset X$ be a rational tail
(with rational tail as explicitly defined above).
For any field extension $K/k$ the base change $C_K \subset X_K$
is a finite disjoint union of rational tails.

$L \in D(\mathcal{O}_f)$ we have
$$
R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(L, K) =
R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_f}(L, R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{O}_f, K))
$$
In particular
$R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{O}_f,
R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{O}_f, K)) =
R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{O}_f, K)$.
\item If $g$ is a second global
section of $\mathcal{O}$, then
$$
R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{O}_f, R\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{O}_g, K))

$$
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

records.title: Lemma — Eventually separated

conclusions: The Hodge-level Gysin maps induced by local cohomology commute with exterior differentiation.
hypotheses: $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a Koszul-regular finitely presented closed immersion of codimension $c$.
records.statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.
Assume further that $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is Koszul regular. Then $\mathcal H^j_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})=0$ for $j<c$, and the local-cohomology Gysin morphism induces maps
$$\gamma^{p,q}:H^q(Z,\Omega^p_{Z/S})\longrightarrow H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S}).$$
These are compatible with the maps induced by the de Rham differential: for each $p,q$, $d\circ\gamma^{p,q}=\gamma^{p+1,q}\circ d$ (the target in the first composite has differential form degree $p+c+1$).

records.title: Lemma — Locally projective

conclusions:
$\Spec(k) \to X$ is a finite morphism. If $\kappa(s) = k$
then $\Spec(k) \to X$ is a closed immersion.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $S$.
Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\operatorname{Spec}(k) \ar[rr] \ar[rd] & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
Assume that the image point $s \in S$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to S$ is
a closed point and that the field extension $k/\kappa(s)$ is finite.
Then $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ is a finite morphism. If $\kappa(s) = k$
then $\operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ is a closed immersion.

conclusions: Refinement pullback on descent-data categories is fully faithful.
hypotheses: Each fibre of the index map alpha gives an fpqc cover of the corresponding V_j.
records.statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Assume for each $j\in J$ the subfamily $\{g_i:U_i\to V_j\mid\alpha(i)=j\}$ is an fpqc covering of $V_j$. Then the induced pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is fully faithful. The underlying morphism of disjoint unions $\coprod_iU_i\to\coprod_jV_j$ is an fpqc covering, and the family-to-coproduct equivalence identifies the indicated pullback with pullback along that morphism.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

Let $X$ be locally
of finite type over $S$. Let $\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2$
be finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Then we have the equality
$$
ch(\mathcal{E}_1 \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{E}_2) =
ch(\mathcal{E}_1) ch(\mathcal{E}_2)
$$
More precisely, we have
$$
P_p(\mathcal{E}_1 \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{E}_2) =
\sum\nolimits_{p_1 + p_2 = p}
{p \choose p_1} P_{p_1}(\mathcal{E}_1) P_{p_2}(\mathcal{E}_2)
$$
in $A^p(X)$ where $P_p(\mathcal E)$ is the $p$th power sum of the formal Chern roots of $\mathcal E$.

records.statement:
For any ringed site (C,O), a **strictly perfect complex** E^bullet is a **bounded** complex whose every term is a direct summand of a finite free O-module (source Definition strictly-perfect at 11716–11724). For U∈C a strictly perfect complex on (C/U,O_U) uses the restricted ring; a finite locally projective module is not being assumed globally free. The two alternatives are **independent**: (1) the target complex F^bullet is acyclic; (2) E^j=0 for j<a and H^j(F^bullet)=0 for j≥a. Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$ be an object
of $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\alpha : \mathcal{E}^\bullet \to \mathcal{F}^\bullet$
be a morphism of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules
with $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ strictly perfect and $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$
acyclic. Then there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that each
$\alpha|_{U_i}$ is homotopic to zero.
\item Let $\alpha : \mathcal{E}^\bullet \to \mathcal{F}^\bullet$
be a morphism of complexes of $\mathcal{O}_U$-modules
with $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ strictly perfect, $\mathcal{E}^i = 0$
for $i < a$, and $H^i(\mathcal{F}^\bullet) = 0$ for $i \geq a$.
Then there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ such that each
$\alpha|_{U_i}$ is homotopic to zero.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $i : Z \to X$ be a Koszul regular closed immersion.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a Koszul regular closed immersion.
Then there exists a surjective smooth morphism $X' \to X$ such
that the base change $i' : Z \times_X X' \to X'$ of $i$ is
a regular immersion.

Let $R$ be a ring. Assume $R$ is reduced and has finitely many
minimal primes. Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

\item The support of $\sigma$ is closed in $U$.

abelian sheaves on $S_\mathrm{\acute etale}$, then the support of $\varphi(\sigma)$

of $\mathcal{G}$ is a subset of the support of $\mathcal{F}$.
\item If $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ is injective then the support
of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subset of the support of $\mathcal{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Proposition — Enough acyclics

conclusions:
Let $\varphi : A \to B$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ is syntomic and induces a surjective map on spectra, or
\item $A \to B$ is a faithfully flat local complete intersection, or
\item $A \to B$ is faithfully flat of finite type with Gorenstein fibres.
\end{enumerate}
Then $K \in D(A)$ is a dualizing complex for $A$ if and only if
$K \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} B$ is a dualizing complex for $B$.
Syntomic means flat, finitely presented and locally complete intersection. The three alternatives all include faithful flatness and ensure that the relative shriek complex is invertible; ascension and descension are separate implications.
hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ be finite type over Noetherian rings. Its *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{A/R}^{\bullet}$ is $\varphi^!(R)$, again up to nonunique isomorphism. A *perfect map* is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension; finite-type flat maps are perfect.

records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd]_j \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume $X \to S$ smooth and $i$ and $j$ immersions.
If $i$ is a Koszul-regular (resp.\ $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular)
immersion, then so is $j$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

records.title: Lemma — Locally Japanese

conclusions: Unique pro extension of morphisms, existence of systems, and uniqueness up to pro-isomorphism.
hypotheses: Noetherian open immersion, Deligne systems, bounded coherent derived restrictions.
records.statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ of Noetherian schemes: (1) if $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ are Deligne systems with constant restriction values $K,L$ on $U$, any morphism $\alpha:K\to L$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ extends to a **unique morphism of pro-objects** $(K_n)\to(L_n)$ that restricts to $\alpha$ (not necessarily a levelwise map with matching indices); (2) every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ occurs as the common restriction value of some Deligne system on $X$; and (3) such a pro-object is unique up to the unique pro-isomorphism inducing the identity on $K$. Thus $K\mapsto(K_n)$ defines the coherent pro-extension functor $Rj_!$.

hypotheses: For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For ring maps $A\to B\to C$, the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes is the canonical distinguished triangle in $D(C)$: $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C\to L_{C/A}\to L_{C/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}C)[1]$. A distinguished triangle is a triangle isomorphic to the one associated to a mapping cone of a morphism in a derived category.

Let $R \to S$ be a ring map.

object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we have
$\text{cosk}_m \text{sk}_m \text{cosk}_n U = \text{cosk}_n U$.

the canonical map
$U \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_nU$
is an isomorphism for some $n \geq 0$, then the canonical map
$U \to \text{cosk}_m \text{sk}_mU$
is an isomorphism for all $m \geq n$.

conclusions: $L_{B/A}$ is zero in $D(B)$.
hypotheses: For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For a characteristic-$p$ ring $A$ ($p$ prime), the Frobenius endomorphism is $F_A(a)=a^p$. Given a characteristic-$p$ ring map $A\to B$, its Frobenius square $(F_A,F_B)$ induces maps on the functorial simplicial standard resolution $P_\bullet$ and the cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$; these maps are generally semilinear over $B$ under $F_B$. A homotopy of simplicial maps means simplicial homotopy, and a chain homotopy on a complex induces the same map in its derived category.

conclusions: The inverse system $M_n=H^p(\mathcal C,\mathcal F_n)$ satisfies the Mittag–Leffler condition (indeed eventual stable images admit a uniform shift as in the source footnote).
hypotheses: $A$ is a ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $\mathcal C$ a site.
$(\mathcal F_n)$ is an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules with $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F_{n+1}/I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$ for each $n$.
$p\ge0$ and $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{p+1}(\mathcal C,I^n\mathcal F_{n+1})$ satisfies the graded ascending chain condition as a module over $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n/I^{n+1}$.
records.statement:
An inverse system $(M_n)$ satisfies the Mittag–Leffler condition when, for every fixed $n$, the images of the transition maps $M_m\to M_n$ stabilize for all sufficiently large $m$. The graded ring $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ is the associated graded ring of the $I$-adic filtration. For a site $\mathcal C$ and ring $A$ with ideal $I$, an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules $\cdots\to\mathcal F_3\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_1$ is assumed to have $\mathcal F_n\cong\mathcal F_{n+1}/I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$. The graded module is built from **degree $p+1$** cohomology of the submodules $I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$.

Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules on $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
Let $p \geq 0$. Assume
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{n \geq 0} H^{p + 1}(\mathcal{C}, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})
$$
satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded
$\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$-module.
Then the inverse system $M_n = H^p(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_n)$ satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition\footnote{In fact, there exists
a $c \geq 0$ such that $\Im(M_n \to M_{n - c})$ is the stable image
for all $n \geq c$.}.

records.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $S \to S'$ be a flat map of $R$-algebras.
Let $M$ be a module over $S$, and set $M' = S' \otimes_S M$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $M$ is flat over $R$, then $M'$ is flat over $R$.
\item If $S \to S'$ is faithfully flat, then $M$ is flat
over $R$ if and only if $M'$ is flat over $R$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Quasi excellent nagata

conclusions: Depth agrees with first nonzero Ext and local cohomology, with Ext-vanishing below depth.
hypotheses: A Noetherian, I ideal, M finite and IM≠M; N finite I-power torsion for last part.
records.statement:
For a Noetherian ring $A$, ideal $I$ and finitely generated $A$-module $M$, define $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ to be the maximal length of an $M$-regular sequence of elements of $I$ (and $\infty$ by convention if $IM=M$). A sequence $(x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ is $M$-regular if each $x_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1})M$ and the final quotient is nonzero. Assume $IM\ne M$, so $\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$ is finite. Then the following three integers are equal:
\[
\operatorname{depth}_I(M)
=\min\{i\ge0:\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(A/I,M)\ne0\}
=\min\{i\ge0:H_I^i(M)\ne0\},
\]
where $H_I^i(M)$ is the cohomology of the derived $I$-power-torsion functor (equivalently Čech local cohomology since $A$ is Noetherian). Moreover if $N$ is any finite module with $I^nN=0$ for some $n$, then $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(N,M)=0$ for every $i<\operatorname{depth}_I(M)$.

records.title: Lemma — Derived pushforward composition

conclusions: $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $a : F \to G$ and $b : G \to H$ be
transformations of functors $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta : G \to G \times_H G$ is representable
by algebraic spaces, and
\item $b \circ a : F \to H$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}
records.statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $a : F \to G$ and $b : G \to H$ be
transformations of functors $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta : G \to G \times_H G$ is representable
by algebraic spaces, and
\item $b \circ a : F \to H$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}
Then $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

records.title: Lemma — Representable by spaces permanence

conclusions:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a
Noetherian ring. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a constructible sheaf of sets, abelian
groups, or $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$. Let
$\mathcal{G} = \colim \mathcal{G}_i$ be a filtered colimit of sheaves of
sets, abelian groups, or $\Lambda$-modules. Then
$$
\Mor(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) = \colim \Mor(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}_i)
$$
in the category of sheaves of sets, abelian groups, or $\Lambda$-modules on
$X_\etale$.
The property is *finitely presented with respect to **filtered colimits** in the appropriate sheaf category*; it is not compactness in the unbounded derived category.
hypotheses: On the small étale site $X_{\acute et}$ of a **qcqs scheme**, a sheaf of sets or abelian groups is *constructible* when its restriction to a finite constructible partition is **finite locally constant**; for modules over a **Noetherian** ring $\Lambda$, constructible means *finite type* locally constant on every stratum. For an étale object $j_U:U\to X$, $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$ is the representable sheaf, and $j_{U!}\underline M$ is **extension by zero** of the constant abelian or $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $U$, left adjoint to $j_U^{-1}$. A *torsion abelian sheaf* has torsion stalks at every geometric point. A *filtered colimit* of sheaves is taken in the sheaf category (sheafification of the sectionwise colimit). A constructible sheaf is *finitely presented/compact for filtered colimits* if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\operatorname*{colim}_i\mathcal G_i)\cong\operatorname*{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G_i)$ for every filtered system. *Essentially constant* for an ind-object means isomorphic in its ind-category to a constant ind-object. For a directed inverse system with affine transitions, its category-colimit means objects and morphisms descend from sufficiently large finite stages, **up to category equivalence**.

records.title: Proposition — Loc cst torsion

conclusions:
for every morphism of schemes $g : S' \to S$ the base change
$Z' = S' \times_S Z \to X' = S' \times_S X$
is an $H_1$-regular (resp.\ quasi-regular) immersion.
hypotheses:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $i : Z \subset X$ be an immersion.
Assume
$i$ is an $H_1$-regular (resp.\ quasi-regular) immersion, and
$Z \to S$ is a flat morphism.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $i : Z \subset X$ be an immersion.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $i$ is an $H_1$-regular (resp.\ quasi-regular) immersion, and
\item $Z \to S$ is a flat morphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then for every morphism of schemes $g : S' \to S$ the base change
$Z' = S' \times_S Z \to X' = S' \times_S X$
is an $H_1$-regular (resp.\ quasi-regular) immersion.

records.title: Lemma — Finite locally free

conclusions: a_f preserves arbitrary direct sums.
hypotheses: f proper flat finite presentation over qcqs Y; a_f right adjoint.
records.statement: Let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to Y$ proper, flat, and of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded derived categories with quasi-coherent cohomology, and define the *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{X/Y}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. For every family $(K_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ of objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the canonical map $\bigoplus_\lambda a_f(K_\lambda)\to a_f(\bigoplus_\lambda K_\lambda)$ is an isomorphism. Thus the right adjoint to the derived pushforward preserves arbitrary coproducts, not merely finite sums.

records.title: Lemma — Stalk exact

conclusions:
There exists a simplicial $A$-algebra $P_\bullet$ with an augmentation
$\epsilon : P_\bullet \to B$ such that each $P_n$ is a polynomial algebra
of finite type over $A$ and such that $\epsilon$ is a trivial
Kan fibration of simplicial sets.
hypotheses: For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. records.title: Proposition — Polynomial

conclusions: If there are integral effective Cartier divisors $D_i\subset X$ and a closed subset $Z^{\prime}\subset X$ whose irreducible components have codimension at least2 such that $Z\subset Z^{\prime}\cup\bigcup_iD_i$ set-theoretically, then there exist nonnegative integers $a_i$, zero for almost all $i$, such that $D=\sum_i a_iD_i$ is contained in $Z$ as a closed subscheme and $D\to Z$ is an isomorphism on an open $U\subset Z$ whose complement has all irreducible components of codimension at least2 in $X$.
If $Z$ is nowhere dense and either every $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for $x\in Z$ is a UFD or $X$ is regular, then such a family $D_i$ and subset $Z^{\prime}$ exist.
hypotheses: $X$ is a Noetherian scheme and $Z\subset X$ a closed subscheme.
records.statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Assume there exist
\begin{enumerate}
\item a collection of integral effective Cartier divisors
$D_i \subset X$, $i \in I$
\item a closed subset $Z' \subset X$ all of whose irreducible components
have codimension $\geq 2$ in $X$

\end{enumerate}
such that $Z \subset Z' \cup \bigcup_{i \in I} D_i$ set-theoretically.
Then there exist integers $a_i \geq 0$ with $a_i = 0$ for almost all $i \in I$
such that the effective Cartier divisor
$$
D = \sum a_i D_i
$$
is contained in $Z$ and such that the inclusion morphism $D \to Z$
is an isomorphism away from codimension $2$ in $X$
(in the sense that there exists an open $U \subset Z$ such that
$D \cap U \to Z \cap U$ is an isomorphism and such that every
irreducible component of $Z \setminus U$ has codimension $\geq 2$ in $X$).
When $Z$ is nowhere dense in $X$ existence of the $D_i$, $i \in I$ and $Z'$
is guaranteed if $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a UFD for all $x \in Z$
or if $X$ is regular.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.
