records.title: Lemma — Lift through quasi isomorphism

conclusions:
Let $A\to B$ be finite type ring map and $\mathfrak p \subset A$ a prime
ideal. Then there exist an \'etale ring map $A \to A'$ and a prime
$\mathfrak p' \subset A'$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$\kappa(\mathfrak p) = \kappa(\mathfrak p')$,
\item
$ B \otimes_A A' = B_1\times \ldots \times B_r \times C$,
\item
$ A'\to B_i$ is finite and there exists a unique prime $q_i\subset B_i$ lying
over $\mathfrak p'$, and
\item all irreducible components of the fibre
$\Spec(C \otimes_{A'} \kappa(\mathfrak p'))$ of $C$ over $\mathfrak p'$
have dimension at least 1.
\end{enumerate}
The étale extension A→A' includes a **chosen prime p' above p with identical residue field**, and the decomposition B⊗_A A'=∏B_i×C is global over A'. Each finite B_i has exactly one prime over p'; C has **no zero-dimensional irreducible component in the fibre** at p', though it can have positive-dimensional fibre components.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. A local ring is **strictly henselian** if henselian with separably closed residue field. A finite $R$-algebra is a ring $A$ finite as an $R$-module. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.

records.title: Theorem — Quasi finite etale locally

conclusions: The triangle K→L→M→K[1] whose boundary is represented by π·d_L·s for graded splittings π,s is, up to canonical isomorphism in the homotopy category, independent of the splittings.
hypotheses: (A,d) is a dg algebra and 0→K→L→M→0 is an admissible short exact sequence of dg A-modules.
records.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Let
$0 \to K \to L \to M \to 0$ be an admissible short exact sequence
of differential graded $A$-modules. The triangle
\begin{equation}
K \to L \to M \xrightarrow{\delta} K[1]
\end{equation}
where $\delta$ is the connecting arrow represented by $\pi\circ\mathrm d_L\circ s:M\to K[1]$ for graded $A$-module splittings $s:M\to L$ and $\pi:L\to K$ with $\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}s$ is, up to canonical
isomorphism in $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$, independent of the choices of such graded splittings.

records.title: Lemma — Triangle independent splittings

conclusions: (Aff/S)_etale→(Sch/S)_etale is special cocontinuous.
It induces Sh((Aff/S)_etale)≃Sh((Sch/S)_etale).
hypotheses: S is a scheme.
Sch_etale is a big étale site containing S.
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\Sch_\etale$ be a big \'etale
site containing $S$.
The functor
$(\textit{Aff}/S)_\etale \to (\Sch/S)_\etale$
is special cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi from
$\Sh((\textit{Aff}/S)_\etale)$ to
$\Sh((\Sch/S)_\etale)$.
Here special cocontinuous means continuous and cocontinuous, locally faithful (equal image arrows become equal on a cover), locally full (arrows between images lift on a cover of the source object), and cover-dense (every target object has a cover by images).

records.title: Lemma — Idempotents determined modulo radical

hypotheses:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is separated and
locally quasi-finite.
records.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is separated and
locally quasi-finite. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $\mathcal{F}$ in $\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)$ and a geometric
point $\overline{y} : \Spec(k) \to Y$ we have
$$
(f_!\mathcal{F})_{\overline{y}} =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{f(\overline{x}) = \overline{y}} \mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}}
$$
functorially in $\mathcal{F}$, and
\item the functor $f_!$ is exact.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Normalization and henselization

conclusions: An exact triangulated functor $Lf^*:D(\mathcal O')\to D(\mathcal O)$ exists, and for any K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O'$-modules having flat terms, $Lf^*\mathcal K^\bullet$ is represented by the ordinary termwise pullback $f^*\mathcal K^\bullet$.
In particular the same computation applies to any bounded-above complex of flat $\mathcal O'$-modules.
hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C'),\mathcal O')$ is a morphism of ringed topoi.
records.statement:
A complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules is K-flat when $\mathrm{Tot}(\mathcal A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ (sites-cohomology.tex:2998–3008). For an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C'),\mathcal O')$, $f^*$ is the ordinary module pullback $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O')\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. The source names the result `derived-base-change` but the claim is the **existence and computation of derived pullback** (not a cartesian base-change isomorphism).

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}) \to (\Sh(\mathcal{C}'), \mathcal{O}')$
be a morphism of ringed topoi. There exists an exact functor
$$
Lf^* : D(\mathcal{O}') \longrightarrow D(\mathcal{O})
$$
of triangulated categories so that
$Lf^*\mathcal{K}^\bullet = f^*\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ for any
K-flat complex $\mathcal{K}^\bullet$ with flat terms and
in particular for any bounded above complex of flat $\mathcal{O}'$-modules.

records.title: Lemma — Normal effective Cartier divisor S1

conclusions: There is a Leray spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(\mathcal D,R^q f_*(\mathcal F^\bullet))\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(\mathcal C,\mathcal F^\bullet)$.
hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ is an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi.
$\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a bounded-below complex of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules.
records.statement:
For a morphism of ringed topoi $f$, $Rf_*$ is the derived pushforward and $R^qf_*(\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is its $q$th cohomology sheaf. The groups $H^p(\mathcal D,-)$ and $H^{p+q}(\mathcal C,-)$ are derived global-sections cohomology; a bounded-below complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is assumed to ensure the indicated spectral sequence applies. There is **no flatness hypothesis** on $f$.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules. There is a spectral sequence
$$
E_2^{p, q} = H^p(\mathcal{D}, R^qf_*(\mathcal{F}^\bullet))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)$.

records.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ an fpqc covering. Here fpqc covering means each $g_i$ is flat and, for each affine open $U\subset Y$, there are finitely many affine opens $V_j\subset Y_{i_j}$ with $\bigcup_j g_{i_j}(V_j)=U$. records.title: Lemma — Descending property locally finite type

conclusions: The pushed-forward complex $f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ is K-injective over $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$.
hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ is a **flat** morphism of ringed topoi.
$\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a K-injective complex of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules.
records.statement:
A complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$ of modules is K-injective if $\mathrm{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet[n])=0$ for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ and every integer $n$; such complexes compute unbounded right derived functors. A flat morphism of ringed topoi is assumed because its module pullback functor is exact, making the right adjoint $f_*$ preserve K-injectivity in this case. This flatness is candidate-local, not a chapter hypothesis.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a flat morphism
of ringed topoi. If $\mathcal{I}^\bullet$ is a K-injective
complex of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules, then
$f_*\mathcal{I}^\bullet$ is K-injective
as a complex of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-modules.

records.title: Lemma — Norm invertible

conclusions: Their pullback exists in $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$; if $f$ is strict, the pullback map $f':B\times_A C\to C$ is strict.
hypotheses: Let $f:B\to A$ and $g:C\to A$ be morphisms in $\mathrm{Fil}(\mathcal A)$.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $A, B, C \in \text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$.
Let $f : B \to A$ and $g : C \to A$ be morphisms.
Then there exists a fibre product
$$
\xymatrix{
B \times_A C \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & B \ar[d]^f \\
C \ar[r]^g & A
}
$$
in $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$. If $f$ is strict, so is $f'$.

records.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $0 \to K \to L \to M \to 0$ be an admissible short exact sequence
of differential graded $A$-modules. Let $s : M \to L$ and $\pi : L \to K$
be splittings such that $\Ker(\pi) = \Im(s)$.
Then we obtain a morphism
$$
\delta = \pi \circ \text{d}_L \circ s : M \to K[1]
$$
of $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ which induces the boundary maps
in the long exact sequence of cohomology associated to the displayed short exact sequence.

conclusions: There exists one compatible sequence of bounded-above complexes $\mathcal K_n^\bullet$ and maps $\mathcal K_n^\bullet\to\tau_{\le n}\mathcal G^\bullet$, arranged in a commuting truncation diagram, such that each vertical map is a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism.

Every term of each $\mathcal K_n^\bullet$ is a direct sum of extension-by-zero modules $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$; all transition maps $\mathcal K_n^\bullet\to\mathcal K_{n+1}^\bullet$ are termwise split monomorphisms with cokernel of the same direct-sum form.
The induced map $\operatorname{colim}_n\mathcal K_n^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.

records.statement:
For a ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ and $U\in\mathcal C$, let $\mathcal O_U$ be the restricted ring on the slice site $\mathcal C/U$ and let $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ denote extension by zero along the localization $j_U:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C$, the left adjoint to restriction of $\mathcal O$-modules. The truncation $\tau_{\le n}\mathcal G^\bullet$ is the usual good truncation of a complex at degree $n$. The source asserts an **existential** resolution diagram with the same $\mathcal K_n^\bullet$ satisfying all listed properties, not unrelated resolutions for each $n$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
For any complex $\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
there exists a commutative diagram of complexes of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{K}_1^\bullet \ar[d] \ar[r] &
\mathcal{K}_2^\bullet \ar[d] \ar[r] & \ldots \\
\tau_{\leq 1}\mathcal{G}^\bullet \ar[r] &
\tau_{\leq 2}\mathcal{G}^\bullet \ar[r] & \ldots
}
$$
with the following properties: (1) the vertical arrows are quasi-isomorphisms
and termwise surjective,
(2) each $\mathcal{K}_n^\bullet$ is a bounded above complex whose terms
are direct sums of $\mathcal{O}$-modules of the form $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$, and
(3) the maps $\mathcal{K}_n^\bullet \to \mathcal{K}_{n + 1}^\bullet$ are
termwise split injections whose cokernels are direct sums of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules of the form $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$. Moreover, the map
$\colim \mathcal{K}_n^\bullet \to \mathcal{G}^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

conclusions:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let
$\eta \in X$ be a generic point of an irreducible component of $X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$
whose stalk $\mathcal{F}_{\overline{\eta}}$ is zero.
Then $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$ is a filtered colimit of
constructible abelian sheaves $\mathcal{F}_i$ such that for each $i$
the support of $\mathcal{F}_i$ is contained
in a closed subscheme not containing $\eta$.
\item Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and $\mathcal{F}$ a sheaf
of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\etale$ whose stalk
$\mathcal{F}_{\overline{\eta}}$ is zero. Then
$\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$
is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules $\mathcal{F}_i$ such that for each $i$
the support of $\mathcal{F}_i$ is contained in a closed subscheme
not containing $\eta$.
\end{enumerate}
All quantifiers and conditions from the pinned source are retained. The result is for constructible sheaves in the **small** étale category of a qcqs scheme.

records.title: Lemma — Zero in generic point

conclusions:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category. Let
$\mathcal{D}' \subset \mathcal{D}$ be a full triangulated subcategory. Let
$X \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})$. The category of arrows $E \to X$ with
$E \in \Ob(\mathcal{D}')$ is filtered.
The objects are arrows E→X with E in the full triangulated subcategory, and arrows are commutative triangles over X; filtered means nonempty, common successors, and eventual equalizers of any parallel pair.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A $k$-linear triangulated category is a triangulated category with $k$-vector-space Hom sets and $k$-linear composition and shift. For a $k$-vector space $V$ write $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. Let $D_{\mathrm{perf}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denote perfect complexes (locally bounded finite-rank vector-bundle complexes), $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the bounded derived category with coherent cohomology. Global Ext is $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(E,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(E,K[i])$.A $k$-linear *cohomological functor* $H:\mathcal T^{op}\to\mathrm{Vect}_k$ is contravariant and yields a long exact sequence under every shifted distinguished triangle. *Homological* means the analogous covariant long exact property. An object $C$ is *compact* if maps from $C$ commute with arbitrary small direct sums; a triangulated category is *compactly generated* if a set of compact objects detects zero objects.

records.title: Lemma — Characterize integral

conclusions:
$\mathcal{J}$ is regular
(resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) if and only if

such that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and such that $I$
is generated by a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular,
quasi-regular) sequence $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in A$.
hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{J}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{J}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
Then $\mathcal{J}$ is regular
(resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) if and only if
for every $x \in \text{Supp}(\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J})$ there exists
an affine open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$, $U = \Spec(A)$
such that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and such that $I$
is generated by a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular,
quasi-regular) sequence $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in A$.

conclusions:

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

For a nonconstant morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth curves over $k$, the following are equivalent: the function-field extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ is finite separable, the map of invertible differential sheaves $df:f^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$ is generically nonzero, and $f$ is étale on a dense open subscheme of $X$. Under these conditions, the different ideal is the zeroth Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/Y}$, whose closed zero scheme $R_f$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$. Its degree is $\deg R_f=\sum_x\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal O_{R_f,x})[\kappa(x):k]$. For proper smooth curves, $\deg f=[k(X):k(Y)]$.

Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. The $n$-fold Frobenius twist of a $k$-scheme $X$ is $X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^n}\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F_{X/k}^n:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is its relative $n$-fold Frobenius morphism. For a smooth curve it is finite purely inseparable of degree $p^n$ (for $n\ge0$). A morphism of proper integral curves is nonconstant if its function-field homomorphism is injective and not just an extension of constants.

records.title: Lemma — Dualizing localize

conclusions: Base change of the projection comparison is compatible with α (commutative square).
hypotheses: Cartesian Tor-independent qcqs square, canonical α and projection comparisons μ.
records.statement:
For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ for the unbounded derived category of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology on $T$, and let $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$. Its unit and counit are $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_fRf_*$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes $X'=X\times_Y Y'\xrightarrow{g'}X$ above $g:Y'\to Y$ and with vertical maps $f':X'\to Y'$ and $f:X\to Y$. Assume the pair $(f,g)$ is Tor-independent, so that the standard derived base-change map $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*L(g')^*$ is an isomorphism. Let $a_f,a_{f'}$ be the respective right adjoints. The *duality base-change transformation* is $\alpha:L(g')^*a_f\to a_{f'}Lg^*$, constructed by adjunction from $\beta$ using its mate $Rg'_*a_{f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}a_fRg_*$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. Then for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the square
\[
\begin{matrix}
L(g')^*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))&\xrightarrow{L(g')^*(\mu_{f,K})}&L(g')^*a_f(K)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\alpha_K\\
L(f')^*Lg^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_{f'}(\mathcal O_{Y'})&\xrightarrow{\mu_{f',Lg^*K}}&a_{f'}(Lg^*K)
\end{matrix}
\]
commutes, where the left vertical map uses derived-pullback associativity and $\alpha_{\mathcal O_Y}:L(g')^*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_{f'}(\mathcal O_{Y'})$. All tensors in each row are over the relevant source scheme.

records.title: Lemma — Constructible is retrocompact

conclusions: Normalized dualizing data are independent of cover up to canonical compatible isomorphism.
hypotheses: S Noetherian and D_S dualizing; finite-type T with two finite separated-over-S open covers.
records.statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. Let $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ be two finite open coverings of the same finite-type $S$-scheme $T$ by $S$-separated open subschemes. If a dualizing complex normalized relative to $(D_S,\mathcal U)$ exists, then one normalized relative to $(D_S,\mathcal V)$ exists, and their underlying complexes are canonically isomorphic compatibly with the local identifications on a common refinement. No separatedness assumption on all of $T$ is required.

records.title: Lemma — From hausdorff

conclusions: Every-affine and some-affine-cover definitions of a dualizing scheme complex coincide.
hypotheses: X locally Noetherian and K in D(O_X), dualizing ring-complex defined explicitly.
records.statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and let $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$. For each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, the sheafification functor $D(A)\to D(\mathcal O_U)$ sends a complex $D$ of $A$-modules to the associated quasi-coherent complex $\widetilde D$. A dualizing complex over the Noetherian ring $A$ means a bounded coherent complex $D$ of finite injective dimension for which $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$ is an isomorphism. Then the following are equivalent: (1) for *every* affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ there exists a dualizing $A$-complex $D_U$ with $K|_U\simeq\widetilde{D_U}$; (2) there exists *some* affine open cover $\{U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i\}$ of $X$ and dualizing $A_i$-complexes $D_i$ with $K|_{U_i}\simeq\widetilde{D_i}$. Hence being dualizing is an affine-local condition independent of a chosen affine cover.

records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $Z \to X$ be a relative $H_1$-regular immersion.
Assume $X \to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists an open subscheme $U \subset X$ such that
$Z \subset U$ and such that $U \to S$ is flat, and
\item $Z \to X$ is a regular immersion and the same remains
true after any base change.
\end{enumerate}

If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. records.statement: For a map of spaces f, generalizations lift if for every point x over y and every generalization y-prime of y there is a generalization x-prime of x over y-prime; specializations lift if the analogous statement holds with specialization in both places. The ring map satisfies going down if and only if generalizations lift along \(f\); it satisfies going up if and only if specializations lift along \(f\).

A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $F : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$
be a $1$-morphism of stacks in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{X}$ is representable by an algebraic space, and
\item $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation,
\end{enumerate}
then $\mathcal{Y}$ is an algebraic stack.

conclusions: $A^p(X \to Y) = A^{p - d}(X \to Z)$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The *geometric genus* of a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme is the sum of the genera of smooth projective models of the geometrically integral components over suitable field extensions, counted after extension to an algebraic closure; finite purely inseparable extensions may be required to achieve such models.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $C$ be a proper curve over $k$.
Set $\kappa = H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C)$. Then
$$

conclusions: A reduced, locally Noetherian singleton algebraic space $Z$ is regular.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

conclusions: The local rings of X are UFDs iff X is normal and the canonical $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is surjective.

hypotheses:

(\ref{equation-c1}) $\Pic(X) \to \text{Cl}(X)$.
records.statement:
For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Consider the map
(\ref{equation-c1}) $\Pic(X) \to \text{Cl}(X)$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the local rings of $X$ are UFDs, and
\item $X$ is normal and $\Pic(X) \to \text{Cl}(X)$
is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
In this case $\Pic(X) \to \text{Cl}(X)$ is an isomorphism.

\{s \in \mathcal{F}(U') \mid \text{Supp}(s) \subset Z\}

conclusions:
We have the following implications:
$i$ is regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.
hypotheses: Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
We have the following implications:
$i$ is regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Rightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.

records.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_S$-module
of finite presentation. Let $S = Z_{-1} \supset Z_0 \supset Z_1 \supset \ldots$
be the closed subschemes cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)$.
Set $S_r = Z_{r - 1} \setminus Z_r$.
Then $S' = \coprod_{r \geq 0} S_r$ represents the functor
$$
F_{flat} : \Sch/S \longrightarrow \textit{Sets},\quad\quad
T \longmapsto
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\{*\} & \text{if }\mathcal{F}_T\text{ flat over }T\\
\emptyset & \text{otherwise}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
Moreover, $\mathcal{F}|_{S_r}$ is locally free of rank $r$ and the
morphisms $S_r \to S$ and $S' \to S$ are of finite presentation.
For $T\to S$, $\mathcal F_T$ denotes the pullback to $T$.

Let $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$ be ring homomorphisms with $A'\to A$ surjective and kernel $I$. Put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
An object of $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ is a triple $(N,M',\varphi)$, where $N$ is a $B$-module, $M'$ is an $A'$-module, and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{A'}A=M'/IM'$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. Regard $\varphi$ also as the induced $B$-linear map $N\to M'/IM'$. For such a triple put $M=M'/IM'$ and $N'=N\times_{\varphi,M}M'=\{(n,m')\in N\oplus M':\varphi(n)=m'\pmod{IM'}\}$, with the $B'$-module structure given by the two projections $B'\to B,A'$.
Let $G:\mathrm{Mod}_{B'}\to\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ send $L'$ to $(L'\otimes_{B'}B,L'\otimes_{B'}A',\mathrm{can})$, with $\mathrm{can}$ the canonical identification after tensoring both components with $A$.
The functor $F:(N,M',\varphi)\mapsto N\times_{\varphi,M}M'$ is right adjoint to $G$. Moreover $G\circ F$ is canonically isomorphic to the identity on $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$: for every compatible triple, $N'\otimes_{B'}B\cong N$ and $N'\otimes_{B'}A'\cong M'$, compatibly with $\varphi$.

Let $k$ be a field, and let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$. Define exterior product on cycles by $[W]\times[V]=[W\times_k V]_{\dim W+\dim V}$ for integral closed $W\subset X$, $V\subset Y$, extending bilinearly, where $[W\times_kV]$ uses generic-point multiplicities even if this product is reducible or nonreduced.

For a morphism $f:T\to U$, a degree-$p$ bivariant class $c\in A^p(T\to U)$ consists of homomorphisms $\mathrm{CH}_n(U')\to\mathrm{CH}_{n-p}(T\times_UU')$ for all $U'\to U$ of locally finite type, compatible with proper pushforwards, flat pullbacks of fixed relative dimension, and Gysin maps for zero schemes of invertible-sheaf sections. Products of bivariant classes are composition of their compatible families after base change.

Let $X$ be smooth over a field $k$. Its diagonal $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow X\times_kX$ is a regular immersion and has a Gysin class $\Delta^!$. For schemes $U,V$ locally of finite type over $X$, define intersection of Chow classes by $\alpha\cdot\beta:=\Delta^!(\alpha\times\beta)\in\mathrm{CH}_*(U\times_XV)$; for $X$ smooth of pure dimension $d$, $\mathrm{CH}_n(U)\cdot\mathrm{CH}_m(V)\subseteq\mathrm{CH}_{n+m-d}(U\times_XV)$. For $U=V=X$ this defines the intersection product on $\mathrm{CH}_*(X)$.

For a local complete intersection morphism $f:U\to V$ that has a global factorization $U\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{g}V$ with $i$ a regular immersion and $g$ smooth, its Gysin class is $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$, independent of the factorization. A smooth $k$-morphism between smooth $k$-schemes is lci; the morphisms between smooth $k$-schemes in the statements below have such Gysin classes. On a regular closed immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow T$, $i^!$ is the Gysin pullback of bivariant intersection theory.

records.title: Lemma — Geometrically connected criterion

conclusions:
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item every proper finitely generated ideal $I\subset R$ has a nonzero annihilator,
\item any injective map of projective $R$-modules is
universally injective,
\item if $u : N \to M$ is injective and $N$, $M$ are finite projective
$R$-modules then $\Coker(u)$ is a finite projective $R$-module,
\item if $N \subset M$ and $N$, $M$ are finite projective as $R$-modules, then
$N$ is a direct summand of $M$, and
\item any injective map $R \to R^{\oplus n}$ is a split injection.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

A *residual space* $Z_x\to X$ at $x\in|X|$ is the unique monomorphism from a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space with singleton underlying topology whose image is $x$ and which is universal among morphisms of such spaces into $X$ representing $x$. A space is *locally separated* if its diagonal is an immersion; it is quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. A locally Noetherian algebraic space is one with an étale cover by locally Noetherian schemes.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over $S$. Let $x \in |X|$ be a point. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|f|(|Y|)$ is contained in $\{x\} \subset |X|$,
\item $Y$ is reduced, and
\item $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism
$x : \operatorname{Spec}(k) \to X$ where $k$ is a field (for example if $X$ is decent).
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ factors through
the residual space $Z_x = \operatorname{Spec}(k)$ of $X$ at $x$.

records.statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and a divided power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, where $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with divided powers. Set $S_0=V(\mathcal I)$ and choose a morphism $X\to S_0$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. A divided power thickening of $X/S$ is a triple $(U,T,\delta)$ with a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ inducing a homeomorphism on topological spaces, divided powers $\delta$ on its ideal $\mathcal J_T$, a compatible morphism of divided power schemes $T\to S$, and a map $U\to X$. These objects with compatible maps form $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)$; its full subcategory $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$ has $U\to X$ an open immersion. Both carry the Zariski topology (covers arise from Zariski covers of $T$ compatible with $U$). The forgetful functor $\mathrm{CRIS}(X/S)\to\operatorname{Sch}/X$ sends $(U,T,\delta)$ to $U$.

On the small crystalline site $\mathrm{Cris}(X/S)$, the crystalline structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ restricts to $\mathcal O_T$ on an object $(U,T,\delta)$. A sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules restricts to a sheaf $\mathcal F_T$ on $T$. It is a crystal if each pullback comparison map $f^*\mathcal F_T\to\mathcal F_{T'}$ for a morphism $(U',T',\delta')\to(U,T,\delta)$ is an isomorphism. It is locally quasi-coherent if every $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherent as a module on the site if it is locally presented by free $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules. The sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$ is the universal divided power sheaf of differentials for the structure morphism of the crystalline site to the Zariski site of $S$; it restricts to $\Omega_{T/S,\delta}$ on each object.

A connection on an $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-module $\mathcal F$ is an additive map $\nabla:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X/S}}\Omega_{X/S}$ obeying $\nabla(fs)=f\nabla(s)+s\otimes df$. It extends to the de Rham complex by $\nabla(s\otimes\omega)=\nabla(s)\wedge\omega+s\otimes d\omega$; it is integrable when the resulting composite $\nabla^2:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\otimes\Omega^2_{X/S}$ is zero.

Under the global crystalline setup stated above,
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a crystal in $\mathcal{O}_{X/S}$-modules
on $\text{Cris}(X/S)$. Then $\mathcal{F}$ comes equipped with a
canonical integrable connection.

hypotheses: Let $K$ be a field with separable closure $K^{sep}$ and absolute Galois group $G_K$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
Let $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a category fibred in groupoids.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{S}$ is representable if and only if
the following conditions are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{S}$ is fibred in setoids, and
\item the presheaf $U \mapsto \Ob(\mathcal{S}_U)/\cong$ is
representable.
\end{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{S}$ is representable the pair $(X, j)$, where $j$ is the
equivalence $j : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}/X$, is uniquely determined
up to isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $\mathcal S_X(U)$ be the regular functions acting injectively on $\mathcal O_U$ as a sheaf. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S_X(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal K_X$; a meromorphic section is a global section of this sheaf. For an invertible $\mathcal L$, such a section is regular if multiplication $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is injective. Pullback of meromorphic functions is defined for $f:X\to Y$ when restrictions of $f^\sharp$ send every regular section on Y to a regular section on X. The denominator ideal of $s$ is $\mathcal I(V)=\{a\in\mathcal O_X(V):as\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. For a global function h, $X_h=\{x:h_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\}$. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral scheme. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $s \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be a
regular (i.e., nonzero) meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$. Then the sets
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ a prime divisor with generic point }\xi
\text{ and }s\text{ not in }\mathcal{L}_\xi\}
$$
and
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ is a prime divisor and }
\text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s) \not = 0\}
$$
are locally finite in $X$.

records.title: Lemma — Descending property affine

conclusions: Upper shriek along A^1_Y→Y is isomorphic (noncanonically) to pullback shifted by one.
hypotheses: Affine-line projection over an object of FTS_S.
records.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Let $Y\in\mathrm{FTS}_S$ and $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$ be the affine-line projection. Then there exists a natural isomorphism of functors
\[
p^!(-)\cong Lp^*(-)[1]:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1_Y}).
\]
The isomorphism is explicitly *noncanonical*; it follows after choosing a trivialization of the restriction of the relative canonical line bundle of $\mathbf P^1_Y$.

conclusions:
the bivariant class
of Definition \ref{definition-localized-chern}
$$
P_p(Z' \to X', E') \in A^p(Z' \to X'),
\quad\text{resp.}\quad
c_p(Z' \to X', E') \in A^p(Z' \to X')
$$
constructed as in Lemma \ref{lemma-independent-loc-chern}
using $X', Z', E'$ is the restriction
(Remark \ref{remark-restriction-bivariant}) of the
bivariant class $P_p(Z \to X, E) \in A^p(Z \to X)$,
resp.\ $c_p(Z \to X, E) \in A^p(Z \to X)$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

In the following localized setting, let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, let $E$ be perfect in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, and let $p\ge0$. Suppose that $E|_{X\setminus Z}$ is zero (for $P_p$), or a finite locally free sheaf of rank less than $p$ in degree $0$ (for $c_p$); also assume one of: $X$ is quasi-compact, its irreducible components are quasi-compact, $E$ has a locally bounded finite locally free representative, or $E$ is pulled back from a perfect object on a locally finite type $X'$ with quasi-compact irreducible components. The associated localized classes $P_p(Z\to X,E)$ and $c_p(Z\to X,E)$ lie in $A^p(Z\to X)$, characterized by $i_*\circ P_p(Z\to X,E)=P_p(E)$ and $i_*\circ c_p(Z\to X,E)=c_p(E)$. The localized character is $\operatorname{ch}(Z\to X,E)=\sum_{p\ge0}P_p(Z\to X,E)/p!$.
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

In the following localized setting, let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, let $E$ be perfect in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, and let $p\ge0$. Suppose that $E|_{X\setminus Z}$ is zero (for $P_p$), or a finite locally free sheaf of rank less than $p$ in degree $0$ (for $c_p$); also assume one of: $X$ is quasi-compact, its irreducible components are quasi-compact, $E$ has a locally bounded finite locally free representative, or $E$ is pulled back from a perfect object on a locally finite type $X'$ with quasi-compact irreducible components. The associated localized classes $P_p(Z\to X,E)$ and $c_p(Z\to X,E)$ lie in $A^p(Z\to X)$, characterized by $i_*\circ P_p(Z\to X,E)=P_p(E)$ and $i_*\circ c_p(Z\to X,E)=c_p(E)$. The localized character is $\operatorname{ch}(Z\to X,E)=\sum_{p\ge0}P_p(Z\to X,E)/p!$.

In the localized perfect-complex setup above
let $f : X' \to X$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Denote $E' = f^*E$ and $Z' = f^{-1}(Z)$. Then the bivariant class
of the localized construction specified above
$$
P_p(Z' \to X', E') \in A^p(Z' \to X'),
\quad\text{resp.}\quad
c_p(Z' \to X', E') \in A^p(Z' \to X')
$$
constructed by the localized characteristic-class rule
using $X', Z', E'$ is the restriction
(defined by base change of bivariant-class families) of the
bivariant class $P_p(Z \to X, E) \in A^p(Z \to X)$,
resp.\ $c_p(Z \to X, E) \in A^p(Z \to X)$.

records.statement:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is of finite type.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is universally pure along $X_s$, and
\item for every morphism of pointed schemes $(S', s') \to (S, s)$
the pullback $\mathcal{F}_{S'}$ is pure along $X_{s'}$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $\mathcal{F}$ is universally pure relative to $S$ if and
only if every base change $\mathcal{F}_{S'}$ of $\mathcal{F}$ is
pure relative to $S'$.

conclusions: The base-composition functor u is cocontinuous and has continuous right adjoint v given by fibre product over S.
These functors define the same topos morphism f_big.
For G on (Sch/S)_Zar, f_big^{-1}(G)(U/T)=G(U/S).
For F on (Sch/T)_Zar, f_big,*(F)(U/S)=F((U×_S T)/T).
f_big^{-1} has a left adjoint f_big! preserving fibre products and equalizers.
hypotheses: Sch_Zar is a big Zariski site.
f:T→S is a morphism in Sch_Zar.
records.statement:
Let $\Sch_{Zar}$ be a big Zariski site.
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism in $\Sch_{Zar}$.
The functor
$$
u : (\Sch/T)_{Zar} \longrightarrow (\Sch/S)_{Zar},
\quad
V/T \longmapsto V/S
$$
is cocontinuous, and has a continuous right adjoint
$$
v : (\Sch/S)_{Zar} \longrightarrow (\Sch/T)_{Zar},
\quad
(U \to S) \longmapsto (U \times_S T \to T).
$$
They induce the same morphism of topoi
$$
f_{big} :
\Sh((\Sch/T)_{Zar})
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_{Zar})
$$
We have $f_{big}^{-1}(\mathcal{G})(U/T) = \mathcal{G}(U/S)$.
We have $f_{big, *}(\mathcal{F})(U/S) = \mathcal{F}(U \times_S T/T)$.
Also, $f_{big}^{-1}$ has a left adjoint $f_{big!}$ which commutes with
fibre products and equalizers.

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$, $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)[n]=\{\mathcal L:\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_X\}$. If $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $\dim X=1$, the arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subscheme with ideal locally generated by one nonzerodivisor. A relative effective Cartier divisor on $X/S$ is such a divisor $D\subset X$ with $D\to S$ flat; this does not assume $X\to S$ flat. Sums are defined by products of ideal sheaves. Let $\varphi : X \to S$ be a flat morphism which is locally of finite
presentation. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $x \in Z$ with image $s \in S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$,
then there exists an open $U \subset X$ and a
relative effective Cartier divisor $D \subset U$ such that
$Z \cap U \subset D$ and $Z_s \cap U = D_s$.
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$,
the morphism $Z \to X$ is of finite presentation, and $Z \to S$ is flat at
$x$, then we can choose $U$ and $D$ such that $Z \cap U = D$.
\item If $Z_s \subset X_s$ is a Cartier divisor in a neighbourhood of $x$
and $Z$ is a locally principal closed subscheme of $X$ in a neighbourhood
of $x$, then we can choose $U$ and $D$ such that $Z \cap U = D$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, if $Z \to S$ is locally of finite presentation and flat and
all fibres $Z_s \subset X_s$ are effective Cartier divisors, then
$Z$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor. Similarly, if $Z$
is a locally principal closed subscheme of $X$ such that all fibres
$Z_s \subset X_s$ are effective Cartier divisors, then
$Z$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor. The opens U in the three local assertions are neighbourhoods of x.

records.title: Lemma — Integral closure stalks

conclusions: The derived pushforwards of every $\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and of the full relative de Rham complex are perfect and satisfy derived base change for every $S'\to S$.
hypotheses: $f:X\to S$ is proper and smooth; for base change, $S'\to S$ is arbitrary and $X'=X\times_S S'$.
records.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper, smooth morphism of schemes. For $p\geq 0$ put $\Omega^p_{X/S}=\bigwedge^p_{\mathcal O_X}\Omega^1_{X/S}$, and let $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ be the relative de Rham complex. Each $Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and the derived direct image $Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ are perfect objects of $D(\mathcal O_S)$.

More precisely, for every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of schemes, let $X'=X\times_S S'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to S'$ be the induced maps. For each $p\geq0$ the canonical derived base-change map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^p_{X'/S'}$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{S'})$, and so is the analogous map
$$Lg^*(Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})\longrightarrow Rf'_*\Omega^\bullet_{X'/S'}.$$

records.title: Lemma — Flattening artinian

conclusions:
The group of rank $1$ coherent reflexive $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
is isomorphic to the Weil divisor class group $\text{Cl}(X)$ of $X$.
hypotheses: Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme.
records.statement:
For an $\mathcal O_X$-module F, $F^*=\mathcal Hom(F,\mathcal O_X)$ and reflexive means the evaluation map $F\to F^{**}$ is an isomorphism. The rank-one reflexive group law is $[F][G]=[(F\otimes G)^{**}]$. For a locally Noetherian integral scheme X write $R(X)$ for its function field. A prime divisor is an integral codimension-one closed subscheme; $\operatorname{Div}(X)$ consists of locally finite integer sums of them. At its generic point $\xi$, write $\operatorname{ord}_Z(a/b)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/a)-\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi}/b)$ for nonzero local a,b. For a meromorphic line section s use $a/b=s/e$ with e a local generator of the line bundle; define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_Z\operatorname{ord}_{Z,\mathcal L}(s)[Z]$. Principal divisors are $\operatorname{div}_X(f)$ for $f\in R(X)^*$; $\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ is Div modulo principal divisors. The canonical map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ sends a line bundle to the class of its nonzero meromorphic section. Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme.
The group of rank $1$ coherent reflexive $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
is isomorphic to the Weil divisor class group $\text{Cl}(X)$ of $X$.

conclusions:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth proper schemes over $k$.
Given a $k$-linear, exact, fully faithful functor
$F : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
there exists a Fourier-Mukai functor
$F' : D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ whose kernel
is in $D_{perf}(\mathcal{O}_{X \times Y})$ which is a sibling to $F$.
The conclusion is existence of a perfect-kernel Fourier–Mukai **sibling**, not natural isomorphism. No projectivity of X is required in this lemma.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal A$ be abelian and $\mathcal D$ triangulated. Two exact functors $F,F':D^b(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal D$ are *siblings* if (i) their restrictions to the heart $\mathcal A\hookrightarrow D^b(\mathcal A)$ are **naturally isomorphic**, and (ii) for every $K\in D^b(\mathcal A)$ the objects $F(K)$ and $F'(K)$ are isomorphic (with no claim these isomorphisms are natural in $K$). The category $\mathcal A$ has *enough negative objects* if for each $X\in\mathcal A$ there exists an epimorphism $N\twoheadrightarrow X$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(X,N)=0$.

For a complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_{X\times_SY})$, its *Fourier–Mukai functor* is $\Phi_K:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$, $\Phi_K(M)=R\operatorname{pr}_{2*}(L\operatorname{pr}_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X\times_SY}}K)$; $\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2$ are projections. A *Fourier–Mukai kernel* is the complex $K$. $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ denotes complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $D_{\mathrm{perf}}$ those locally equivalent to bounded complexes of finite-rank locally free sheaves. The factor interchange $\tau:Y\times_SX\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_SY$ sends a kernel to one on the reversed product. For perfect $K$, $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(K,\mathcal O_{X\times_SY})$.

records.title: Lemma — Fully faithful

conclusions: A covering of T in Sch_etale exists which refines {T_i→T}.
If the original covering is standard étale, it is tautologically equivalent to a covering in Sch_etale.
If the original covering is Zariski, it is tautologically equivalent to a covering in Sch_etale.
hypotheses: Sch_etale is a big étale site as defined in topologies.tex:802–817.
T is an object of Sch_etale.
{T_i→T} is an arbitrary étale covering.
records.statement:
Let $\Sch_\etale$ be a big \'etale site as in
Definition \ref{definition-big-etale-site}.
Let $T \in \Ob(\Sch_\etale)$.
Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be an arbitrary \'etale covering of $T$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists a covering $\{U_j \to T\}_{j \in J}$ of $T$ in the site
$\Sch_\etale$ which refines $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ is a standard \'etale covering, then
it is tautologically equivalent to a covering in $\Sch_\etale$.
\item If $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ is a Zariski covering, then
it is tautologically equivalent to a covering in $\Sch_\etale$.
\end{enumerate}
Two families over the same target are tautologically equivalent when there are maps between their index sets in both directions and isomorphisms over the target from each source object to the corresponding source object in the other family.

conclusions:
for every reduced connected closed subscheme

hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

records.title: Lemma — Blow up and irreducible components

conclusions:
$M = \lim M_n$ is a flat $A$-module and
$Q \otimes_A M = \lim Q \otimes_A M_n$ for every finite $A$-module $Q$.
records.statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$. Let
$(M_n)$ be an inverse system of $A$-modules such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M_n$ is a flat $A/I^n$-module,
\item $M_{n + 1} \to M_n$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $M = \lim M_n$ is a flat $A$-module and
$Q \otimes_A M = \lim Q \otimes_A M_n$ for every finite $A$-module $Q$.

records.title: Lemma — Finite presentation permanence

conclusions:
the base change $i' : Z \times_X X' \to X'$
is a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular,
$H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) immersion.
hypotheses:
Let $i : Z \to X$ be a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular,
$H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) immersion. Let $X' \to X$ be a flat
morphism.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular,
$H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) immersion. Let $X' \to X$ be a flat
morphism. Then the base change $i' : Z \times_X X' \to X'$
is a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular,
$H_1$-regular, quasi-regular) immersion.
