A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

In the following localized setting, let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, let $E$ be perfect in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, and let $p\ge0$. The localized character is $\operatorname{ch}(Z\to X,E)=\sum_{p\ge0}P_p(Z\to X,E)/p!$.

conclusions: The inclusion $j:U\to X$ is affine iff for every $x\in X\setminus U$ there exists $n>0$ such that $s^n\in\mathfrak m_x\mathcal F^{[n]}_x$.
hypotheses:
Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a rank 1 coherent reflexive $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$. Let
$$
U = \{x \in X \mid s : \mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{F}_x

$$
records.statement:
For an $\mathcal O_X$-module F, $F^*=\mathcal Hom(F,\mathcal O_X)$ and reflexive means the evaluation map $F\to F^{**}$ is an isomorphism. The rank-one reflexive group law is $[F][G]=[(F\otimes G)^{**}]$. Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a rank 1 coherent reflexive $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$. Let
$$
U = \{x \in X \mid s : \mathcal{O}_{X, x} \to \mathcal{F}_x
\text{ is an isomorphism}\}
$$ Put $\mathcal F^{[1]}=\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F^{[n+1]}=(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F^{[n]})^{**}$; powers of s map into these sheaves. 
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item the inclusion morphism $j : U \to X$ is affine, and
\item for every $x \in X \setminus U$ there is an $n > 0$
such that $s^n \in \mathfrak m_x \mathcal{F}^{[n]}_x$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Flat eq

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

Let $p > 0$ be a prime number. Let $S$ be a scheme in characteristic $p$.
Let $X$ be a scheme over $S$. Then $\Omega_{X/S} = \Omega_{X/X^{(p)}}$.
Absolute Frobenius acts identically on points and by $a\mapsto a^p$ on functions. For $X/S$, $X^{(p)}=X\times_{S,F_S}S$, and $F_{X/S}$ is the canonical map induced by absolute Frobenius.

hypotheses: For a site $\mathcal S$ and a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, form the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $\mathcal A$-algebra resolution $\mathcal P_\bullet\to\mathcal B$, with $\mathcal P_0=\mathcal A[\mathcal B]$, $\mathcal P_1=\mathcal A[\mathcal A[\mathcal B]]$, and so on. Its normalized complex of $\mathcal B$-modules $\Omega_{\mathcal P_\bullet/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P_\bullet}\mathcal B$, in nonpositive degrees, is the cotangent complex $L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\in D(\mathcal B)$, and $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheaf of Kähler differentials. The map $L$ is functorial in squares of ring-sheaf homomorphisms.

For a morphism of ringed topoi or ringed spaces $f:(\mathscr X,\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})\to(\mathscr Y,\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y})$, the cotangent complex $L_f=L_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}\in D(\mathcal O_{\mathscr X})$ is defined using its map of sheaves of rings $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}\to\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}$. Its relative differentials are $\Omega_f=\Omega_{\mathcal O_{\mathscr X}/f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathscr Y}}$. Here $Lf^*$ denotes derived inverse image with scalar extension, and $f^{-1}$ is the exact inverse-image functor for sheaves of modules.

For a sheaf homomorphism $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, the naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ is the sheafified two-term complex $(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\xrightarrow{d}\Omega_{\mathcal P/\mathcal A}\otimes_{\mathcal P}\mathcal B)$ in degrees $-1,0$, where locally $\mathcal P\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ is a polynomial algebra presentation with kernel $\mathcal I$. The canonical comparison identifies this complex with $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ in the derived category.

records.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume all fibres of $f$ are locally Noetherian.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is regular,

with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map $\mathcal{O}_Y(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is regular,
\item there exists an open covering $Y = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$ is regular, and
\item there exists an affine open covering $Y = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring maps $\mathcal{O}_Y(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ are regular.
\end{enumerate}

Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal{F}$ a sheaf of sets on $X_\etale$.

hypotheses: On the **small étale site** $X_{\acute et}$ of a scheme $X$, a *constant sheaf* $\underline E$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value a set $E$ (similarly an abelian group or $\Lambda$-module). A sheaf $\mathcal F$ is *locally constant* if there is an étale cover $\{U_i\to X\}$ on which it becomes isomorphic to a constant sheaf; it is *finite locally constant* for set-valued sheaves if its constant fibre sets are finite, and *finite type locally constant* for $\Lambda$-modules if its local fibre modules are finitely generated. For an étale map $U\to X$, its representable sheaf is $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)$. In an abelian category a *weak Serre subcategory* is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions (without necessarily all subobjects).

records.statement:
The blowup of X in a closed subscheme Z with quasi-coherent ideal I is $\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_X(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$; its exceptional divisor is the scheme inverse image of Z. On an affine chart $A[I/a]$ denotes the degree-zero part of the localization of the Rees algebra at the degree-one element a. For a Cartier divisor D, $\mathcal O(D)$ is the dual of its ideal, with canonical section $1_D$. For the blowup $b:S^\prime\to S$ with center Z and exceptional E and $f:X\to S$, the strict transform of a QC sheaf F is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ modulo sections supported on $\operatorname{pr}_{S^\prime}^{-1}E$; the scheme strict transform is cut out by sections of the structure sheaf supported there. A U-admissible blowup has some finitely presented closed center disjoint from U. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $U \subset X$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme.
Let $b : X' \to X$ be a $U$-admissible blowup.
Let $X'' \to X'$ be a $U$-admissible blowup.
Then the composition $X'' \to X$ is a $U$-admissible blowup.

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.
records.statement:
Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

Let $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a $1$-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids over $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$. If $p$ is
representable by algebraic spaces, then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $p$ is limit preserving on objects, and
\item $p$ is locally of finite presentation (meaning that all algebraic-space base changes have this property).
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: X is a scheme and $\mathcal J$ is an ideal sheaf that is regular, Koszul-regular, H1-regular, or quasi-regular.
records.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Any regular, Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, or quasi-regular sheaf
of ideals on a scheme is a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.

conclusions:
$\Delta : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fppf stacks in groupoids is algebraic if for every scheme $T$ and every object $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$ the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack. This notion is broader than being representable by algebraic spaces.

records.title: Lemma — Generated by local sections stalk

conclusions: Coherent duality and biduality, with bounded-subcategory statements under qc.
hypotheses: X locally Noetherian, K dualizing (affine-locally from ring-theoretic dualizing complexes); X qc for boundedness claims.
records.statement: Here $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ denotes the full derived subcategory of complexes with coherent cohomology, and $D^{\pm},D^b$ denote bounded-below, bounded-above, and bounded derived subcategories. A *dualizing complex* over a Noetherian ring $A$ is a bounded complex with finitely generated cohomology, finite injective dimension, and a homothety quasi-isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a locally Noetherian scheme $X$, a complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is the sheafification of such a ring-theoretic dualizing complex. If $K$ is such a dualizing complex on $X$, then $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and the contravariant functor $\mathbb D_K(E)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(E,K)$ takes $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ to itself and is an anti-equivalence, with the natural biduality map $E\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb D_K\mathbb D_K(E)$ for every $E$ in this coherent-derived category. If $X$ is in addition quasi-compact, $\mathbb D_K$ exchanges $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^{+}$ and $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^{-}$ and restricts to an anti-equivalence of $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b$ with itself.

records.title: Lemma — Genus zero positive degree

hypotheses:

Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a full triangulated subcategory.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category.
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a full triangulated subcategory.
The kernel of the quotient functor
$Q : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}/\mathcal{B}$
is the strictly full subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$ whose objects are
$$
\Ob(\Ker(Q)) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
Z \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})
\text{ such that there exists a }Z' \in \Ob(\mathcal{D}) \\
\text{ such that }Z \oplus Z'\text{ is isomorphic to an object of }\mathcal{B}
\end{matrix}
\right\}
$$
In other words it is the smallest strictly full saturated triangulated
subcategory of $\mathcal{D}$ containing $\mathcal{B}$.

records.title: Lemma — Descending property finite type

conclusions: Deligne-pro-isomorphism characterized by I-adic cohomology pro-systems.
hypotheses: Noetherian open immersion, fixed ideal I cutting out complement, uniformly bounded inverse system K_n.
records.statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Fix a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with $V(\mathcal I)=X\setminus U$. Let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ with a *uniform* cohomological amplitude $[a,b]$, i.e. $H^i(K_n)=0$ for all $n$ when $i\notin[a,b]$. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $(K_n)$ is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for $U\subseteq X$; (2) for every $p\in\mathbf Z$ there is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F_p$ such that the inverse systems of coherent sheaves $(H^p(K_n))_n$ and $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_p)_n$ are isomorphic as pro-objects. This condition is independent of the choice of coherent $\mathcal F_p$ and only finitely many $p$ are nonzero due to $[a,b]$.

records.title: Lemma — Tensor algebra permanence

conclusions: $P'_p(E \oplus F) = P'_p(E) + P'_p(F)$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

For closed immersions $i_j:X_j\hookrightarrow X$ with $X=X_1\cup X_2$ set-theoretically and a perfect $E_2$ on $X_2$ whose Chern classes are defined, assume its restriction to $X_1\cap X_2$ is zero (for the power-sum class $P'_p(E_2)$), or a finite locally free sheaf of rank less than $p$ in degree zero (for the Chern class $c'_p(E_2)$). The canonical localized classes $P'_p(E_2),c'_p(E_2)\in A^p(X_2\to X)$ agree with $P_p(E_2),c_p(E_2)$ on cycles pushed from $X_2$ and vanish on cycles pushed from $X_1$, respectively, compatibly with locally finite type base changes.
records.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$. We say Chern classes of a perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ are defined if an envelope $f:Y\to X$ exists such that $Lf^*E$ is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves on $Y$.

For closed immersions $i_j:X_j\hookrightarrow X$ with $X=X_1\cup X_2$ set-theoretically and a perfect $E_2$ on $X_2$ whose Chern classes are defined, assume its restriction to $X_1\cap X_2$ is zero (for the power-sum class $P'_p(E_2)$), or a finite locally free sheaf of rank less than $p$ in degree zero (for the Chern class $c'_p(E_2)$). The canonical localized classes $P'_p(E_2),c'_p(E_2)\in A^p(X_2\to X)$ agree with $P_p(E_2),c_p(E_2)$ on cycles pushed from $X_2$ and vanish on cycles pushed from $X_1$, respectively, compatibly with locally finite type base changes.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Chern classes of $E$ and $F$ are defined,
\item the restrictions $E|_{X_1 \cap X_2}$ and $F|_{X_1 \cap X_2}$ are zero,
\end{enumerate}
Denote $P'_p(E), P'_p(F), P'_p(E \oplus F) \in A^p(X_2 \to X)$ for $p \geq 0$

$P'_p(E \oplus F) = P'_p(E) + P'_p(F)$.

conclusions: The following four conditions are equivalent: (1) $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is surjective; (2) for every ideal $I\subset R$, $\varphi^{-1}(\sqrt{IS})=\sqrt I$; (3) for every radical ideal $I\subset R$, $\varphi^{-1}(IS)=I$; (4) for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak pS)=\mathfrak p$.

If those equivalent conditions hold, then for every ring map $R\to R^\prime$, the map $R^\prime\to R^\prime\otimes_RS$ has properties (1), (2), and (3) with $R,S$ replaced by $R^\prime,R^\prime\otimes_RS$.
hypotheses: $\varphi:R\to S$ is a homomorphism of commutative rings with identity.
records.statement:
All rings are commutative with identity and all ring maps preserve identity. Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The map $\Spec(S) \to \Spec(R)$ is surjective.
\item For any ideal $I \subset R$
the inverse image of $\sqrt{IS}$ in $R$ is equal to $\sqrt{I}$.
\item For any radical ideal $I \subset R$ the inverse image
of $IS$ in $R$ is equal to $I$.
\item For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ the inverse
image of $\mathfrak p S$ in $R$ is $\mathfrak p$.
\end{enumerate}
In this case the same is true after any base change: Given a ring map
$R \to R'$ the ring map $R' \to R' \otimes_R S$ has the equivalent
properties (1), (2), (3) as well.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

records.title: Lemma — Minimal support in ass

conclusions: For each simplicial object $U$, its face and degeneracy morphisms satisfy the five explicitly enumerated identities.
Conversely, any sequence of objects with face and degeneracy maps satisfying these five identities determines a unique simplicial object.
A simplicial morphism is exactly a degreewise family of arrows commuting with every face and degeneracy map.
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Given a simplicial object $U$ in $\mathcal{C}$
we obtain a sequence of objects $U_n = U([n])$ endowed
with the morphisms $d^n_j = U(\delta^n_j) : U_n \to U_{n-1}$ and
$s^n_j = U(\sigma^n_j) : U_n \to U_{n + 1}$. These morphisms satisfy the following simplicial identities:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $0 \leq i < j \leq n + 1$, then
$d^n_i \circ d^{n + 1}_j = d^n_{j - 1} \circ d^{n + 1}_i$.
\item If $0 \leq i < j \leq n - 1$, then
$d^n_i \circ s^{n - 1}_j = s^{n - 2}_{j - 1} \circ d^{n - 1}_i$.
\item If $0 \leq j \leq n - 1$, then
$\text{id} = d^n_j \circ s^{n - 1}_j = d^n_{j + 1} \circ s^{n - 1}_j$.
\item If $0 < j + 1 < i \leq n$, then
$d^n_i \circ s^{n - 1}_j = s^{n - 2}_j \circ d^{n - 1}_{i - 1}$.
\item If $0 \leq i \leq j \leq n - 1$, then
$s^n_i \circ s^{n - 1}_j = s^n_{j + 1} \circ s^{n - 1}_i$.
\end{enumerate}
\item Conversely, given a sequence of objects $U_n$ and morphisms
$d^n_j$, $s^n_j$ satisfying (1)(a) -- (e) there exists a unique
simplicial object $U$ in $\mathcal{C}$ such that $U_n = U([n])$,
$d^n_j = U(\delta^n_j)$, and $s^n_j = U(\sigma^n_j)$.
\item A morphism between simplicial objects $U$ and $U'$
is given by a family of morphisms $U_n \to U'_n$ commuting
with the morphisms $d^n_j$ and $s^n_j$.
\end{enumerate}

For a Noetherian ring $A$, a *dualizing complex* means a bounded complex with coherent cohomology, finite injective dimension, and the canonical self-Hom identification $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. If $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is local, *normalized* means $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A/\mathfrak m,D)\simeq(A/\mathfrak m)[0]$. For an ideal $I$, write $\widehat A^I=\varprojlim_n A/I^n$ for ordinary $I$-adic completion, and $(A^h,I^h)$ for henselization of the pair. A *strict henselization* is at a chosen separably closed residue-field extension.

The following types of rings have a dualizing complex:
\begin{enumerate}
\item fields,
\item Noetherian complete local rings,
\item $\mathbf{Z}$,
\item Dedekind domains,
\item any ring which is obtained from one of the rings above by
taking an algebra essentially of finite type, or by taking an
ideal-adic completion, or by taking a henselization, 
or by taking a strict henselization.
\end{enumerate}

The closure operations are taken successively where the resulting ring remains in the stated Noetherian category; no normalization choice is implied.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a

be exact functors of triangulated categories. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item the functors $F \circ i$ and $F' \circ i$ are isomorphic
where $i : \mathcal{A} \to D^b(\mathcal{A})$ is the inclusion functor, and
\item for all $X, Y \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$ we have

if $F$ is fully faithful).

records.title: Lemma — Extensions of relative ringed topoi

conclusions: The two differ by tensoring with derived-invertible L.
hypotheses: A Noetherian, two dualizing complexes.
records.statement:
For a Noetherian ring $A$, let $D_{\rm Coh}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full derived category of complexes with finitely generated cohomology in every degree. A *dualizing complex* $\omega_A^\bullet\in D(A)$ means a bounded complex with finite injective dimension and finitely generated cohomology such that the homothety map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\omega_A^\bullet,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. The functor $\mathbb D_A(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,\omega_A^\bullet)$ is contravariant. If $\omega_A^\bullet$ and $(\omega'_A)^\bullet$ are two dualizing complexes, then there is a derived-invertible $L\in D(A)$, locally a shift of a line bundle, and an isomorphism
\[
(\omega'_A)^\bullet\simeq\omega_A^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L.
\]
Thus dualizing complexes are unique up to a derived-invertible twist, not generally an unshifted unique isomorphism.

An *absolutely integrally closed ring* is one in which **every monic polynomial over the ring has a root in the ring**; this does not presume a domain. Such rings have strictly henselian local rings. A *monogenic extension* $A\subseteq B$ is a quotient $B=A[y]/(P(y))$ for a monic polynomial $P$, finite free as an $A$-module. hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. records.title: Lemma — Directed colimit coherent

conclusions: $\omega_X$ is ample.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

Then (1) for every closed subset $T\subseteq Y$ and every $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ supported on $T$, $a_f(Q)$ is supported on $f^{-1}(T)$; and (2) for every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq Y$ and *every unbounded* $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the restriction comparison $\rho_K$ is an isomorphism. records.title: Lemma — Inverse limit is derived limit

conclusions: The inverse system $M_n=H^p(\mathcal C,\mathcal F_n)$ satisfies the Mittag–Leffler condition.
hypotheses: $I$ is an ideal of a ring $A$, and $\mathcal C$ is a site.
$(\mathcal F_n)$ is an inverse system of sheaves of $A$-modules with $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F_{n+1}/I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$.
$p\ge0$, $N_n$ is the intersection of the specified images for all $m\ge n$, and the graded module $\bigoplus_n N_n$ satisfies ACC over $\bigoplus_n I^n/I^{n+1}$.
records.statement:
An inverse system $(M_n)$ satisfies the Mittag–Leffler condition when, for every fixed $n$, the images of the transition maps $M_m\to M_n$ stabilize for all sufficiently large $m$. The graded ring $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ is the associated graded ring of the $I$-adic filtration. For every $n$, set $N_n=\bigcap_{m\ge n}\mathrm{Im}(H^{p+1}(\mathcal C,I^n\mathcal F_{m+1})\to H^{p+1}(\mathcal C,I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}))$. The graded Noetherian/ACC hypothesis is on **$\bigoplus N_n$**, not on the larger direct sum of all degree-$p+1$ cohomology groups; the weaker image condition is essential.

Let $I$ be an ideal of a ring $A$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_1
$$
be an inverse system of $A$-modules on $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\mathcal{F}_n = \mathcal{F}_{n + 1}/I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1}$.
Let $p \geq 0$. Given $n$ define
$$
N_n =
\bigcap\nolimits_{m \geq n}
\Im\left(
H^{p + 1}(\mathcal{C}, I^n\mathcal{F}_{m + 1}) \to
H^{p + 1}(\mathcal{C}, I^n\mathcal{F}_{n + 1})
\right)
$$
If $\bigoplus N_n$ satisfies the ascending chain condition as a graded
$\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n/I^{n + 1}$-module, then the inverse system
$M_n = H^p(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_n)$ satisfies the Mittag-Leffler
condition\footnote{In fact, there exists
a $c \geq 0$ such that $\Im(M_n \to M_{n - c})$ is the stable image
for all $n \geq c$.}.

hypotheses: Fix a base scheme $S$ and the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. A category fibred in groupoids over this site assigns a groupoid of objects over each $S$-scheme, with pullback functors and coherent comparison isomorphisms. A stack in groupoids additionally satisfies effective descent for objects and the sheaf condition for isomorphisms under fppf covers. A representable fibred groupoid is the one associated to an algebraic space. All fibre products of such fibred groupoids are $2$-fibre products (objects include comparison isomorphisms).

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of fibred groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces if, for every scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. A representable morphism has a property such as étale, smooth, flat, locally of finite presentation, or surjective when every such $X_y\to T$ has that property. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times\mathcal X$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$; its diagonal $\Delta_\Delta$ maps $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ and corresponds to the identity automorphism in the inertia groupoid. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective atlas by a scheme.

A morphism $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is limit preserving on objects if, whenever an affine scheme $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ is an inverse limit of affine $S$-schemes, $y_i\in\mathcal Y(U_i)$, $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_U$ are given, then for some $j\ge i$ there exist $x_j\in\mathcal X(U_j)$, an isomorphism $\beta:x_j|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x$, and an isomorphism $\gamma_j:p(x_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{U_j}$ whose pullback to $U$ agrees with $\gamma$ after $p(\beta)$.

conclusions: The upper-shriek functor for a closed immersion equals derived exact-support Hom.
hypotheses: i closed immersion in FTS_S; K bounded-below D_QCoh.
records.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. If $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed immersion in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, then for each $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ there is a functorial isomorphism
\[
i^!(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_X(\mathcal O_X,K),
\]
where $R\mathcal Hom_X(\mathcal O_X,-)$ denotes the *exact-support* derived right adjoint to $Ri_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$; its pushforward is $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(i_*\mathcal O_X,K)$, and on affines $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $B=A/I$ it is the sheafification of $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,-)$ with its natural $B$-module structure.

its structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_S$ is a locally ringed site, see

A *locally ringed site* here means a **ringed site whose stalks at all points are local rings and local morphisms are induced on the stalks** (in the Modules on Sites sense). The stalks are strict henselizations, not ordinary local rings.
hypotheses:

A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **geometric point** $\bar s$ of $S$ is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Its small étale stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar s}$ is the filtered colimit of sections $\mathcal F(U)$ over lifted étale neighbourhoods $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar s$. The structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{S_{\acute etale}}$ assigns $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ to an étale $S$-scheme $U$. For $s\in S$, $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is the **ordinary Zariski local ring**, $\mathcal O_{S,s}^{h}$ its henselization, and $\mathcal O_{S,s}^{sh}$ its strict henselization with chosen residue-field separable closure.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. A local ring is **strictly henselian** if henselian with separably closed residue field. A finite $R$-algebra is a ring $A$ finite as an $R$-module. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.

conclusions: There is a spectral sequence with $E_2^{p,q}=\check H^p(\mathcal U,\underline H^q(\mathcal F))$ converging to $H^{p+q}(U,\mathcal F)$.
The spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal F$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site and $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$ is a covering.

records.statement:
For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ and $q\ge0$, write $\underline H^q(\mathcal F)$ for the abelian presheaf $V\mapsto H^q(V,\mathcal F)$ with natural restriction maps. For a covering $\mathcal U$, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,-)$ is Čech cohomology of this presheaf.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$. For any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ there
is a spectral sequence $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = \check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(U, \mathcal{F})$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$.

is fully faithful (indeed an equivalence of categories).

records.title: Lemma — Special case triangle

conclusions: $\deg(\omega_X|_C) < 0$.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

For a proper Cohen–Macaulay $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, put $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$, $g=\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and for invertible $\mathcal L$ let $\deg(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is Gorenstein, $\omega_X$ is an invertible sheaf of degree $2g-2$. For a zero-dimensional subscheme $Z\subset X$, $\deg(Z)=\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

records.title: Lemma — Monomorphism injective points

conclusions: The elements of $S$ integral over $I$ form an $R$-submodule of $S$.
If $s\in S$ is integral over $R$ and $s^{\prime}\in S$ is integral over $I$, then $ss^{\prime}$ is integral over $I$.
hypotheses: $R\to S$ is a ring map and $I\subset R$ is an ideal.
records.statement:
Let $\varphi : R \to S$ be a ring map.
Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
The set of elements of $S$ which are integral
over $I$ form a $R$-submodule of $S$.
Furthermore, if $s \in S$ is integral over
$R$, and $s'$ is integral over $I$, then
$ss'$ is integral over $I$.
For a ring map $R\to S$ and ideal $I\subset R$, an element $g\in S$ is integral over $I$ if some monic equation $g^d+\sum_{j<d}a_jg^j=0$ holds with $a_j\in I^{d-j}$, mapped to $S$.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. Under base change, the pulled-back section defines the corresponding Gysin map. This Gysin map descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

finitely many irreducible components. Let $\nu : X^\nu \to X$
be the normalization of $X$. Let $x \in X$.

inverse images of $x$ in $X^\nu$.

Branch number is the number of minimal primes of the henselization of the local ring; geometric branch number uses its strict henselization (infinity if not finite). Geometrically unibranch means one geometric branch.

For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. A morphism of algebraic spaces $Y\to X$ is *integral* if it is affine and integral after base change to every scheme over $X$. hypotheses: Let $f:x\to x$ be idempotent in a preadditive category, and put $g=1_x-f$; then $fg=gf=0$.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a preadditive category,
$x$ be an object of $\mathcal{A}$,
and $f : x \to x$ be idempotent.
Write $g = \text{id} _ x - f$
so that $f\circ g=g\circ f=0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ has kernel $i : \Ker (f) \to x$
and $p$ is the unique morphism such that $g = i \circ p$,
then $p \circ i = \text{id} _ {\Ker (f)}$
and $p$ is the cokernel of $f$.
\item If $f$ has cokernel $p : x \to \Coker (f)$
and $i$ is the unique morphism such that $g = i \circ p$,
then $p \circ i = \text{id} _ {\Coker (f)}$
and $i$ is the kernel of $f$.
\item If $g$ has kernel $j : \Ker (g) \to x$
and $q$ is the unique morphism such that $f = j \circ q$,
then $q \circ j = \text{id} _ {\Ker (g)}$
and $q$ is the cokernel of $g$.
\item If $g$ has cokernel $q : x \to \Coker (g)$
and $j$ is the unique morphism such that $f = j \circ q$,
then $q \circ j = \text{id} _ {\Coker (g)}$
and $j$ is the kernel of $g$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Lift factorization monic

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is *decent* when it satisfies $(\gamma)$, equivalently every point $x$ can be represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is *reasonable* when it satisfies $(\delta)$, equivalently the fibres of every affine étale presentation $U\to X$ are universally bounded. It is *very reasonable* when it satisfies $(\epsilon)$, equivalently it has a Zariski-local quasi-compact surjective étale cover by schemes. The implications scheme or quasi-separated $\Rightarrow$ very reasonable $\Rightarrow$ reasonable $\Rightarrow$ decent hold.

For $x\in|X|$ and an étale morphism $U\to X$, write $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ for a pointed étale neighborhood. It is *elementary* when $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is a monomorphism representing $x$. When $X$ is decent, such neighborhoods are cofiltered: they exist, any two have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized after refinement. The residue field $\kappa(x)$ is the field of the unique representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, and the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}$ is the filtered colimit of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over elementary étale neighborhoods; equivalently $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}^{h}$ for any elementary étale neighborhood.

For points $a,b$ of a topological space, $b\leadsto a$ means $a\in\overline{\{b\}}$, i.e., $a$ is a specialization of $b$. The space is $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) when distinct points have distinct closures, and sober when every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point. A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

records.title: Lemma — Proetale subcanonical

conclusions:
A ring map $A \to B$ is \'etale at a prime $\mathfrak q$ if and only if there
exists $g \in B$, $g \not \in \mathfrak q$ such that $B_g$ is standard
\'etale over $A$.
The element g avoids q and **localizes B**, not A; B_g is standard étale as defined. The two local conditions are equivalent for arbitrary ring maps and primes of B.
hypotheses:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A scheme morphism is **étale** if it is flat, locally of finite presentation and unramified, equivalently smooth of relative dimension zero. A map $A\to B$ is **standard étale** if $B\simeq(A[t]/(f))_g$, with $f\in A[t]$ monic, $g\in A[t]$ and $f'(t)$ invertible in $B$. A map $A\to B$ is étale **at** $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ if $A\to B_h$ is étale for some $h\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$. An étale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ has étale maps and jointly surjective images.
records.statement:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A scheme morphism is **étale** if it is flat, locally of finite presentation and unramified, equivalently smooth of relative dimension zero. A map $A\to B$ is **standard étale** if $B\simeq(A[t]/(f))_g$, with $f\in A[t]$ monic, $g\in A[t]$ and $f'(t)$ invertible in $B$. A map $A\to B$ is étale **at** $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ if $A\to B_h$ is étale for some $h\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$. An étale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ has étale maps and jointly surjective images.

A ring map $A \to B$ is \'etale at a prime $\mathfrak q$ if and only if there
exists $g \in B$, $g \not \in \mathfrak q$ such that $B_g$ is standard
\'etale over $A$.

**Precise scope:** The element g avoids q and **localizes B**, not A; B_g is standard étale as defined. The two local conditions are equivalent for arbitrary ring maps and primes of B.

records.title: Lemma — Efface cohomology on closed by finite cover

conclusions: $X$ is catenary.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.

The abelian group $Z_q(T)$ consists of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$. For a closed subscheme $A$ of dimension at most $q$, let $[A]_q$ sum the $q$-dimensional components with multiplicities $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{T,\eta}}\mathcal O_{A,\eta}$. Let $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ be $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite sums of principal Weil divisors on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q+1$.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$ and a nonzero meromorphic section $u$, define $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ as the Weil divisor whose coefficients at codimension-one integral closed subschemes are orders of the local meromorphic function representing $u$ in a trivialization; at a height-one local domain $A$, for $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$, the order of $a/b$ is $\operatorname{length}_A(A/aA)-\operatorname{length}_A(A/bA)$. The class of this divisor in $\mathrm{CH}_{\dim_\delta(W)-1}(W)$ is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. For a global section $u$, $Z(u)$ is its scheme-theoretic zero locus.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$, the operator $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ sends an integral $[W]$ of $\delta$-dimension $q$ to $(W\hookrightarrow T)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ and extends linearly.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the pushforward of an integral $[W]\in Z_q(T')$ is $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if $\dim_\delta h(W)=q$, and $0$ if that dimension is smaller. This extends linearly and induces a map on Chow groups.

records.title: Lemma — Subsheaf of constant sheaf

conclusions: The global Gysin maps commute with the de Rham differential.
hypotheses: $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a finitely presented closed immersion with locally free conormal of rank $c$, and $\gamma^p$ is its canonical Gysin map.
records.statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.

For all $p\geq0$, the canonical global Gysin maps $\gamma^p$ commute with exterior differentiation: the square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\Omega^p_{Z/S}&\xrightarrow{\gamma^p}&\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})\\
\downarrow d&&\downarrow d\\
\Omega^{p+1}_{Z/S}&\xrightarrow{\gamma^{p+1}}&\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c+1}_{X/S})\end{array}$$
commutes.

records.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $n \geq m$. Let $A$ be an
$n \times m$ matrix with coefficients in $R$. Let $J \subset R$
be the ideal generated by the $m \times m$ minors of $A$.

\end{enumerate}

conclusions: Its spectral sequence is bounded; each cohomology filtration is finite; it converges to $H^*(K)$.
hypotheses: Let $(K^\bullet,F)$ be a filtered cochain complex in an abelian category.
For each $n$, $H^n(F^pK)$ vanishes for sufficiently large $p$ and $H^n(F^pK)\to H^n(K)$ is an isomorphism for sufficiently small $p$.
records.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category. Let $(K^\bullet, F)$ be a
filtered complex of $\mathcal{A}$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every $n$ there exist $p_0(n)$ such that
$H^n(F^pK^\bullet) = 0$ for $p \geq p_0(n)$,
\item for every $n$ there exist $p_1(n)$ such that
$H^n(F^pK^\bullet) \to H^n(K^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism
for $p \leq p_1(n)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the spectral sequence associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$ is bounded,
\item the filtration on each $H^n(K^\bullet)$ is finite,
\item the spectral sequence associated to $(K^\bullet, F)$ converges
to $H^*(K^\bullet)$.
\end{enumerate}

records.title: Lemma — Cohomology with support quasi coherent

conclusions: The projection formula for the right adjoint holds on all unbounded quasi-coherent-derived inputs.
hypotheses: f perfect proper Noetherian, a_f right adjoint.
records.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *perfect proper* morphism of Noetherian schemes (proper and of finite Tor-dimension, with the usual pseudo-coherence/finiteness built into perfectness) and let $a_f$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. For a qcqs morphism $f:X\to Y$ with right adjoint $a_f$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to a_f(K)$ be the canonical comparison obtained by adjunction from the projection formula $Rf_*(Lf^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y))\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by the counit $Rf_*a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_Y$. For every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, including unbounded $K$, the canonical projection-comparison morphism
\[
Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}a_f(\mathcal O_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_f(K)
\]
is an isomorphism. This requires perfect properness, but not flatness.

hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring and $M$ a finite-length $R$-module of length $\ell$. Let $\gamma_\varphi:\det K_\varphi\otimes\det I_\varphi\to\det M$, $\gamma_\psi:\det K_\psi\otimes\det I_\psi\to\det M$ be the determinant isomorphisms and $\sigma$ swap the tensor factors. records.title: Lemma — Periodic determinant sign

conclusions: $\delta_X$ is a dimension function on $|X|$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

At a point $x$ of a decent algebraic space, the number of branches is the number of minimal primes of the henselian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$, possibly infinite. The space is *unibranch at $x$* if $\mathcal O_{X,x}^h$ has precisely one minimal prime. A topological space is *catenary* if all saturated chains of specializations between fixed comparable points have the same length. A dimension function $\delta$ on a sober catenary topological space satisfies $\delta(x)=\delta(y)+1$ whenever $x\leadsto y$ is an immediate specialization. For a locally finite type map $f:X\to S$ with $S$ universally catenary carrying dimension function $\delta_S$, its induced function is $\delta_X(x)=\delta_S(f(x))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}\kappa(x)$.
